contract.settlement_definition: Binary ladder on one player's official rebounds in the named game: YES if rebounds are at or above N (floor_strike N-0.5, strike_type greater, titles like '10+ rebounds'). Inactive or never-entering players settle at a fair price; once he enters the market settles on actual rebounds. A postponed game that begins within 48 hours stays open, otherwise all markets resolve at a fair price. The protected variant (KXNBAREBPROT) additionally refunds, at the pre-tip fair price, a player who enters in the first half but not after halftime (including overtime), unless he already has the required rebounds. Both live series (KXNBAREB, KXNBAREBPROT) have sampled rules; neither says whether overtime rebounds count.

rules_evidence.quote: Once a player enters the game the market settles based on the player's rebounds recorded.
rules_evidence.establishes: Standard rebound ladder settles on actual rebounds once the player enters; no early-exit protection.

rules_evidence.quote: this Contract resolves to the fair price prior to the opening tip of the game unless the player records the required number of rebounds
rules_evidence.establishes: Protected variant: first-half-only participation is refunded at the pre-tip fair price unless the threshold was already met.

rules_evidence.quote: If the player enters the game after the conclusion of the first half, this Contract settles based on actual statistics, regardless of first-half participation.
rules_evidence.establishes: Protection switches off once the player appears after halftime, so the voided branch is exactly first-half-only appearances.

variants_and_edge_cases: Protected (KXNBAREBPROT) vs standard (KXNBAREB) on the same player and strike have different payoffs for the same early-exit event; a model must carry both forms.
Sampled strikes include 10+ for a wing (Mario Hezonja, floor_strike 9.5) which is a far-tail rung; ladder rungs span the tail and low-probability rungs are dominated by pool variance not talent.
Overtime is not addressed in the sampled standard text; official box score rebounds normally include OT, adding five minutes of pool in about 6% of games.

Protected refund value: KXNBAREBPROT refunds at 'the fair price prior to the opening tip', a price that already embeds the pre-tip chance of a first-half-only appearance, so the protected contract's fair value is not simply the standard rung conditional on playing the second half.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official box-score rebounds as named in the full rules (the sampled secondary text is cut before listing source agencies, so the exact source and correction policy are unverified).

mechanism.summary: Rebounds are minutes times the rate at which missed shots (both teams') land within reach times the share of those the player secures. The chain is: participation and minutes (bigs are foul- and blowout-sensitive), the supply of creditable misses given pace, both teams' shot quality and the free-throw and team-rebound leakage, how that supply splits between offensive and defensive boards given each coach's crash policy, the player's share given which other rebounders are on the floor and where he stands (rim vs perimeter), conversion of chances to rebounds (contested vs uncontested, deferrals), and the distributional consequences: counts are overdispersed because the supply itself varies with shooting luck of both teams, and the shared supply makes teammates' rebound counts negatively dependent. The existing catalog captures supply and share conceptually but not the credit leakage, the lineup-pairing arithmetic or the protected-contract state.

stages.name: Appearance, minutes and foul exposure
stages.description: A big either plays a standard 28-36 minutes or loses time to foul trouble, a blowout, or an injury. Rebounds are strongly minutes-dependent, and bigs pick up early fouls that trigger first-half benching, so the minutes distribution has a heavy left tail. For protected contracts the first-half-only branch has a distinct payoff.
stages.distribution: Minutes mixture with a left-tail mass from fouls and blowouts; foul accumulation is a count process with a coach-specific benching threshold (two early, three in first half).

stages.name: Supply of creditable misses
stages.description: The number of missed shots is the sum of two teams' misses, a function of pace and each side's shot quality; part of the supply is lost to team rebounds, out-of-bounds recoveries and dead free-throw attempts. High-scoring, high-FG% games shrink the pool, while games with bad shooting enlarge it, which makes rebounds negatively correlated with total points.
stages.distribution: Supply approximately normal with sd of about 5-6 misses but with a negative dependence on shooting luck; leakage varies with foul volume.

stages.name: Offensive and defensive split by team strategy
stages.description: Offensive rebounds depend on how many players crash and how the opponent defends the glass; defensive boards depend on the opponent's attack style and whether players leak out in transition. A big on a crashing team has a higher offensive component with more variance. Opponent scheme (drop vs switching) positions centers near or far from the rim.
stages.distribution: OREB count is a thinned process with team-specific rate; DREB dominates the mean but OREB adds right-tail variance.

stages.name: Share among on-court rebounders
stages.description: Given a creditable miss, who secures it depends on position, box-out assignment and the other bigs on the floor. The share is lineup-specific: a center's TRB% is far higher beside four perimeter players than beside another big. Teammate absences reallocate shares to specific survivors, and bench bigs inherit starters' shares only partly.
stages.distribution: Shares are bounded, sum to one across the five on court (negative dependence among teammates); share estimates carry sampling error that depends on possessions together.

stages.name: Count distribution and settlement
stages.description: Conditional on supply and share, the count is overdispersed relative to Poisson and discrete at the strike; rungs near the mean are very sensitive to dispersion. Scorer credit for team rebounds and rare video-review corrections matter only at exact-threshold counts. Settlement uses the official box score with a fair-price refund only for inactive players (or first-half-only in the protected series).
stages.distribution: Negative-binomial-like with dispersion driven by pool variance and minutes mixture; integer counts; rung probabilities concentrated in a 7-12 range.

talent_strength.note: Individual rebounding ability expressed as chances and share per on-court possession, adjusted for pairings.

opponent_matchup.note: Opponent scheme and glass strategy shift where rebounds fall; positional allowance is weak.

role_personnel.note: Zero-sum share among bigs on the floor; the key variable set.

availability_news.note: Own and opposing frontcourt status and the first-half-only hazard needed for the protected variant.

coaching_scheme.note: Crash policy, coverage and rotation choices of both coaches.

environment.note: Venue and altitude influence rebounds only through shooting percentages and fatigue, both of which are small and already reflected in the pool and minutes inputs; no standalone environment variable is warranted for this contract.

game_context_script.note: Blowout minutes loss and late-game foul sequences.

pace_volume.note: Supply of misses and the creditable fraction of it.

efficiency_conversion.note: Conversion of chances to rebounds (contested vs uncontested) and the shooting-percentage side of the pool.

distribution_variance.note: Overdispersion from pool variance and minutes mixture; dependence among teammates through the shared pool.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Back-to-back, minutes ramp-up after injury and clinch-rest decisions change bigs' minutes but are not represented by any input in this archetype's list; rest enters implicitly through projected minutes only.

officiating_rules.note: Scorer credit of team rebounds and the foul-call environment that drives bigs' benching.

settlement_contract.note: Standard vs protected refund logic and the official rebounds count.

nba.creditable_rebound_pool.label: Player-creditable rebound pool: misses net of team rebounds and dead-ball leakage
nba.creditable_rebound_pool.mechanism: Official player rebounds exclude team rebounds (shot-clock violations, balls out of bounds, first free-throw misses of a pair), so the pool a player can be credited from is smaller than total misses and varies by game flow.
nba.creditable_rebound_pool.rationale: A pool built from field-goal misses alone overstates supply when games have many foul-heavy trips, where missed first free throws and dead-ball team rebounds produce no player rebound; the leakage share is hypothesised to be of the order of 6-10% of misses (unverified, to be estimated from team rebound counts; see pr-leakage-source) and should vary with foul rate.
nba.creditable_rebound_pool.measurement: For each team-game: creditable_pool = FG misses + live FT misses (last free throw of a trip) - (team rebounds + out-of-bounds recoveries); estimate team-level leakage ratio by regressing team rebounds on FG misses, FT trips and out-of-bounds counts over 2 seasons with 80-game half-life; project tonight's pool as projected combined misses (ratings and shot-quality based, not market totals) times (1 - projected leakage). Leakage uses opponent foul rate and arena (scorer) effect.
free_sources: nba_api team box scores (reb, oreb, dreb, team reb)
raw_data: Team box scores incl. team rebound counts
Projected team misses from own model
nba.creditable_rebound_pool.why: Fixes the denominator of the rebound process; bigs in foul-heavy games see a smaller player-creditable pool even when total misses are high.

nba.pairing_adjusted_reb_share.label: Rebound percentage conditional on specific frontcourt pairings (ridge on/off)
nba.pairing_adjusted_reb_share.mechanism: A big's share of available boards depends on which other rebounders share the floor in each stint; the same player has very different shares beside a stretch four vs a second center.
nba.pairing_adjusted_reb_share.rationale: Season TRB% averages over pairings; because rotation patterns change with injury news, what matters is the expected minute-weighted mix of tonight's pairings, which is predictable pregame once availability is known.
nba.pairing_adjusted_reb_share.measurement: From stint data, regress player TRB% on indicator vectors of teammates on court (ridge, lambda chosen by rolling-origin CV on previous season, minimum 150 possessions per pair) with opponent offensive-rebounding strength as a covariate; project tonight's stint mix = rotation minutes by lineup weighted by injury-conditioned availability; output expected share and its standard error. DREB% and OREB% estimated separately because OREB is lineup-sensitive.
raw_data: Lineup stints: possessions, player oreb/dreb, opponent misses while on court
nba.pairing_adjusted_reb_share.why: Turns the unquantified frontcourt competition label into a number and links it to injury-conditioned rotation changes.

nba.team_glass_strategy.label: Offensive-glass crash rate versus transition-defense tradeoff of each team and coach
nba.team_glass_strategy.mechanism: Coaches choose how many players crash the offensive boards; heavy crashing raises OREB for bigs and lowers the opponent's DREB share while increasing transition possessions for opponents.
nba.team_glass_strategy.rationale: Crash policy is a team trait that is persistent across seasons within a coach, and it changes both rebound counts and pace; it is not recoverable from rebound pool or pace alone.
nba.team_glass_strategy.measurement: Per team-season (70-game half-life, reset at a coaching change): offensive crash rate = OREB% and opponent transition points per possession after the team's own missed shots (possession-start types from play-by-play: defensive rebound, steal, live-ball turnover). Opponent weakness term = opponent's DREB% minus the DREB% expected from team size (average rebounder height and team minutes by position) and its transition-defense points allowed per 100. Matchup net value = own crash rate x opponent weakness minus (own transition-defense cost per crash). Report team OREB%, DREB% and net value; per-player attribution is by minutes-weighted position share. As-of: games before tip.
raw_data: possession start type, oreb counts, transition scoring
nba.team_glass_strategy.why: Adjusts the side-specific mix (OREB vs DREB) which the pooled rebound total hides; relevant for forwards who crash.

nba.big_exit_protection_state.label: Big-man early-exit and first-half-only participation hazard, mapped to protected-contract voiding
nba.big_exit_protection_state.mechanism: Protected rebound contracts refund any player who enters in the first half but does not enter after halftime (including overtime), whatever the cause: injury or foul-out, ejection, or a coach resting him for the whole second half of a lopsided game.
nba.big_exit_protection_state.rationale: In standard contracts an early exit settles NO; in protected series the same event refunds at a pre-tip fair price, so the same underlying hazard has opposite market consequences and must be tracked separately for the two forms. Blowout-driven second-half rest is the cause most likely to be missed: a bench big who played 6 first-half minutes in a game that is 25 points at halftime is refunded, so the refund branch also depends on the margin path.
nba.big_exit_protection_state.measurement: Per player-season, estimate P(minutes in 2H+OT = 0 | entered 1H) and P(exit before 12 total minutes) from play-by-play with beta(2,40) shrinkage and a status multiplier; output separately, by cause (injury or ejection, foul-out, blowout rest of the whole second half): hazard of 'plays only first half' (protected refund branch) and 'exits early without refund'. The blowout-rest cause is estimated as P(no second-half minutes | entered 1H, halftime margin bin) and is driven by nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve (rare for starters, common for deep-bench bigs). As-of: injury report vintage.
nba.big_exit_protection_state.why: Needed to price KXNBAREBPROT correctly versus KXNBAREB for the same player and strike. Cause split includes whole-second-half blowout rest, which interacts with the ratings-based blowout curve.

nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.label: Ratings-based blowout probability and starter-minutes-vs-margin curve (market-free)
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.mechanism: Rebuilds the blowout risk from team strength and rotation history instead of the closing spread: a ratings-implied expected margin and margin spread give P(large lead), and a coach/player minutes-versus-margin curve converts each margin path into expected minutes lost by starters and gained by bench players.
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.rationale: The catalog input nba.garbage is defined from the closing spread, which is a market price and so a benchmark, not an input. The causal quantity is the chance that the margin passes the coach's pull threshold early enough to matter, and how much playing time each player then loses. Subtle: the loss depends on when the lead arrives (a 20-point lead entering Q4 removes far more starter minutes than one reached with 3 minutes left), on the coach, and on whether the trailing team also pulls starters, so the curve must be conditional on the margin path and not only on the final margin.
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.measurement: Step 1, expected margin: mu = (NetRtg_home_adj - NetRtg_away_adj) * expected_possessions/100 + home_adv, where NetRtg_adj is the as-of-tipoff opponent-adjusted net rating from nba.off_rtg and nba.def_rtg (ridge regression on game point differential, half-life about 25 games, shrunk to the preseason prior with n_prior about 20 games as a placeholder to be fitted), adjusted for the confirmed unavailable players via nba.lineup_adj_rating, home_adv fitted on the last 5 seasons (about 2 points). Step 2, margin spread: sd_margin fitted on 5 seasons of residuals of final margin versus mu (league-wide roughly 12-13 points, to be estimated, with a heavier empirical tail than normal). Step 3: P(final |margin| >= 15/20/25) and P(|lead| >= 15/20 entering Q4) from the empirical residual distribution around mu. Step 4, minutes curve: from play-by-play stints, per team-season, expected minutes of each rotation player conditional on margin entering Q4 in bins (0-9, 10-14, 15-19, 20+), shrunk toward the league curve with k about 30 blowout games. Output per player: expected minutes lost and the probability of falling below a stated minutes level. No closing line or other price is used; the spread is retained only to benchmark calibration of step 3.

nba.minutes.reason: Rebound chances accrue per minute on court and bigs are the players most exposed to foul-driven benching; delivered as a mixture it also gives the fat left tail the existing text only mentions.

nba.reb_chances.reason: Chances (a rebound within reach) are far more stable than rebounds because conversion is largely deferred or contested; this is the correct first-stage variable but depends on tracking data that is only partly public.

nba.rebound_pool.reason: The supply of missed shots is the denominator of every rebound; as defined (expected misses by type) it omits the team-rebound leakage and free-throw-miss composition that determine how much of the supply a player can actually be credited with.

nba.frontcourt_competition.reason: Boards are zero-sum among the bigs on the floor, which makes this the key pairing variable; but only a label exists, no calculation, so it needs the pairing-adjusted board share defined below.

nba.teammate_absence_shift.reason: A missing big raises the survivor's share, but with/without samples for specific frontcourt pairs are small; shrink to role prior and combine with the pairing-adjusted share.

nba.shot_profile.reason: The opponent's three-point and rim attempt mix changes rebound distance and who gets the ball; useful but already partly present in the pool-by-type; second-order for centers.

nba.opp_def_pos.reason: Rebounds allowed to a position are dominated by pace, opponent miss volume and who was on the floor; as a positional average it largely repeats the pool and pairing inputs.

nba.pace.reason: Possessions scale misses, but the relevant quantity is the combined misses of both teams, already in the rebound pool; keep only for the lineup-aware component.

nba.def_scheme.reason: Drop coverage anchors the center near the rim (more boards), switching pulls him out and pushes rebounds to wings; effect real for the center, undetectable for guards.

nba.foul_rates.reason: Foul-trouble benching truncates a big's minutes and is a major left-tail driver; the per-minute foul rate needs combining with referee crew and opponent drive rate.

nba.garbage.reason: Catalog definition is "blowout probability from spread", a closing-line quantity, so it is a market benchmark and not an input. Removed from stages, coverage, interactions and data feeds; replaced by the market-free nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve built from ratings and rotation history. Prior note: Blowouts take starters off the floor; the rebound ladder is hit hard because bench bigs are not simple replacements. Must be rebuilt from ratings, not the spread.

nba.injuries_pit.reason: Frontcourt availability of both teams (own co-big, opposing rebounders and rim protectors) sets shares; timing vintage matters.

nba.scorer_bias.reason: Arena-level credit differences are mainly for assists, steals and blocks; rebound credit is mostly objective except team-rebound assignment, so the effect is small compared with the Poisson noise at a 10+ threshold.

nba.stat_dist.reason: Overdispersion of rebounds is driven by the shared pool variance and minutes mixture; distribution must be conditional on both.

m.quote_history.reason: A price series does not generate rebounds; use only to date information arrival.

m.rules_text.reason: Contains the standard fair-price void and the distinct protected variant that voids players who only play the first half; the settled quantity differs by series.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook rebound lines are benchmark priors; an input copy of them removes the model's independent signal.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Diagnostic of quote quality across rungs; a rebound model's own ladder is monotone by construction.

m.strike_hit_rates.reason: Label history for calibrating rung probabilities; no causal content.

nba.market_calibration_bias.reason: Kalshi price-bucket bias is an overlay on model output, not an input to rebounding.

m.volume_oi.reason: Open interest has no link to the rebound process and reflects the player's popularity.

m.trade_tape.reason: Order flow is microstructure; belongs in an execution overlay.

m.settlement_truth.reason: Labels for calibration; reconcile with the official box score rebounds.

nba.stat_corrections.reason: Rebound credit occasionally changes after video review; matters only at exact-threshold counts.

nba.tracking.reason: Box-out and contested/uncontested splits are the best refinement of conversion, but public availability at game level is limited and this is a label for several distinct tracking fields.

nba.player_role_position.reason: Rim-runner versus perimeter big determines where he stands on missed shots; the five-position label is too crude and should be replaced by defensive-rebound-location data.

nba.late_game_script.reason: Intentional-foul sequences add free throws but their effect on rebound counts is small (misses on intentional trips are mostly team-controlled); retained only as context.

interactions.mechanism: Expected rebounds equal minutes share times the pool times conversion share, so a fast game of poor shooting multiplies the benefit of a full minutes load; in a blowout the pool is large but the starter is on the bench, leaving the product small.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress rebounds on log pool, log minutes and their product; check that the elasticity of minutes rises with pool size.

interactions.mechanism: The share a big inherits when another big is absent depends on which player replaces the minutes: a stretch forward replacing a rim-runner gives the survivor extra share, a second center gives little; so the absence effect is conditional on the replacement type, not additive.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate absence effect separately by replacement archetype (big vs wing) with stint data and test equality of effects.

interactions.mechanism: A team that crashes the offensive glass concedes transition chances and plays slower after its own misses; opponent transition frequency changes pace and the miss supply in subsequent possessions, so crash policy has a nonlinear effect on the pool via pace.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare possession counts per 48 for high-crash vs low-crash teams, controlling for opponent, and relate to OREB totals.

interactions.mechanism: A big with a high foul rate in a lopsided game is likelier to be benched early in the first half and then not return, producing joint extreme left-tail minutes; the two sources of truncation are not independent because coaches avoid risking a foul-prone starter once the margin is large.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute P(minutes<20) by foul-rate tercile within blowout-probability terciles; test for a non-additive cell.

interactions.mechanism: A designated or returning big carries a first-half-only appearance hazard; protected contracts refund this branch while standard contracts settle NO, so identical status information has opposite value in the two series.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realised first-half-only appearances by status vintage and test the resulting price gap between KXNBAREBPROT and KXNBAREB for the same strike.

interactions.mechanism: For protected rebound contracts a halftime margin beyond about 20 points makes a no-second-half appearance likely for bench bigs but not for starters, so the refund branch probability and the value of the protection depend on the margin path and the player's rotation slot, in opposite directions for the two groups.
interactions.how_to_test: From play-by-play compute P(no second-half minutes | entered first half) by halftime margin bin and by starter or bench status, and compare with the injury-only hazard.

nonlinearities.shape: concave: conversion share saturates as chances rise
nonlinearities.why: Chances above a player's available share increase contested boards, where conversion falls; the marginal rebound per added chance declines, so the mean response flattens for the top rebounders.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold: benching onset at 2 first-half fouls and 4-5 total
nonlinearities.why: Coaches bench bigs on a foul count, so the minutes loss from fouls is a step function of foul count rather than linear in the per-minute foul rate.

nonlinearities.shape: convex in dispersion: rung probability for 10+ rises faster than the mean when the pool variance is high
nonlinearities.why: Because the 10+ threshold sits in the upper tail for most players, doubling pool variance raises tail probability more than a proportional mean shift would.

contract.settlement_definition: Binary ladder: YES if the named player makes at least N three-pointers (floor_strike N-0.5, e.g. 5+ with floor 4.5) in the named game. Per the KXNBA3PT text, inactive or never-entering players settle at a fair price; once he enters, the market settles on actual made threes; postponed games that start within 48 hours stay open, otherwise all markets resolve at a fair price (the KXNBA3PTPROT sample is cut off after its protection clause, so these clauses are assumed, not read, for it). KXNBA3PT and KXNBA3PTPROT have sampled rules; the protected variant resolves at the pre-tip fair price when a player enters in the first half but not after it (including overtime) unless he already has the required threes. KXNBALADDER3PT is TITLE_ONLY. Neither sampled text says whether overtime makes count for the standard ladder.

rules_evidence.quote: Once a player enters the game the market settles based on the player's made three-pointers recorded.
rules_evidence.establishes: Standard threes ladder settles on actual made threes once the player enters; no early-exit protection.

rules_evidence.quote: If a player is inactive, or active but never takes the court, the market settles to a fair price.
rules_evidence.establishes: Void branch: only inactive or never-entering players settle at a fair price; a player who enters and leaves early settles on actual made threes.

rules_evidence.quote: this Contract resolves to the fair price prior to the opening tip of the game unless the player records the required number of threes
rules_evidence.establishes: Protected threes refund a first-half-only appearance at the pre-tip fair price unless the strike is already met, so the early-exit branch largely disappears from the protected rung.

variants_and_edge_cases: Ladder rungs: only 5+ rungs (KXNBA3PT and KXNBA3PTPROT, floor_strike 4.5) are sampled; a 1+ to 7+ span is assumed from the ladder titles and is not verified from rules text. Low rungs would depend mostly on attempts>=1 and minutes, high rungs on the attempt tail and shooting luck, so key drivers would differ by rung.
Protected (KXNBA3PTPROT, rules-verified): a first-half-only appearance is refunded at the pre-tip fair price unless the strike is met; any appearance after halftime puts it back on actual makes.
Overtime is not addressed in the sampled text; official box score made threes normally include OT, adding about five minutes of attempts in about 6% of games.
Ladder series (KXNBALADDER3PT, TITLE_ONLY): assumed to be the same nested 'N+' rungs as KXNBA3PT, so cross-rung monotonicity must hold, but its void rule is not read.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official box score made three-pointers as named in the full rules; the sampled secondary text is truncated before naming source agencies, so the exact source is unverified.

mechanism.summary: Made threes equal attempts times make probability. Attempts are minutes times a per-minute rate set by role (catch-and-shoot spot-up vs on-ball creator), the team's pace and who passes to him, modified by the score path (trailing teams launch more, leading teams bench shooters). Make probability is a context-weighted talent estimate (open catch-and-shoot vs contested pull-up) that is overwhelmingly noise in a single game, so the predictable component is attempts, and the make count is a thinned process whose variance exceeds a plain binomial because attempts and team-level shooting form are random. Settlement is the official count on single-game ladders and protected rungs. The main modelling hazards are role-specific minutes volatility for bench shooters and the dependence between a shooter's attempts and a specific passer's availability.

stages.name: Participation and minutes for a role player
stages.description: Spot-up shooters are often rotation players whose minutes change sharply with matchup, injury news and blowouts, so the minutes distribution is wide and sometimes zero-inflated for players on the edge of the rotation. Once he enters, the contract settles on his count, so brief appearances produce zero or one make.
stages.distribution: Wide mixture, zero- or low-inflated for fringe rotation players; bench minutes weakly dependent on game margin.

stages.name: Attempt rate given role and teammates
stages.description: Three-point attempts per minute reflect the shooter's role: off-ball spot-up players take 7-10 per 36 minutes mostly from passes, on-ball creators take pull-ups. The rate depends on who passes to him (passer availability) and who competes for the same looks, and on the team's pace and style. Attempt counts are overdispersed relative to Poisson because role and game flow change within games.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed count with variance exceeding mean (dispersion index about 1.3-1.8); mean attempt rate shifts by specific teammate absences.

stages.name: Defensive scheme and shot openness
stages.description: The opponent's scheme sets how many attempts are open or contested: drop coverage concedes above-the-break openings, switching and aggressive closeouts reduce them, and blitzing creates kick-out threes for the shooters. Openness affects both attempt volume and per-shot make probability, and it is a scheme trait rather than a luck outcome.
stages.distribution: Categorical scheme effect on both the attempt rate and per-shot make probability; effects of a few percentage points on make probability, 10-20% on attempts.

stages.name: Make probability: talent versus luck
stages.description: Given attempt context, each shot is a Bernoulli trial with probability depending on shot type and openness; single-game make rates are overwhelmingly luck and require heavy shrinkage (hundreds of attempts of prior). Team-level shooting form creates positive correlation across a team's shooters within a game, while player-level hot hands are statistically elusive.
stages.distribution: Sum of heterogeneous Bernoulli trials; per-game variance close to binomial with p near 0.36 plus a team-level shared shock; shrinkage weight depends on attempts.

stages.name: Game script effects on attempts
stages.description: Trailing teams take more threes late in the game and bench shooters gain minutes in blowouts, while starters who sit lose attempts; close games push closers to higher minutes. The net effect on a given shooter depends on role and on the margin path, which makes simple blowout penalties wrong for bench specialists.
stages.distribution: Path-dependent: attempt rate per minute is a function of margin bin and quarter; mixture over projected margin paths.

stages.name: Settlement form
stages.description: The ladder and protected forms are thresholds on one game's count, nested across rungs so the curve must be monotone; the protected form (KXNBA3PTPROT text) removes the first-half-only branch unless the strike is already met, so its value differs from the standard rung exactly in the early-exit scenarios, whose weight is nba.early_exit_hazard (injury exits plus a coach-rested second half). Low rungs depend mostly on the probability of at least one attempt and minutes, high rungs on the attempt tail and shooting luck.
stages.distribution: Integer count per game (mixture of binomials over attempts); protected rungs replace the first-half-exit mass by the pre-tip price.

talent_strength.note: Shooting skill by context with heavy shrinkage; team strength is secondary.

opponent_matchup.note: Scheme and openness allowed matter more than opponent 3P% allowed.

role_personnel.note: Role, passers and competing shooters determine attempts.

availability_news.note: Own status and passer/creator status by vintage, plus the first-half-only participation hazard that the protected series refunds.

coaching_scheme.note: Offensive spacing and rotation decisions plus opponent coverage choice.

environment.note: Arena and altitude effects on three-point percentage are small and unreliable once shooter talent is shrunk; the mechanism for a single game is dominated by attempts and noise, so no separate environment variable is justified.

game_context_script.note: Margin-path dependence of attempts by role.

efficiency_conversion.note: Context-specific make probability and luck regression.

distribution_variance.note: Mixture over attempts with team-level shooting shocks.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest-day effects on shooting legs and minutes, and rest-for-seeding decisions for rotation players, have no input in this archetype; second-night-of-back-to-back shooting effect on makes is unmeasured here.

officiating_rules.note: Officials influence threes only through foul calls on shooters (rare) and no official scorer discretion is involved in a made-three count; the contract needs no officiating variable beyond settlement text.

settlement_contract.note: Ladder and protected forms are rules-verified (KXNBA3PT, KXNBA3PTPROT); the ladder series KXNBALADDER3PT is TITLE_ONLY.

nba.three_make_by_openness_prior.label: Hierarchical make probability by shot type (catch-and-shoot vs pull-up) and defender openness
nba.three_make_by_openness_prior.mechanism: Make probability depends on shot context more than on a single season 3P%, so talent should be estimated per context and recombined with tonight's expected context mix.
nba.three_make_by_openness_prior.rationale: Overall 3P% averages over open catch-and-shoot threes (about 38%) and tightly contested pull-ups (about 31%); a shooter's attempt mix changes with teammates and opposing closeouts, so the make probability changes even with fixed talent.
nba.three_make_by_openness_prior.measurement: Base model (public per-shot data): beta-binomial hierarchy on made/attempted by shot zone (corner, above the break) x pull-up flag from shotchartdetail ACTION_TYPE and SHOT_ZONE fields over 3 seasons, league-cell mean as prior with prior weight 250 attempts per cell, partial pooling by player, recent-season weight 0.5 per year. Optional refinement if the tracking dashboards are confirmed (p3-defender-distance): aggregate catch-and-shoot versus pull-up and closest-defender bins (wide open 6+ ft, open 4-6, tight under 4) as separate multiplicative adjustments, not a crossed cell, because the dashboards are not per-shot. Combine with tonight's predicted context mix from shot-creation role and opponent openness allowed. Output a single p3 with credible interval. As-of: shots finished before tip.
free_sources: nba_api shotchartdetail (location, zone, action type; no per-shot defender distance to this resolver's knowledge)
nba_api tracking shot dashboards with closest-defender and catch-and-shoot splits (aggregate, SOURCE_UNVERIFIED)

aggregate tracking shot splits by closest-defender bin
nba.three_make_by_openness_prior.why: Separates context-driven make probability from luck; the existing regression input shrinks a pooled 3P% instead. Rebased on public per-shot fields so it does not depend on per-shot defender distance; role is secondary until the tracking splits are confirmed.

nba.three_att_script_elasticity.label: Elasticity of a shooter's three-point attempt rate to score margin and quarter
nba.three_att_script_elasticity.mechanism: Trailing teams take more threes late and leading teams run clock and bench shooters, so 3PA per minute is a function of the margin path, not a constant.
nba.three_att_script_elasticity.rationale: Blowout dynamics cut starters but raise bench shooters' attempts; a close fourth quarter raises volume for closers; the sign differs between roles, so a single 'blowout' penalty misprices spot-up wings and bench shooters.
nba.three_att_script_elasticity.measurement: From play-by-play estimate per player 3PA per minute in margin bins (<-12, -12..-5, -5..+5, +5..+12, >+12) by quarter, with empirical-Bayes shrinkage to role-archetype bins (prior weight 120 minutes per bin); combine with the projected distribution of margin paths from team ratings (not the spread). Output expected 3PA integrating over the margin-path distribution and minutes mixture.
raw_data: play-by-play shot events with score margin and quarter
nba.three_att_script_elasticity.why: Captures role-specific blowout asymmetries that make bench shooters better, not worse, in lopsided games.

nba.assisted_three_passer_map.label: Share of shooter's made threes assisted by each teammate (passer dependence)
nba.assisted_three_passer_map.mechanism: A catch-and-shoot three requires a passer; the loss of a particular creator removes a specific fraction of assisted looks, with replacement playmakers delivering fewer.
nba.assisted_three_passer_map.rationale: Absence adjustments built from with/without splits ignore that dependence is concentrated in a few passers; in many pairs one creator generates 30-40% of a shooter's threes, so his absence matters far more than other absences.
nba.assisted_three_passer_map.measurement: For shooter s over the last 2 seasons: share_sp = (made threes by s assisted by passer p + 40*q_p) / (made threes by s that were assisted + 40) where q_p is the team-average share of assisted threes from p, using play-by-play assist credit. Expected assisted-three makes lost = sum_p share_sp * P(p out) * (1 - r), where r is the replacement factor = (s three-point makes assisted per 36 in games p missed)/(same with p playing), shrunk to 0.65 with prior weight 5 games, clipped to [0,1]. Report the change in assisted-three makes per game (not attempts); as-of = injury-report vintage before tip.
raw_data: Play-by-play: shooter, assister, made flag, shot type for all threes
Games the passer missed (for replacement factor)
nba.assisted_three_passer_map.why: Translates an injury headline into a number of lost assisted threes for each shooter.

nba.opp_three_openness_allowed.label: Opponent's rate of open and wide-open three-point attempts allowed (closeout quality)
nba.opp_three_openness_allowed.mechanism: A defense's effect on a shooter's threes shows up in the proportion of attempts that are open, which is a scheme trait and more persistent than opponent 3P% allowed.
nba.opp_three_openness_allowed.rationale: Opponent 3P% allowed mixes luck with scheme; the open-attempt share allowed and the opponent's volume allowed by shot type are stable within a season and map directly to a shooter's catch-and-shoot context.
nba.opp_three_openness_allowed.measurement: From team-level aggregate defense dashboards (closest-defender bins, one row per team and date window, not per-shot; window set by a DateTo filter to games before tip) compute per defense the percentage of opponent threes taken with closest defender >= 4 ft (wide open) and 2-4 ft (open), the corner share allowed, and opponent 3PA allowed per 100 possessions; 60-game half-life, shrink to league mean with prior weight 40 games; match against the shooter's tonight's expected cell mix.
free_sources: nba_api defense dashboards by closest defender
raw_data: Team defense shot dashboard: attempts by defender distance range
nba.opp_three_openness_allowed.why: A stable, scheme-based replacement for the noisy position-allowed variable. Depends on team-level aggregate dashboards whose date-window vintages are SOURCE_UNVERIFIED (p3-defender-distance).

nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.label: Ratings-based blowout probability and starter-minutes-vs-margin curve (market-free)
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.mechanism: Rebuilds the blowout risk from team strength and rotation history instead of the closing spread: a ratings-implied expected margin and margin spread give P(large lead), and a coach/player minutes-versus-margin curve converts each margin path into expected minutes lost by starters and gained by bench players.
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.rationale: The catalog input nba.garbage is defined from the closing spread, which is a market price and so a benchmark, not an input. The causal quantity is the chance that the margin passes the coach's pull threshold early enough to matter, and how much playing time each player then loses. Subtle: the loss depends on when the lead arrives (a 20-point lead entering Q4 removes far more starter minutes than one reached with 3 minutes left), on the coach, and on whether the trailing team also pulls starters, so the curve must be conditional on the margin path and not only on the final margin.
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.measurement: Step 1, expected margin: mu = (NetRtg_home_adj - NetRtg_away_adj) * expected_possessions/100 + home_adv, where NetRtg_adj is the as-of-tipoff opponent-adjusted net rating from nba.off_rtg and nba.def_rtg (ridge regression on game point differential, half-life about 25 games, shrunk to the preseason prior with n_prior about 20 games as a placeholder to be fitted), adjusted for the confirmed unavailable players via nba.lineup_adj_rating, home_adv fitted on the last 5 seasons (about 2 points). Step 2, margin spread: sd_margin fitted on 5 seasons of residuals of final margin versus mu (league-wide roughly 12-13 points, to be estimated, with a heavier empirical tail than normal). Step 3: P(final |margin| >= 15/20/25) and P(|lead| >= 15/20 entering Q4) from the empirical residual distribution around mu. Step 4, minutes curve: from play-by-play stints, per team-season, expected minutes of each rotation player conditional on margin entering Q4 in bins (0-9, 10-14, 15-19, 20+), shrunk toward the league curve with k about 30 blowout games. Output per player: expected minutes lost and the probability of falling below a stated minutes level. No closing line or other price is used; the spread is retained only to benchmark calibration of step 3.

nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.why: Three-point attempts concentrate among starters and fall when starters sit in garbage time, but trailing teams also raise three volume; the margin-path curve separates the two.

nba.early_exit_hazard.label: Protected-void probability: first-half-only participation (injury, ejection, illness or coach-rested second half)
nba.early_exit_hazard.mechanism: P(player enters in the first half but never after halftime, including OT) = injury/ejection/illness exit hazard plus the coach decision to rest him for the whole second half in a lopsided game; the protected clause voids both unless the strike was already reached.
nba.early_exit_hazard.rationale: Early exit by injury is only one route to the void state: the sampled protected text voids any player who enters in the first half and does not enter after it, so a starter pulled for the entire second half of a first-half blowout is also void. Both routes are unrelated to per-minute rates and the second is strongly tied to the first-half margin.
nba.early_exit_hazard.measurement: Two components over the last 3 seasons. (a) Injury/ejection/illness exit hazard h = exits (left and did not return) / minutes, shrunk to a position prior with k=2000 minutes and scaled by 1.5 for the first 3 games after a listed injury; P(exit before half) = 1 - exp(-h*minutes_in_half1). (b) Coach-rest route: from play-by-play, P(no second-half entry | played first half and non-injury) by own-model pregame spread bucket and coach, estimated on 3 seasons with beta shrinkage k=30 games; combine as 1-(1-a)(1-b); then convert by contract wording (protected void vs actual stats, with the strike-already-reached carve-out).
nba.early_exit_hazard.why: Generates the KXNBA3PTPROT refund branch: P(enters in the first half but not after it) from injury/ejection exits and coach-rested second halves; no other input of this archetype models it.

nba.minutes.reason: Attempts scale with court time and spot-up shooters have the most volatile minutes of any role; must be a scenario mixture because bench shooters swing between 8 and 28 minutes with matchup and injury news.

nba.three_volume.reason: 3PA per minute and catch-and-shoot share are the most predictive stable variables; the label bundles four different quantities (attempt rate, C&S share, 3P% shrinkage, opponent 3PA allowed) into one id and so cannot be audited or measured as stated.

nba.player_shooting_regression.reason: Heavy shrinkage of 3P% is the core of any threes model; value depends on using attempts-weighted shrinkage (about 750 attempts of prior), not a generic regression-to-mean factor.

nba.usage.reason: Usage is a weak proxy for three-point volume since spot-up shooters have low usage but high 3PA rate; useful only for the on-ball vs off-ball split.

nba.teammate_absence_shift.reason: Absence of passers lowers assisted-three share while absence of competing shooters raises attempts; direction depends on who is out, which this single label does not specify.

nba.opp_def_pos.reason: 3PA and 3P% allowed by position blends scheme with opponent shot-making luck and contains a large noise component at single-game scale; replace by contest-rate allowed.

nba.def_scheme.reason: Drop coverage concedes above-the-break threes and switching tightens them; useful when interacted with the shooter's catch-and-shoot share and with opponent closeout tendencies.

nba.shot_profile.reason: Opponent share of shots from three and the corner/above-break split matter for volume, but the shooter's own location mix must be matched.

nba.pace.reason: Possessions scale attempts; second-order next to role and minutes.

nba.garbage.reason: Catalog definition is "blowout probability from spread", a closing-line quantity, so it is a market benchmark and not an input. Removed from stages, coverage, interactions and data feeds; replaced by the market-free nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve built from ratings and rotation history. Prior note: Blowouts cut starters' minutes but also inflate bench shooters' time and trailing teams' attempts, so the sign is role dependent; needs rebuild from ratings.

nba.three_pt_luck.reason: Team three-point luck regresses between games; shared team hot nights do create a within-game correlation among shooters, which is the real use.

nba.injuries_pit.reason: Own and creator availability define role changes; vintage discipline required.

nba.stat_dist.reason: Binomial given attempts understates variance; count distribution must come from a mixture over attempts and minutes.

m.quote_history.reason: Price path is observable market state, not a driver of made threes.

m.rules_text.reason: Distinguishes the standard ladder and the protected form, which pay differently for the same count distribution when the player leaves after the first half; KXNBA3PT and KXNBA3PTPROT have rules text.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook threes lines are priors to benchmark, not inputs to a model of attempts and makes.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Cross-rung coherence is a quote-quality diagnostic.

m.strike_hit_rates.reason: Calibration history per rung of realised outcomes; non-causal and used only to check probabilities.

m.orderbook_depth.reason: Execution realism only: book depth limits tradable size on thin high rungs but carries no information on made threes.

nba.market_calibration_bias.reason: Overlay on model output specific to Kalshi prices.

m.volume_oi.reason: Open interest has no mechanism link to made threes; weak even as a liquidity proxy.

m.trade_tape.reason: Order-flow microstructure on Kalshi; no causal content for made threes.

m.settlement_truth.reason: Settlement labels; reconcile with official three-pointers made before use.

nba.stat_corrections.reason: Made threes are rarely corrected after the game; negligible for this contract.

nba.player_role_position.reason: Spot-up vs pull-up classification determines how attempts react to absences; needs creation type, not positions.

nba.late_game_script.reason: Intentional fouls reduce live possessions where shooters take threes; the main late-game effect on threes is trailing-team heave volume, which is not captured by this label.

interactions.mechanism: Expected threes are minutes times attempt rate times make probability, so minutes swings dominate for bench shooters whose attempt rate is high but whose minutes vary between 8 and 28; the same minutes error costs far more for a 9-attempt-per-36 shooter than a 3-attempt one.
interactions.how_to_test: Decompose variance of threes into minutes, attempt-rate and make-rate components by role using player-game data and test that the minutes share is largest for bench shooters.

interactions.mechanism: The shrinkage weight on observed 3P% depends on cumulative attempts: a rookie with 150 attempts keeps little of a hot start while a veteran with 3000 attempts keeps most; recent form matters only for the low-attempt sample.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit predictive error of next-game 3P% using recent-form weight interacted with log career attempts and check that weight declines with attempts.

interactions.mechanism: A shooter's loss from an absent creator equals the share of his assisted attempts that creator generated times the shortfall of replacements; the effect is therefore concentrated in specific pairs rather than being a general absence penalty, and shooters with diversified passers are insulated.
interactions.how_to_test: For shooters with a dominant passer, compare attempts with vs without that passer; for diversified shooters expect near-zero effect.

interactions.mechanism: In a blowout the favorite's starters leave and bench shooters play expanded minutes with higher attempt rates, while the trailing team's shooters take more late threes; the sign of the effect of margin on threes depends on role, flipping between starters and bench specialists.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate 3PA per minute by margin bin for starters and bench separately; verify opposite slopes.

interactions.mechanism: Team-level shooting shocks (a hot night for the whole team) correlate the made-three counts of teammates; this does not change marginals but matters for parlays or when the same team's shooters appear on several rungs at once.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute correlation of made-three residuals between teammates over a season and compare with the independence benchmark.

nonlinearities.shape: convex tail: P(5+) rises faster than the mean attempt rate
nonlinearities.why: A threshold of five makes needs about 13 attempts at 36%; small increases in attempt rate move tail probability multiplicatively because 5+ sits far above the mean.

nonlinearities.shape: saturating: weight on recent make rate declines with attempt count
nonlinearities.why: Bayesian shrinkage gives a weight n/(n+k) on observed rate; with k near 750 attempts the weight on a 100-attempt sample is under 12%, so predicted make probability barely moves.

nonlinearities.shape: non-monotone in margin: attempts fall for starters, rise for bench and trailing team
nonlinearities.why: The effect of blowout probability on threes depends on role and on late-game urgency, giving a U- or inverted-U relation rather than a monotone one.

contract.settlement_definition: Period contracts settle on points scored in a defined segment of the named game: quarter and half winner (the team scoring more points in the period), 'tie' contracts (YES if neither team wins the period), spreads (named team wins the period by more than X.5), totals (combined period points above X.5) and team totals (one team's period points above X.5). Quarters 1-4 and the first half count regulation points only. The second half differs by family: KXNBA2H, KXNBA2HSPREAD and KXNBA2HTOTAL say '(including overtime)', while KXNBA2HWINNER covers 'the second half (excluding overtime)'. Two winner families coexist: KXNBA1Q-4Q/KXNBA1H/KXNBA2H list a separate tie contract, and the KXNBA*WINNER series state that on equal points all team strikes resolve No and the Tie strike Yes; the WINNER family keeps postponed games open until the rescheduled game ends within two weeks, while the spread/total/tie texts sampled show no postponement wording. KXNBA1QTEAMTOTAL and KXNBA4QTEAMTOTAL are TITLE_ONLY.

rules_evidence.quote: Note: Only points scored during the 1st half count towards this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: First-half contracts count only first-half points, so overtime cannot enter them.

rules_evidence.quote: Note: Only points scored during the 2nd half (including overtime) count towards this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: Second-half contracts include overtime points, creating a wedge between 2H and Q3+Q4 regulation totals.

rules_evidence.quote: Note: 4th quarter markets do not include overtime.
rules_evidence.establishes: Quarter markets exclude overtime; the same standard note is printed on Q1-Q3 contracts.

rules_evidence.quote: If neither team wins the 1st quarter of the Miami vs Sacramento Pro Basketball game originally scheduled for Nov 8, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Period tie is a separate YES contract; winner markets therefore carry three outcomes with tie mass of about one in twenty.

rules_evidence.quote: If over 68.5 total points are scored in the 4th quarter (excluding overtime)
rules_evidence.establishes: Fourth-quarter totals explicitly exclude overtime in the primary text, so the overtime mixture applies only to 2H contracts.

rules_evidence.quote: If the market references the 2nd half, that does not include overtime.
rules_evidence.establishes: The second-half winner family excludes overtime, the opposite of KXNBA2H/KXNBA2HSPREAD/KXNBA2HTOTAL, so the same game produces different 2H outcomes across series when it goes to overtime.

rules_evidence.quote: If both teams score the same amount of points during the half, all team strikes resolve to No and the Tie strike resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Winner-family contracts are three-way partitions with an explicit Tie strike; a team strike pays nothing on a tied period.

variants_and_edge_cases: Overtime inclusion differs by series, not only by period: Q1-Q4 and 1H exclude OT; KXNBA2H, KXNBA2HSPREAD and KXNBA2HTOTAL include it; KXNBA2HWINNER excludes it. A game tied after regulation adds roughly 22-26 combined points to 2H totals and spreads but cannot change the KXNBA2HWINNER result.

Winner contracts are three-way: the KXNBA1Q-4Q/1H/2H series list 'tie' as its own contract and the WINNER family pays a Tie strike while team strikes resolve No, so a model must output a three-way probability with integer tie mass.

Sampled strikes are far from central values (1st quarter total 71.5, 2nd quarter total 70.5, 2nd half total 135.5) and 1H team total 64.5, consistent with ladders of rungs; which rungs are live is not stated in the rules.
Spread strikes are half-points (7.5, 8.5), so no push exists; a tied period is NO for any team-wins-by-X spread.
Postponement: the WINNER family stays open until a rescheduled game finishes within two weeks; the sampled tie/spread/total texts carry no postponement sentence, so their void handling is not read.

The WINNER-family samples (KXNBA1QWINNER-KXNBA4QWINNER, KXNBA1HWINNER, KXNBA2HWINNER) are finalized markets from the 26JUN13 New York vs San Antonio Finals game, while the tie/spread/total samples are November 2026 regular-season markets; whether the WINNER family is still listed with the same wording is not verified.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official game linescore / play-by-play scoring by period from the named league sources; the sampled period rules do not name the source agencies.

mechanism.summary: A quarter or half is a short scoring contest of roughly 24 possessions per team whose outcome is determined by who is on the floor in that segment, the number of possessions, efficiency per possession and small-sample noise, with score-state feedback across periods. The chain is: starters and rotation templates by quarter (Q1 and Q3 starters, Q2 bench-heavy, Q4 closers or garbage time), the period possession count (fast starts, slow lopsided Q4), unit-level offensive and defensive strength against the opponent's units, shooting variance that is large relative to a 24-possession sample, foul and bonus timing that resets each quarter, end-of-period shot-clock possessions, and the settlement rule (overtime excluded from quarters and first half, included in the second half for KXNBA2H, KXNBA2HSPREAD and KXNBA2HTOTAL but excluded for KXNBA2HWINNER; ties pay a separate market). Because the sample is small, period margin is a noisy integer variable whose discreteness (ties, half-point cut points) matters, and most information comes from lineup identity and rotation structure rather than team-season averages.

stages.name: Lineups and rotation templates by quarter
stages.description: Coaches deploy starters for the first six to eight minutes, stagger substitutions into Q2, restart with starters in Q3 and then use closers or reserves in Q4 depending on score. Which five play in each period, and who is absent, determine the strength of the units. Starters confirmed shortly before tip are the most valuable late information for Q1 and Q3 markets; Q2 and Q4 depend on bench availability and coaching style.
stages.distribution: Discrete personnel states by quarter; the Q1 state is nearly deterministic after the starters are announced while Q4 is a mixture dependent on score.

stages.name: Period possessions and pace
stages.description: Possessions per period reflect both teams' tendencies and game state: fast early periods, decreased pace in lopsided late periods, long possessions at the end of a quarter. Period pace is not the game pace; each team's style and the identity of the units determine it, and totals markets scale with this count.
stages.distribution: Approximately normal around 24-26 possessions per team with sd about 2.5; correlated across the two teams and right-skewed by end-of-period shot-clock dynamics.

stages.name: Unit efficiency and matchup
stages.description: Each unit's points per possession against the opponent's units come from ratings of the relevant players, shot profile and defensive scheme. Opponent-adjusted ratings from full games blur unit differences, especially in Q2 and Q4, where bench-heavy units dominate. Matchup-specific mismatches (a bench big against a switching unit) matter more in short periods.
stages.distribution: Unit PPP roughly normal across units (sd of unit ratings about 6 per 100 possessions) with large sampling noise per period.

stages.name: Small-sample scoring noise and the margin distribution
stages.description: With about 24 possessions per team the sd of a team's quarter points is around five and the margin sd around seven; shooting luck therefore dominates and the probability mass at small integer margins (including the tie) cannot be treated as continuous. Hot starts regress rather than carry into later periods, so period luck is nearly independent across quarters.
stages.distribution: Discrete difference of two near-Poisson-binomial scores (Skellam-like) with excess kurtosis; tie mass of about 4-6% per quarter, higher in low-pace periods.

stages.name: Score-state feedback, halftime adjustments and foul resets
stages.description: Leads and trailing affect later periods: leading teams in the 2H may rest starters early, Q3 sees halftime adjustments, Q4 sees intentional fouling and clock management. Team fouls reset each quarter so bonus free throws cluster late in periods; end-of-quarter possessions and heaves shift totals. These effects are small for Q1 but central for Q4 and 2H markets.
stages.distribution: State-dependent mixture: Q4 and 2H are regime-switching with blowout versus close-game regimes; foul effects add right-skew to period totals.

stages.name: Settlement partitions and cross-market identities
stages.description: The contracts partition the game: Q1+Q2=1H and Q3+Q4 = regulation second half, to which overtime is added only for KXNBA2H, KXNBA2HSPREAD and KXNBA2HTOTAL; KXNBA2HWINNER and all quarter series stop at regulation. A game tied after regulation triggers a five-minute overtime that adds roughly 22-26 combined points (about 11-13 per team) to the OT-inclusive 2H series only. Period winners carry a tie outcome. Consistency across period totals and the game total is an identity, not a signal, and the series-specific rule text defines which points count.
stages.distribution: Deterministic sum identities with a mixture over OT presence; P(OT) roughly 5-7% overall, taken from the zero mass of the ratings-implied regulation margin rather than a spread bucket, plus a small multi-OT tail.

stages.name: In-play conditioning for quarter and half markets
stages.description: Because the quarter and half markets (Q1 and 1H included) stay open until a winner or the event is decided, a quote placed during the game is a bet on the remaining part of a period given what has already happened. The value is the conditional distribution of the remaining margin given the current score, period start score, clock, the lineups actually on the floor, team-foul and bonus state and timeouts. Pregame inputs set the prior; the live state dominates once a period is under way.
stages.distribution: Remaining-margin variance shrinks roughly linearly with remaining possessions; a period lead late in the quarter makes the outcome near-deterministic, with discrete jumps at each score.

talent_strength.note: Unit-level strength by quarter rather than full-game team ratings.

opponent_matchup.note: Opponent units faced in each period, with scheme interactions at unit level.

role_personnel.note: Who plays each quarter is the central variable.

availability_news.note: Confirmed starters and absentees vintage matter for Q1/Q3.

coaching_scheme.note: Stagger patterns, Q3 adjustments and closing-unit decisions.

environment.note: Travel, altitude and rest may slow Q1 but effects are small; kept as context.

game_context_script.note: Blowout and close-game regimes for Q4/2H, and OT presence for 2H.

efficiency_conversion.note: Period shooting luck and unit efficiency.

distribution_variance.note: Discrete margin and total pmfs with tie mass, built from raw period scores (nba.period_margin_pmf); the line-residual nba.score_resid is benchmark-only and no longer used here.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest and travel; weakly evidenced for period effects, and no motivation or clinch variable is included.

officiating_rules.note: Quarter-specific bonus and foul-reset mechanics and crew foul rates.

nba.quarter_unit_projection.label: Per-quarter expected on-court units and their projected net/offensive rating
nba.quarter_unit_projection.mechanism: Each quarter's scoring is the possession-weighted sum of ratings of the specific five-man units on the floor; coaches' stagger patterns make Q2 and Q4 weak or strong depending on who is available.
nba.quarter_unit_projection.rationale: Full-game ratings average over rotation; Q2 often features bench units with one starter, while Q1 and Q3 start with the best five. Because rotation patterns are predictable from coach tenure and are altered by injuries, a projection by quarter is a pregame-computable improvement over team ratings.
nba.quarter_unit_projection.measurement: Per team build a player x quarter minute-share matrix from the last 30 games (15-game half-life) separately for each coach, conditioned on the as-of starters list and injury vintage by renormalising when players are out. Player ratings = RAPM-style ridge regression (lambda by rolling-origin CV on game-level data) of stint point margin per 100 possessions on on-court player indicators using only games before tip. Quarter strength = sum over on-court players of rating x minute share (additive player model, not 5-man lineup ratings) and opponent quarter strength by the same method; expected quarter points per 100 = league ORtg + offensive rating terms. Output expected team points, possessions and margin per quarter with standard errors from bootstrap over games; as-of: confirmed starters (about 30 minutes before tip) else a mixture over probable starters.
raw_data: stint and substitution data by quarter
injury report vintages and confirmed starters
nba.quarter_unit_projection.why: Replaces team-season averages with the actual quarter-specific personnel, which is where period markets differ from the game market.

nba.period_margin_pmf.label: Empirical period-margin and period-total probability mass functions (ties, half-point cut points)
nba.period_margin_pmf.mechanism: Quarter margins are small integers with a sizeable mass at zero and at +/-1..3; winner, spread and total contracts cut this discrete distribution at specific points, so pmf shape (not only mean and sd) sets the probability.
nba.period_margin_pmf.rationale: A Gaussian approximation misprices tie mass (about 4-6% per quarter) and the probability of exceeding a half-point strike; the shape depends on pace (lower-possession periods have fewer scoring events) and on variance of the team-pair.
nba.period_margin_pmf.measurement: From all games in 5 seasons compute standardized period margin and total (actual minus rating-based expectation, built without market lines), fit a discrete mixture (Skellam-like with pace-dependent variance and a small-excess-kurtosis component) per period type (Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4, 1H, 2H-with-OT) via maximum likelihood with a team-pair variance covariate; report pmf at integer margins within +/-25 and the tie probability by expected pace tercile.
raw_data: Linescore by period for each game incl. OT points
nba.period_margin_pmf.why: Directly gives tie probability for the winner contracts and exceedance probabilities at 7.5/8.5 margin strikes without relying on a normal approximation.

nba.period_foul_bonus_state.label: Team-foul and bonus-state exposure per period (foul reset each quarter, end-of-period fouling)
nba.period_foul_bonus_state.mechanism: Team fouls reset each quarter, so the shape of free-throw production within a period depends on when a team reaches the penalty, and Q4 end-of-period fouling adds free throws that distort Q4 totals and margins.
nba.period_foul_bonus_state.rationale: Free-throw volume per period differs from per-game rates because bonus onset is quarter-specific; crews that call more early fouls bring forward bonus situations in Q1/Q3, which can change period totals by 2-3 points; the effect is partly predictable from crew and team foul rates.
nba.period_foul_bonus_state.measurement: Compute team FTA per quarter and fouls per quarter from play-by-play over 2 seasons with 60-game half-life; estimate crew and team coefficients on quarter FTA via mixed model; project expected time-to-bonus in each quarter and expected FTA by period for tonight's matchup and crew; output expected FT points by period. As-of: crew assignment (announced game day) and team rates.
free_sources: nba_api playbyplayv3 foul and FT events
raw_data: PBP fouls and FTA by period
nba.period_foul_bonus_state.why: Period markets, unlike full-game markets, are sensitive to bonus timing because FT points cluster after the penalty begins.

nba.second_half_adjustment_effect.label: Coach-specific second-half and Q3 adjustment effect (Q3 efficiency minus game baseline)
nba.second_half_adjustment_effect.mechanism: After halftime coaches adjust schemes and starters re-enter, so Q3 scoring is not an average of Q1 and Q2 and certain coaches systematically outscore their baseline in Q3.
nba.second_half_adjustment_effect.rationale: Q3 and Q1 both start with starters but have different information sets; evidence of Q3 effects by coach is plausible but noisy; the quantity matters for Q3 winner/spread/total and for the 2H markets, and interacts with lead size.
nba.second_half_adjustment_effect.measurement: For each coach-team-season compute Q3 net rating minus first-half net rating regressed on margin at halftime and minutes played by starters in the first half; empirical-Bayes shrink across coaches (variance component estimated by method of moments) so that individual coach effects are heavily shrunk (typical shrinkage 80-90%); apply only when the coach is unchanged. As-of: games before tip.
raw_data: period net rating by team and game
nba.second_half_adjustment_effect.why: Provides the only structural reason for 2H/Q3 prices to differ from simple linear splits of full-game lines.

nba.period_possession_split.label: Possessions by quarter and team pace profile (fast early, slower late in lopsided games)
nba.period_possession_split.mechanism: Possessions per quarter vary by period (fast Q1, slower Q4 in decided games) and each coach has a pace style, so period totals scale with a period-specific possession count.
nba.period_possession_split.rationale: Applying game pace to a quarter overstates Q4 possessions in blowouts and understates Q1 for fast starters; the possession count times PPP is the correct decomposition for totals and team totals.
nba.period_possession_split.measurement: From play-by-play compute possessions per quarter per team with the standard possession formula (FGA - OREB + TOV + 0.44 FTA) by period for the last 2 seasons with 50-game half-life; model matchup period pace as weighted geometric mean with a slow-team weight of about 0.55 (estimate by regression); condition Q4 on pregame blowout-probability tercile. Output expected possessions per period and sd.
free_sources: nba_api box scores by period / PBP
nba.period_possession_split.why: Gives the period-specific volume term missing from the full-game pace input.

nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.label: Ratings-based blowout probability and starter-minutes-vs-margin curve (market-free)
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.mechanism: Rebuilds the blowout risk from team strength and rotation history instead of the closing spread: a ratings-implied expected margin and margin spread give P(large lead), and a coach/player minutes-versus-margin curve converts each margin path into expected minutes lost by starters and gained by bench players.
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.rationale: The catalog input nba.garbage is defined from the closing spread, which is a market price and so a benchmark, not an input. The causal quantity is the chance that the margin passes the coach's pull threshold early enough to matter, and how much playing time each player then loses. Subtle: the loss depends on when the lead arrives (a 20-point lead entering Q4 removes far more starter minutes than one reached with 3 minutes left), on the coach, and on whether the trailing team also pulls starters, so the curve must be conditional on the margin path and not only on the final margin.
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.measurement: Step 1, expected margin: mu = (NetRtg_home_adj - NetRtg_away_adj) * expected_possessions/100 + home_adv, where NetRtg_adj is the as-of-tipoff opponent-adjusted net rating from nba.off_rtg and nba.def_rtg (ridge regression on game point differential, half-life about 25 games, shrunk to the preseason prior with n_prior about 20 games as a placeholder to be fitted), adjusted for the confirmed unavailable players via nba.lineup_adj_rating, home_adv fitted on the last 5 seasons (about 2 points). Step 2, margin spread: sd_margin fitted on 5 seasons of residuals of final margin versus mu (league-wide roughly 12-13 points, to be estimated, with a heavier empirical tail than normal). Step 3: P(final |margin| >= 15/20/25) and P(|lead| >= 15/20 entering Q4) from the empirical residual distribution around mu. Step 4, minutes curve: from play-by-play stints, per team-season, expected minutes of each rotation player conditional on margin entering Q4 in bins (0-9, 10-14, 15-19, 20+), shrunk toward the league curve with k about 30 blowout games. Output per player: expected minutes lost and the probability of falling below a stated minutes level. No closing line or other price is used; the spread is retained only to benchmark calibration of step 3.

nba.ot_prob_ratings_margin.label: Market-free overtime probability and overtime scoring increment from the ratings-implied regulation margin
nba.ot_prob_ratings_margin.mechanism: A game goes to overtime only if the regulation margin is exactly zero, so P(OT) is the mass at zero of the regulation-margin distribution, highest for evenly matched teams; each five-minute overtime then adds scoring at both teams' per-minute rates, and a further overtime follows with the tie probability of a five-minute period.
nba.ot_prob_ratings_margin.rationale: The catalog nba.ot_model conditions P(OT) on the closing-spread bucket (a market quantity) and says one OT adds about 10-12 points to totals, which is the per-team figure, not the combined one. A market-free version takes the regulation-margin distribution from team ratings and sizes OT correctly: roughly 11-13 points per team and 22-26 combined per period, with repeated overtimes possible. Subtle: the zero-margin mass is larger than a continuous normal approximation gives, because end-of-game tactics (holding for the last shot, fouling when ahead by three) cluster regulation margins between 0 and 3.
nba.ot_prob_ratings_margin.measurement: Step 1: regulation-margin mean mu from nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve (opponent-adjusted net ratings x expected possessions/100 + home advantage, as of tipoff, adjusted for confirmed inactives). Step 2: P(regulation tie) = logistic regression of the indicator "regulation margin = 0" on |mu| over the last 5 regular seasons (about 6,000 games; league base rate to be estimated), smoothed across 1-point |mu| bins. Step 3: per-team OT points = league points per team per OT period from play-by-play scaled by the team's opponent-adjusted pace and offensive rating relative to league; combined OT points = sum over both teams. Step 4: P(k-th OT | (k-1)-th OT) = pooled empirical tie rate of five-minute periods with prior weight 200 OT periods. Output P(OT), P(2+ OT), per-team and combined OT-points distributions. Only team ratings, pace and results enter.
