Basketball-Reference box scores with OT period lines (free, polite scraping)
raw_data: Team game logs with regulation and overtime period scores
Opponent-adjusted team ratings as of tipoff
Play-by-play overtime periods with possessions and points
nba.ot_prob_ratings_margin.why: The 2H winner, spread and total include overtime while Q1-Q4 and 1H do not, so the wedge between 2H and Q3+Q4 is exactly P(OT) times the combined OT points; this supplies both without a spread bucket.

nba.second_half_reg_ot_joint_margin.label: Joint second-half margin: regulation-only and overtime-inclusive outputs from one simulated game
nba.second_half_reg_ot_joint_margin.mechanism: The OT-inclusive second-half margin equals the regulation second-half margin plus the overtime margin, and overtime happens only when the regulation full-game margin is zero, so both 2H contract versions come from one draw.
nba.second_half_reg_ot_joint_margin.rationale: Rules text: KXNBA2H, KXNBA2HSPREAD and KXNBA2HTOTAL count the 2nd half including overtime, KXNBA2HWINNER excludes it. Pricing the two separately breaks the identity that they differ only in games tied after regulation; e.g. a 2H tie under KXNBA2HWINNER plus OT gives a decided KXNBA2H.
nba.second_half_reg_ot_joint_margin.measurement: Per simulated game: draw H1 and regulation H2 margins from nba.period_margin_pmf (correlated via nba.second_half_adjustment_effect); regulation full margin = H1 + H2reg; if zero, draw number of OT periods and each OT margin from nba.ot_prob_ratings_margin (5-minute periods, repeat while tied); outputs: M2H_reg = H2reg (settles KXNBA2HWINNER, tie possible), M2H_ot = H2reg + sum(OT margins) (settles KXNBA2H, KXNBA2HSPREAD; totals add OT points); 50,000 draws per game; as-of tip. Check on settled pairs from every overtime game.
nba.second_half_reg_ot_joint_margin.why: Produces both settlement variants of the second half from one coherent game draw.

nba.live_period_state.label: In-play game state for period and half markets (score, clock, on-court lineups, team fouls, timeouts)
nba.live_period_state.mechanism: Quarter, first-half and second-half markets keep trading after tipoff, so their value is conditional on the realised state at the quote time rather than the pregame distribution.
nba.live_period_state.rationale: Verified on the Kalshi API (9 Nov 2026): KXNBA2H markets for 9 Nov games have close_time 12 Nov 03:00Z, two days after the game, with early close 'after a winner is declared'; KXNBA1Q markets for the 10 Nov OKC-POR game have close_time 13 Nov 04:00Z with the same early-close condition, and a KXNBA1HTOTAL market for the 8 Nov BKN-DAL game carried 'close early if the event occurs' and closed at 02:10:05Z on 9 Nov, well after its open_time (the exact tip time was not read, so how long after tip it stayed open is unverified). Q1 and 1H markets therefore also trade in play once the game starts, while Q1 is still the most pregame-predictable quantity before tip. Prices then depend on the current margin, period, on-court five, team fouls toward the bonus, and timeouts left, none of which a pregame input carries.
nba.live_period_state.measurement: At each quote timestamp: period, game clock (seconds), score by team, score at the start of the current period, five players on court per team, team fouls in the period (bonus at 5), timeouts remaining, possession; source cdn.nba.com liveData play-by-play and boxscore JSON polled every 5-10 s with receipt timestamps; the period-margin model is re-run conditional on elapsed time and remaining possessions (nba.period_possession_split scaled by remaining clock) and the on-court units' ratings from nba.quarter_unit_projection. As-of: quote timestamp minus feed latency (record both).
free_sources: cdn.nba.com liveData play-by-play and boxscore JSON (free, unofficial)
raw_data: Live boxscore with on-court flags and team fouls
nba.live_period_state.why: Quarter (Q1-Q4), 1H and 2H markets all trade in play (KXNBA1Q and KXNBA2H early-close only after a winner is declared; KXNBA1HTOTAL closes early on the event), so value is conditional on the live state at the quote time; Q1 and 1H keep their pregame prior until tip.

nba.starters_pit.reason: Confirmed starters, available about 30 minutes before tip, fix Q1 and Q3 personnel; the single most informative late-arriving variable for early-period markets, but only if the vintage is time-stamped relative to the order time.

nba.rotation.reason: Stint templates (when starters sit in Q1, Q2 staggering, Q4 closing unit) are what make each period different; too generic as written, it needs to be turned into expected on-court units per quarter.

nba.q_scoring.reason: Historical period scoring by team confounds lineup, opponent and game-script effects and uses small samples per team-quarter (about 80 games); as a standalone average it is mostly noise around full-game ratings, so only a shrunk period-specific deviation is useful.

nba.pace.reason: Period possessions drive total and team-total markets; but pace differs by quarter and is not the mean of two season paces, so a period-specific, lineup-aware version is required.

nba.off_rtg.reason: Full-game offensive rating mixes starters and bench; needs a starter-weighted version for Q1/Q3 and a bench-weighted one for Q2 to be informative.

nba.def_rtg.reason: Same issue as offensive rating; duplicates what an on-court-unit projection delivers once rotation is modelled.

nba.injuries_pit.reason: An absent starter changes Q1/Q3 more than the full-game average; vintage and confirmation timing matter.

nba.garbage.reason: Catalog definition is "blowout probability from spread", a closing-line quantity, so it is a market benchmark and not an input. Removed from stages, coverage, interactions and data feeds; replaced by the market-free nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve built from ratings and rotation history. Prior note: Blowout probability matters for Q4 and for the 2H but is irrelevant for Q1; built from the spread it is a market observable and should be rebuilt from ratings.

nba.late_game_script.reason: Q4 fouling and clock are the key to Q4 totals and spreads and to end-of-quarter possessions in other periods; applies mostly to Q4 and 2H.

nba.score_resid.reason: Defined as residuals around market lines, so it is a calibration of the book not a driver; the required object is the raw period-margin distribution from scores, built without lines.

nba.three_pt_luck.reason: Hot starts regress; correct that a Q1 3P% outlier has no persistence into Q3, but this is a contextual caution rather than a predictor.

nba.rest_travel.reason: Slow-start-after-travel effects are small and unconfirmed for Q1; kept as context.

m.quote_history.reason: Price path is market state; useful to time when lineup news hit the quote, not a driver of period scoring.

m.rules_text.reason: Defines the split: Q1-Q3 and Q4 and 1H exclude overtime, 2H includes it, tie markets resolve YES when neither team wins; essential.

m.external_lines.reason: Labelled primary but is the sportsbook price; it is a benchmark to compare against, and using it as an input would copy the market rather than model periods.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Cross-strike coherence is a quote-quality diagnostic; the sum-to-game-total consistency across periods is a useful arbitrage check but not a model input.

interactions.mechanism: Team Q1 history is valid only if tonight's starting five matches the historical one; a changed starter makes the stored Q1 rating stale, and the loss is larger for first and third quarters than for second and fourth, where the bench pattern matters more.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare Q1 margin prediction error when the starting five is the modal five versus when one starter differs, holding team rating fixed.

interactions.mechanism: Second-half lineups depend on the first-half margin: when the margin exceeds roughly 15 at halftime coaches shorten Q3 starter minutes and use bench units in Q4, so Q3 and Q4 are two different regimes whose scoring rates differ in both pace and efficiency.
interactions.how_to_test: Condition Q3/Q4 total and margin on halftime-margin bins and test a break at |margin| near 15.

interactions.mechanism: Because 2H contracts include overtime and Q4 contracts do not, the 2H total is Q3 plus Q4 plus an overtime component with probability about 5-7% and size about 22-26 combined points (about 11-13 per team), producing a right-skew in the 2H total and a wedge to Q3+Q4 prices.
interactions.how_to_test: Decompose 2H total into regulation and OT parts in history and compare tail probabilities of the 2H total with and without the OT mixture component.

interactions.mechanism: Tie probability and margin variance both rise as possessions per period fall because fewer scoring events produce smaller margins; slow-pace matchups therefore have higher tie mass and lower probability of crossing 7.5/8.5 margin strikes.
interactions.how_to_test: Bin quarters by projected possessions and compare empirical tie frequency and exceedance rates at 7.5.

interactions.mechanism: End-of-quarter fouling when the team is in the bonus produces clusters of free throws at near-100% value; this convexly raises Q4 totals when the game is within 5 points, whereas early-quarter fouls matter less because bonus onset is later.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare Q4 FTA and points per possession in the final two minutes by margin bin and team-foul count.

nonlinearities.shape: discrete, peaked at zero with excess kurtosis (Skellam-like)
nonlinearities.why: Winner, tie and spread-at-7.5 contracts cut a discrete integer distribution at specific points; a Gaussian approximation misstates tie mass and tail probability by 1-2 percentage points.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold: Q4 regime switch when margin exceeds about 15-18 entering Q4
nonlinearities.why: Starters are removed once the game is decided so Q4 pace and efficiency change discontinuously; effect on Q4 total and margin is small until the threshold.

nonlinearities.shape: step: effect of a missing starter on Q1 is larger than a proportional rating drop
nonlinearities.why: A missing starter changes all four teammates' lineup context in Q1 and also removes the scripted first-stint plays; the rating loss of the unit exceeds the player's marginal contribution.

nonlinearities.shape: concave: possessions saturate in fast periods while slow periods cluster tightly
nonlinearities.why: Pace is bounded by the 24-second clock so possession counts have limited upside but can drop sharply in lopsided Q4s.

contract.settlement_definition: Two live series, both with sampled rules. KXNBARACE is a single-game TEAM race: YES if the named team is 'the first to score' N points in the named game (sample: New Orleans reaches 30 first vs Golden State). KXNBAPTSLEADER is a single-game argmax over all players of both teams: YES if the named player records the most points in the game; co-leaders split, with Yes paying $1/N (rounded down) for N tied players; a player who is inactive or never enters is deemed to have scored 0 points, so he settles NO rather than void. For both, a game postponed but starting within 48 hours stays open and resolves on the official final result, otherwise all markets resolve to a fair price. Neither text says whether overtime points count for the leader (overtime is part of the official final result in normal usage) nor what happens if neither team reaches N.

rules_evidence.quote: If New Orleans is the first to score 30 points in the New Orleans vs Golden State Pro Basketball game originally scheduled for Nov 9, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Race contract is single-game and team-based (not player-based, not season-long), with N = 30 in the sample; the event is decided by first passage of the team score.

rules_evidence.quote: If multiple players are tied for the most points at the end of the game, “Yes” positions will pay $1/N (rounded down to the nearest cent), where N is the number of tied players
rules_evidence.establishes: Leader ties are split 1/N among tied players rather than voided or decided by a tiebreak, so a tied maximum is a partial payout.

rules_evidence.quote: If a player is inactive or does not enter the game, they are deemed to have recorded 0 points.
rules_evidence.establishes: No void branch for the leader contract: the probability of being inactive enters the price directly, unlike single-player ladders that settle inactive players at a fair price.

variants_and_edge_cases: Leader ties pay $1/N: for two near-equal stars the payout is a mixture of 1, 1/2 and 0, so the tied-maximum probability (to be computed from box scores, plausibly several percent of games) must be modelled, not ignored.

Inactive equals 0 points for the leader contract: a questionable star's price is P(plays) x P(leads | plays), so the injury-status vintage enters at full weight, unlike points ladders where inactive players are voided.

Race to N is team-based and single-game; the sample has N = 30, a level usually reached late in the first quarter or early in the second, so the opening possession matters little and first-stint unit strength and pace dominate. Other N values may be listed; the rules do not fix a set.
Neither team reaching N is possible only for large N or an abandoned game; the race text gives no NO/void rule for it, and for N = 30 it is practically impossible in a completed game.
Overtime: the leader rules say 'at the end of the game' and resolve on the official final result, which suggests OT points count, but the text does not say so explicitly (open item rl-no-rules).
contract.settlement_data_source: Official final result and box score of the named game (the sampled rules say 'resolve based on the official final result' for postponed games); play-by-play scoring order is needed to determine who reached N first. The specific source agencies are not named in the sample.

mechanism.summary: Race-to-N is a first-passage problem on two alternating-possession scoring processes with lumpy 0-3 point outcomes, so the winner is determined by who starts with the ball, the starters' first-stint scoring rates and the early-game noise, with the first-possession edge hypothesised at roughly half a possession (unverified) and diminishing relative to noise as N grows. Points leader is the argmax over around twenty players' final points, driven by minutes (including overtime and blowout cuts), usage allocation within the unit, per-shot efficiency and a heavy-tailed scoring distribution, with negative dependence between teammates and positive dependence across teams through pace. Both contracts are winner-take-all functionals of the underlying scoring processes, so the tails and dependence matter far more than means, and settlement details (ties, overtime) change the answer materially.

stages.name: Opening conditions: tip, starters and first possession
stages.description: The race starts with the opening tip determining first possession and with the identity of the starters, confirmed only shortly before tip. The first possession is hypothesised to be worth about half a possession (unverified, to be estimated from play-by-play) in expected points, which is a large share of the total edge for small N and a minor one for N of 25 or more. Starter changes shift early scoring rates immediately.
stages.distribution: Binary tip outcome near 50/50 with weak team dependence; starters a discrete state known late; early scoring edge is assumed to scale as the inverse of sqrt(N) (to be tested).

stages.name: Alternating-possession scoring dynamics
stages.description: Each possession ends in 0, 1, 2 or 3 points (with and-ones and free throws as lumps) and possession passes to the other team after a made field goal. The time to N points is a sum of lumpy renewals with correlation between teams induced by alternation, and per-possession efficiency of the starters against the opposing starters determines the winner.
stages.distribution: First-passage of two correlated renewal-reward processes with increments in {0,1,2,3}; overshoot and lumpiness matter at small N; the lead changes frequently.

stages.name: Participation and minutes of candidate leaders
stages.description: For the leader contract, each candidate's minutes are a mixture: full starter load, blowout trimming, foul trouble, early exit and overtime. The pool of plausible leaders shrinks to the top two to three scorers per team, so the minutes tail of those stars largely determines the winner.
stages.distribution: Mixture with left-tail and OT bump; the minutes of the top scorers are positively correlated with a close game.

stages.name: Shot allocation, efficiency and the tail of points
stages.description: Given minutes, a candidate's points depend on usage within the unit and shooting efficiency. Teammate absences concentrate scoring on fewer players and remove competitors for the title. Points distributions have a heavy right tail, so the maximum is often set by an outlier shooting night.
stages.distribution: Right-skewed, overdispersed points per player; negatively correlated within team given team total, positively across teams.

stages.name: Selection of the maximum and settlement
stages.description: The leader is the argmax over the candidate set; leader probability depends on the gap in expected points to the nearest rival and on the variance of each, and decays quickly with the gap. Settlement is read from the rules: co-leaders split $1/N, so near-equal stars carry partial payouts; inactive players score 0 and settle NO, so P(active) multiplies the whole price; the race is won by the team whose score first reaches N.
stages.distribution: Winner-take-all functional (max of correlated heavy-tailed variables); probability concentrated in top few candidates; ties possible at integer maxima.

talent_strength.note: Starter-first-stint strength for the race and scoring ability of the top candidates for the leader market.

opponent_matchup.note: Opposing starters' defense in the first stint and rim protection facing the candidates.

environment.note: Neither contract has a venue-specific mechanism beyond what pace and starters already encode; home court has a small effect on early scoring and is absorbed in the race regression covariate.

nba.first_passage_race_table.label: Empirical race-to-N first-passage table by N, opening possession and early-game rating gap
nba.first_passage_race_table.mechanism: First-to-N is a first-passage problem on two alternating-possession scoring processes with lumpy increments; the answer depends on N, who has the ball first and the early-game scoring rate gap.
nba.first_passage_race_table.rationale: Treating the race as two independent Poisson clocks mispredicts because possessions alternate and scores come in 1-3 point lumps; the first-possession advantage is hypothesised to be about half a possession (unverified) and its relative value shrinks with N, so a table by N is needed. Scope: single-game race-to-N only; it does not describe a season-long first-to-threshold contract.
nba.first_passage_race_table.measurement: From 5 seasons of play-by-play compute for each game and each N in {5,10,15,20,25,30} which team reached N first, whether that team had the opening possession and the starters' first-stint net rating gap; fit logistic regressions per N with covariates (opening possession, rating gap, home) and ridge shrinkage; output P(win race) with standard errors. Rating gap uses the first-stint rating below, not full-game rating.
raw_data: PBP scoring events with clock and running totals
First-stint rating from the opening-stint input
nba.first_passage_race_table.why: Gives the exact functional form of the race outcome as a function of N, so thresholds below 15 are not treated like game totals.

nba.opening_stint_unit_rating.label: Starting-five first-stint offensive and defensive rating and scoring-event mix
nba.opening_stint_unit_rating.mechanism: The race is decided in the first 4-8 minutes by the starters, whose joint rating differs from season team rating and depends on the exact five.
nba.opening_stint_unit_rating.rationale: Season team ratings average starters and bench; a starter-specific, first-stint rating (with set plays, shot mix and turnover rate) is the relevant strength and changes immediately if one starter is replaced.
nba.opening_stint_unit_rating.measurement: For each team compute points per 100 possessions and per-possession scoring-event distribution (0,1,2,3 points) for the first 8 minutes of games using the modal starting five over last 60 games (half-life 30 games), shrink to the team's full-game rating with prior weight 400 possessions; when tonight's starters differ, recompute via player-level on/off ridge ratings. As-of: starters confirmation time.
raw_data: Lineup stints in first period with possessions and points
nba.opening_stint_unit_rating.why: Provides the strength variable at the right horizon and sensitivity to a single lineup change.

nba.leader_share_by_usage_rank.label: Historical probability of being the game's top scorer by team scoring rank and usage gap
nba.leader_share_by_usage_rank.mechanism: The leader is the maximum of about 20 players' points, concentrated among each team's top two or three scorers; the share a player has as leader depends on the gap in expected points to the nearest rivals, not on his own mean.
nba.leader_share_by_usage_rank.rationale: Treating each player's points as independent normals overstates the chance of the second option and ignores that teammates' points are negatively correlated given team total; empirical leader shares by rank and gap calibrate the max-of-correlated-variables model.
nba.leader_share_by_usage_rank.measurement: From 5 seasons of box scores compute for every player-game his rank among teammates by pregame expected points, the gap to the top rival in expected points, minutes and the indicator of leading both teams in points (with tie handling set per rule); fit a conditional logit on gap, team scoring concentration and OT; output P(leader) by rank-gap cell with empirical-Bayes shrinkage (prior weight 80 games per cell).
raw_data: Player-game points, minutes, team and opponent identifiers
nba.leader_share_by_usage_rank.why: Anchors the argmax model and shows how fast leader probability decays with expected-points gap.

nba.star_pair_scoring_correlation.label: Correlation of scoring between a team's top scorers and across the two teams
nba.star_pair_scoring_correlation.mechanism: Teammates split a roughly fixed number of shots so a big night for one lowers the other, while both teams share pace and officiating; this sets the covariance structure of the maximum.
nba.star_pair_scoring_correlation.rationale: Leader probability depends on the joint distribution: if two stars were positively correlated, the max would be less spread out than if negatively correlated; both are estimable from box scores.
nba.star_pair_scoring_correlation.measurement: Estimate residual-points correlation (actual minus minutes-conditional expectation) for each team's top-3 scorer pairs and for cross-team top-scorer pairs over 2 seasons using Fisher-z shrinkage to a league pair-type prior (prior weight 40 games); condition on co-star availability. Output a covariance matrix over the candidate set.
nba.star_pair_scoring_correlation.why: Required for the joint distribution that defines the maximum.

nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.label: Ratings-based blowout probability and starter-minutes-vs-margin curve (market-free)
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.mechanism: Rebuilds the blowout risk from team strength and rotation history instead of the closing spread: a ratings-implied expected margin and margin spread give P(large lead), and a coach/player minutes-versus-margin curve converts each margin path into expected minutes lost by starters and gained by bench players.
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.rationale: The catalog input nba.garbage is defined from the closing spread, which is a market price and so a benchmark, not an input. The causal quantity is the chance that the margin passes the coach's pull threshold early enough to matter, and how much playing time each player then loses. Subtle: the loss depends on when the lead arrives (a 20-point lead entering Q4 removes far more starter minutes than one reached with 3 minutes left), on the coach, and on whether the trailing team also pulls starters, so the curve must be conditional on the margin path and not only on the final margin.
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.measurement: Step 1, expected margin: mu = (NetRtg_home_adj - NetRtg_away_adj) * expected_possessions/100 + home_adv, where NetRtg_adj is the as-of-tipoff opponent-adjusted net rating from nba.off_rtg and nba.def_rtg (ridge regression on game point differential, half-life about 25 games, shrunk to the preseason prior with n_prior about 20 games as a placeholder to be fitted), adjusted for the confirmed unavailable players via nba.lineup_adj_rating, home_adv fitted on the last 5 seasons (about 2 points). Step 2, margin spread: sd_margin fitted on 5 seasons of residuals of final margin versus mu (league-wide roughly 12-13 points, to be estimated, with a heavier empirical tail than normal). Step 3: P(final |margin| >= 15/20/25) and P(|lead| >= 15/20 entering Q4) from the empirical residual distribution around mu. Step 4, minutes curve: from play-by-play stints, per team-season, expected minutes of each rotation player conditional on margin entering Q4 in bins (0-9, 10-14, 15-19, 20+), shrunk toward the league curve with k about 30 blowout games. Output per player: expected minutes lost and the probability of falling below a stated minutes level. No closing line or other price is used; the spread is retained only to benchmark calibration of step 3.

nba.ot_prob_ratings_margin.label: Market-free overtime probability and overtime scoring increment from the ratings-implied regulation margin
nba.ot_prob_ratings_margin.mechanism: A game goes to overtime only if the regulation margin is exactly zero, so P(OT) is the mass at zero of the regulation-margin distribution, highest for evenly matched teams; each five-minute overtime then adds scoring at both teams' per-minute rates, and a further overtime follows with the tie probability of a five-minute period.
nba.ot_prob_ratings_margin.rationale: The catalog nba.ot_model conditions P(OT) on the closing-spread bucket (a market quantity) and says one OT adds about 10-12 points to totals, which is the per-team figure, not the combined one. A market-free version takes the regulation-margin distribution from team ratings and sizes OT correctly: roughly 11-13 points per team and 22-26 combined per period, with repeated overtimes possible. Subtle: the zero-margin mass is larger than a continuous normal approximation gives, because end-of-game tactics (holding for the last shot, fouling when ahead by three) cluster regulation margins between 0 and 3.
nba.ot_prob_ratings_margin.measurement: Step 1: regulation-margin mean mu from nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve (opponent-adjusted net ratings x expected possessions/100 + home advantage, as of tipoff, adjusted for confirmed inactives). Step 2: P(regulation tie) = logistic regression of the indicator "regulation margin = 0" on |mu| over the last 5 regular seasons (about 6,000 games; league base rate to be estimated), smoothed across 1-point |mu| bins. Step 3: per-team OT points = league points per team per OT period from play-by-play scaled by the team's opponent-adjusted pace and offensive rating relative to league; combined OT points = sum over both teams. Step 4: P(k-th OT | (k-1)-th OT) = pooled empirical tie rate of five-minute periods with prior weight 200 OT periods. Output P(OT), P(2+ OT), per-team and combined OT-points distributions. Only team ratings, pace and results enter.

nba.ot_prob_ratings_margin.why: Overtime gives the highest-minutes stars five more minutes and can change the points leader; the race-to-N is decided long before OT except for very high N. P(OT) from the ratings-implied regulation margin.

nba.starters_pit.reason: Opening five set the early scoring rates for the race and decide which stars are on the floor first; it is the most valuable late-arriving variable for the race, though the leader market needs full-game minutes more than the opening five.

nba.pace.reason: For race-to-N the relevant quantity is the possession rate of the first eight minutes, not the game pace; the existing definition is a full-game variable and will misrepresent early tempo.

nba.off_rtg.reason: A full-game offensive rating is a weak proxy for the starters' first-stint rating, which is what the race measures; useful only through the opening-stint version.

nba.def_rtg.reason: Same limitation as offensive rating: starter defense in the first stint is the relevant input; full-game values average over bench units.

nba.q_scoring.reason: First-quarter scoring history is the closest existing proxy for the race's early-game scoring rate, but it confounds lineups and opponents; shrink hard.

nba.tip_first_shot.reason: Opening possession matters materially for low N and decays with N; for the race this is a core input but the evidence for team-specific tip-off skill is thin, so the effect should be treated as a league-wide constant with weak team deviations.

nba.usage.reason: Shot shares are the main determinant of who leads the scoring; for the leader contract the usage of the top two scorers in each team and the gap between them is what matters, not the player's average usage.

nba.minutes.reason: The leader is typically the star with the most minutes; the tail of minutes (OT, blowout cuts) separates leaders and is a mixture variable.

nba.garbage.reason: Catalog definition is "blowout probability from spread", a closing-line quantity, so it is a market benchmark and not an input. Removed from stages, coverage, interactions and data feeds; replaced by the market-free nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve built from ratings and rotation history. Prior note: Blowouts reduce the favorite's stars and raise the underdog's relative chances; the existing note is right but built from the spread it uses a market observable instead of ratings.

nba.ot_model.reason: Catalog measurement bins P(OT) by |spread| and total buckets (closing-line quantities), so as defined it is market-derived and a benchmark; it also states OT adds about 10-12 points to totals, which is the per-team figure (combined is about 22-26). Replaced in stages, coverage, interactions, nonlinearities and feeds by the market-free nba.ot_prob_ratings_margin.

nba.teammate_absence_shift.reason: Absence of a co-star concentrates scoring and also removes a competitor for the leader title, an effect that is non-additive and large.

nba.injuries_pit.reason: Inactive players are deemed to score 0 in the leader contract (no void), so the status vintage enters the price multiplicatively and changes the candidate set; needs both teams' statuses.

m.quote_history.reason: A price path is market state, not a determinant of who scores first or most.

m.rules_text.reason: Rules are now sampled for both series: 1/N leader ties, inactive counted as 0 points, team-based single-game race; still primary because OT inclusion and the never-reached-N case are unstated.

m.external_lines.reason: Labelled primary but is the sportsbook price; benchmark for a fundamentals model, not an input.

interactions.mechanism: Race thresholds below 15 depend almost entirely on the identity of the starters and the opening tempo; a starter swap changes the scoring-event mix per possession, and the effect is largest when the replaced player is the primary creator.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare first-passage times to 10 points by starter-change indicator, controlling for opponent and opening possession.

interactions.mechanism: First possession is hypothesised to be worth about half a possession in points (unverified); in a race to 5-10 it is a large share of the total edge but for N of 25 or above it is swamped by rating gap and noise, so the effect shrinks like 1/sqrt(N).
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the opening-possession coefficient separately for each N in the logistic race model and check the decline.

interactions.mechanism: When a co-star sits the top scorer's expected points rise and a rival for the leader title disappears, so the leader probability grows faster than the usage gain alone; the effect on the opposing team's best scorer is the opposite.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare leader share of a star in games with and without his top teammate, holding opponent and minutes.

interactions.mechanism: Overtime favors the highest-minutes stars while blowouts remove the favorite's stars; leader probability therefore switches between a star-dominated regime in close games and a bench-diluted regime in lopsided ones.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate leader share by star team win-probability bin and OT indicator.

interactions.mechanism: Negative same-team correlation in points lowers the chance of both teammates scoring high, so the maximum is often a single outlier; positive cross-team correlation via pace increases both sides' high tails, spreading leader probability across teams.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate max with the observed covariance vs independent marginals and compare to realised leader frequencies.

nonlinearities.shape: convex/softmax-like: leader probability rises faster than expected points gap
nonlinearities.why: The maximum of several heavy-tailed variables gives winner-take-all behavior; a player with a modest expected-points edge over the second option wins disproportionately more often because the field is split among many low-probability candidates.

nonlinearities.shape: decaying like 1/sqrt(N) in the race threshold
nonlinearities.why: First-possession advantage is a roughly constant half possession of points while the standard deviation of the margin at N points grows with N, so the probability edge declines with N.

nonlinearities.shape: piecewise with an OT step and blowout truncation
nonlinearities.why: Stars' minutes jump by about five in OT games and are cut in lopsided games, making leader probability a discontinuous function of projected game closeness.

contract.settlement_definition: Thirty-two team-season series, 31 with rules text. Regular season: win totals (KXNBAWINS: at least N wins), any team to 72+ wins (KXNBAMOSTWINS), breaking the 73-win record (KXNBAWINRECORD, 2025-26 edition: more than 73 wins), more wins than a named rival (KXNBAH2HWINS: equal wins resolve 50/50), worst record (KXNBARECORD: ties by win-loss percentage at 1/N), best winning percentage to the All-Star break (KXNBAPOSTASREC: ties $1/N), six division winners (end-of-regular-season standings, ties by the league's official tiebreak rules, no split), conference 1 seeds at the end of the regular season, seed thresholds on the pre-Play-In seed (KXNBASEEDOU) versus exact seeds with 7 and 8 set by the Play-In (KXNBASEED), Play-In qualification and playoff qualification (Play-In qualification does not count). Postseason: conference-finals qualifiers, conference champions, champion, conference of the champion, exact Finals winner and runner-up (No if either team is eliminated from its role), playoff wins at least N (Play-In wins excluded), any Play-In team reaching the Conference Finals, three-peat, franchise-set champions (ten never-champions; teams without a title in 2018-19 to 2025-26) and the regular-season MVP's team winning the title. Regular-season series exclude preseason, Play-In, playoffs, the All-Star Game and the Cup final; Cup games before the final count. KXNBANEWCHAMP is TITLE_ONLY.

rules_evidence.quote: If the Utah Pro Basketball team wins at least 60 games in the 2026-27 regular season, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Win-total contract counts regular-season wins only with a greater_or_equal strike, so playoffs and the play-in are excluded.

rules_evidence.quote: If multiple teams are tied for the best winning percentage at the start of the All-Star break, “Yes” positions will pay $1/N
rules_evidence.establishes: Partial-season record contract judged on winning percentage (teams have played unequal numbers of games at the break) with ties split 1/N.

rules_evidence.quote: If either team is eliminated from contention for its specified role, the market resolves to No.
rules_evidence.establishes: Exact winner-and-runner-up contract: the joint probability that both named teams reach the Finals and the first beats the second, not a single-team title probability.

rules_evidence.quote: If the 2026-27 regular season Pro Basketball MVP wins the championship in the 2026-27 Pro Basketball season, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Conjunction of an award vote (regular-season MVP) and the title: sum over MVP candidates of P(MVP) x P(his team wins the title | he is MVP).

rules_evidence.quote: Division winners are based on the standings at the end of the regular season.
rules_evidence.establishes: Division winner is a standings outcome with ties broken by the league's tiebreak rules (no 1/N split), so the tiebreak ledger decides boundary cases.

rules_evidence.quote: If San Antonio and Philadelphia record an equal number of wins in the 2026-27 Pro Basketball regular season, then all markets will resolve to 50/50.
rules_evidence.establishes: Head-to-head win-total contract: the difference of two teams' win totals, with the integer tie paid at half, so the tie probability (several percent for close teams) matters.

rules_evidence.quote: If two or more teams are tied for the worst regular-season record based on win-loss percentage, dead-heat rules apply
rules_evidence.establishes: Worst-record contract is a minimum over 30 teams with tanking incentives, ties split 1/N; it needs the bottom tail of the win distribution, not the title side.

rules_evidence.quote: NBA Cup games before the Championship game are part of the regular season.
rules_evidence.establishes: Cup group and knockout games before the final count in regular-season records (read on a contract of this archetype; KXNBAWINS is silent, so applying it to win totals is the league convention, not Kalshi text).

rules_evidence.quote: Results of Play-In games do not affect the outcome.
rules_evidence.establishes: Seed over/under contracts settle on the pre-Play-In conference seed.

rules_evidence.quote: Seeds #7 and #8 are determined by the results of the Western Conference Play-In Tournament.
rules_evidence.establishes: Exact-seed contracts use the post-Play-In seed for 7 and 8, so one simulated table must be mapped through two seed definitions.

rules_evidence.quote: Qualifying for the Pro Basketball play-in tournament does not count as playoff qualification.
rules_evidence.establishes: Teams finishing 7-10 qualify for the playoffs only by winning Play-In games.

rules_evidence.quote: Any wins in the Pro Basketball Play-In Tournament will not be considered.
rules_evidence.establishes: Playoff-win ladders count best-of-seven wins only; a Play-In team's two Play-In wins add nothing.

rules_evidence.quote: win more than 73 games in a single regular season
rules_evidence.establishes: Record-breaking contract needs 74+ wins; 73 ties the record and resolves No.

rules_evidence.quote: Only NBA championships count for the purposes of this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: Franchise-set contract is a sum of title probabilities over the ten listed never-champion franchises; ABA titles are ignored.

variants_and_edge_cases: Three tie rules coexist: 1/N dead heat (KXNBARECORD worst record, KXNBAPOSTASREC best record at the break), 50/50 (KXNBAH2HWINS on equal wins) and the league tiebreak hierarchy with no split (division winners, 1 seeds, seeds); each needs integer-level win distributions, not means.

Two seed definitions: KXNBASEEDOU uses the seed before the Play-In (a 10 seed that enters as the 8 is still 10), KXNBASEED assigns 7 and 8 from the Play-In; KXNBAPLAYIN is qualification for the Play-In (seeds 7-10) and KXNBAPLAYOFF excludes it.

KXNBAWINS and KXNBAMOSTWINS use greater_or_equal integer strikes (no push); KXNBAWINRECORD needs more than 73 wins; KXNBAMOSTWINS is a maximum over 30 teams, so it is the upper tail of the best team, not of one named team.
KXNBAPOSTASREC compares winning percentage at the All-Star break (Feb 19, 2027) when teams have played different numbers of games; ties split 1/N.
KXNBAMVPCHAMP couples the regular-season MVP vote with the title, and the dependence is strong because voters reward team success; it is not a Finals MVP contract.

Franchise-set contracts (KXNBAFIRSTTIMECHAMP, KXNBANEWCHAMPION) are sums of title probabilities over fixed lists; KXNBANEWCHAMPION lists New York as 2025-26 champion, which also means the Oklahoma City three-peat (KXNBA3PEAT, 2024-25 to 2026-27) can no longer occur.

Several sampled tickers refer to completed seasons (KXNBAWINRECORD 2025-26, KXNBAPLAYOFFWINS and KXNBAPIADVANCE for the 2026 playoffs); the mechanism is the same for the 2026-27 editions but strikes and lists must be read per edition.

Playoff-win ladders exclude Play-In wins; KXNBAPIADVANCE asks whether any Play-In team reaches the Conference Finals; of the eight Play-In entrants only the four that win through (the 7 and 8 seeds, two per conference) can, so it is a union over the bracket paths of those 7 and 8 seeds.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official league standings, tiebreak procedure, Play-In and playoff results, and league announcements for the champion and regular-season MVP; the sampled texts name no source agency.

mechanism.summary: Season-level team contracts are functionals of a simulated season: a latent team strength (a prior from the roster plus in-season updates, with real uncertainty), the realized availability of its stars over the games and into the playoffs, the remaining schedule with home/away and rest, game results as correlated Bernoulli trials giving a Poisson-binomial win total, standings with official tiebreakers, two seed definitions around the Play-In, and then a playoff bracket of best-of-seven series with tightened rotations. Probabilities of rare outcomes (title, 72 wins, a Play-In team in the Conference Finals) are convex in uncertainty: errors in rating sd and star health matter more than error in the mean, and boundary effects at tiebreaks, seed cut points and the 1/N or 50/50 tie rules drive seed, division and record contracts. The MVP-champion conjunction and franchise-set champion contracts add functionals (a vote correlated with team success, sums over fixed franchise lists) on top of the bracket.

stages.name: Latent team strength: prior and in-season update
stages.description: True strength before the season is a roster-based prior (minutes-weighted player impact, aging, continuity, rookies), with an error sd of roughly 3-4 net rating points. Each game updates it with a gain that declines with games played; with ten games played the prior still dominates. Trades and coaching changes shift both mean and variance with a lag for integration.
stages.distribution: Gaussian posterior with sd about 2.5-3.5 net rating points early in the season shrinking with games; heavy tail for roster shocks (trades, injuries to stars).

stages.name: Availability of stars over the season and into the playoffs
stages.description: Stars miss a random number of games through injury and load management, with a heavy right tail of long absences; the quantity that matters differs by contract: expected games missed for win totals and seeds, probability of being healthy in April-June for round-reach and titles. Availability changes the team rating by a player-specific amount.
stages.distribution: Mixture: most players miss 5-15 games, a few percent miss most of the season; time-to-injury is a survival process with age and workload dependence.

stages.name: Schedule: opponent strength, rest and Cup games in the regular season
stages.description: The remaining schedule determines each game's win probability through opponent strength, home/away and rest asymmetry. Cup group and knockout games before the Cup final count as regular-season games (KXNBAPOSTASREC text) and teams eliminated early receive filler games scheduled later, so part of the schedule is unknown in November. Early in the season schedule effects are small next to rating uncertainty, but they matter for division races, 1 seeds and the final-weeks seed battle.
stages.distribution: Deterministic schedule given; game win probabilities range 15-85%; the rest/travel adjustments are about +/-1 point of margin.

stages.name: Regular-season win totals, extremes and pairwise records
stages.description: The win total is a sum of correlated game outcomes: independent Bernoulli noise (sd about 4.5 wins for an average team) plus common shocks through rating uncertainty and injuries, so the distribution is wider than a binomial. KXNBAMOSTWINS and KXNBAWINRECORD are upper-tail events of the best team (72+ or 74+ wins), KXNBARECORD is the minimum over 30 teams where lottery incentives make weak teams rest veterans late, KXNBAPOSTASREC is a maximum of partial-season percentages, and KXNBAH2HWINS is a difference of two totals linked by their head-to-head games, with the equal-wins mass paid at half.
stages.distribution: Poisson-binomial with a hierarchical shock (total sd about 6-7 wins); extreme-value behaviour for maxima and minima over 30 teams; integer ties paid 1/N or 50/50.

stages.name: Division titles, seeding, Play-In and playoff qualification
stages.description: Six division winners, conference 1 seeds and seed contracts are ranks of simulated records resolved by the official tiebreak hierarchy (head-to-head, division and conference records). Seeds 7-10 enter the Play-In (KXNBAPLAYIN), whose bracket decides playoff qualification (KXNBAPLAYOFF) and the exact 7 and 8 seeds (KXNBASEED), while KXNBASEEDOU stays on the pre-Play-In seed. Boundary probabilities hinge on one win and on the tiebreak ledger, and division titles carry no seeding reward, so late-season resting follows the conference table.
stages.distribution: Discrete rank outcomes with deterministic tiebreaks; the Play-In adds a three-game mini-bracket with per-game probabilities near 50% that maps seeds 7-10 to 7, 8 or out.

stages.name: Playoff bracket and series conversion
stages.description: Each series is a best-of-seven with home-court structure, playoff-tightened rotations and game-to-game correlation; per-game win probability converts steeply to series probability. The bracket path and star health in each round give conference-finals qualification, conference and league titles, the exact Finals pair, the playoff-win count (sum of wins over series reached, Play-In excluded) and whether a Play-In entrant reaches the Conference Finals; all are strongly convex in team strength.
stages.distribution: Series win probability is an S-shaped function of per-game edge (60% per game gives about 71% series); correlation between games from injuries and adjustments widens outcomes.

stages.name: Derived award and franchise-set functionals
stages.description: Two contract families sit on top of the bracket. The MVP-champion conjunction needs the regular-season MVP vote (a conditional choice among a few candidates whose odds rise with team record) joined to that player's team title probability, including his playoff health. Franchise-set contracts (first-time champion, no title in eight seasons, the three-peat) are sums or single terms of title probabilities over fixed lists, so their errors are the correlated errors of those teams' strength estimates.
stages.distribution: Conditional logit over MVP candidates joined to a title probability (strong positive dependence); sums of correlated team title probabilities for franchise sets.

talent_strength.note: Latent strength with prior, aging and update gain.

opponent_matchup.note: Bracket path and matchup-specific series results.

role_personnel.note: Who plays and how playoff rotations concentrate minutes.

coaching_scheme.note: Coaching changes and playoff rotation tightening; only weakly quantified.

environment.note: Venue, altitude and arena effects are small at the season-aggregate level and are absorbed in home/away win probabilities within the schedule; no separate environment variable is warranted for futures.

game_context_script.note: Close-game luck and series dynamics (game-to-game correlation).

pace_volume.note: Possession count has no direct role at the season-futures level; it enters only through net rating, which already includes pace effects, so no separate pace or volume input is needed.

efficiency_conversion.note: Luck versus skill in point differential and records.

distribution_variance.note: Win-total, extreme-record and series distributions with rating uncertainty and head-to-head linkage.

officiating_rules.note: Format rules: tiebreak hierarchy, Play-In bracket and Cup games counted in the regular season.

settlement_contract.note: Per-series forms: integer win strikes, 1/N and 50/50 tie rules, tiebreak-decided divisions and seeds, pre- versus post-Play-In seeds, Play-In wins excluded, exact Finals pair, franchise lists and the MVP-title conjunction.

nba.preseason_roster_aging_prior.label: Preseason team prior from minutes-weighted roster impact with aging curves and continuity
nba.preseason_roster_aging_prior.mechanism: A team's true strength before and early in the season is a function of who is on the roster, how those players age, and how much of last year's unit returns; this prior dominates for the first 20-30 games.
nba.preseason_roster_aging_prior.rationale: With about ten games played, the 2026-27 rating is mostly the prior; building it from last season's team rating ignores offseason roster churn, aging and rookie contributions, and the error of the prior sets the uncertainty of every futures contract.
nba.preseason_roster_aging_prior.measurement: Player projection = 0.6 x impact(last season) + 0.3 x impact(season-1) + 0.1 x impact(season-2), each impact term shrunk to a minutes-based prior with k=1500 minutes (use nba.player_impact), plus age adjustment delta(age) estimated from year-over-year change by age bucket on 15 seasons (fit, not fixed at +1.0/-0.3/-1.0), plus rookie/new-signing prior by draft slot. Team prior = sum over projected rotation of expected minutes share x projection + continuity adjustment b x (minutes-weighted share of last season's minutes returning), with b estimated by backtest on 10 seasons, then shrunk to the league mean by the backtested prior-error variance (report mean and sd). As-of: before opening night and after each roster transaction, using only information dated before the as-of time.
free_sources: EPM / RAPM published by Dunks&Threes or similar
raw_data: team rosters and transactions with dates
nba.preseason_roster_aging_prior.why: Provides the quantified prior and its sd, which the existing rating input only asserts.

nba.rating_update_gain.label: In-season rating update gain and posterior sd (how fast current results override the prior)
nba.rating_update_gain.mechanism: True team strength is updated game by game with weight given by signal-to-noise; the gain declines with games played, and calibrating it by backtest sets how fast futures should move.
nba.rating_update_gain.rationale: A rating that overweights early results (10 games) swings futures; under-weighting leaves stale priors. The right gain is estimated from past seasons and depends on whether margin or win/loss is used and on roster stability.
nba.rating_update_gain.measurement: Backtest across the last 15 seasons: regress end-of-season margin per game on preseason prior and games-played-weighted current margin; solve for optimal weight w(n) as a function of games played n (expect w near 0.2 at n=10, 0.5 at n=40); posterior sd of true rating = sqrt(prior_var x (1-w)); use margin of victory capped at 15 and garbage-time excluded. As-of: all games before the as-of date.
raw_data: team-game margins, possessions, rosters by game (15 seasons)
nba.rating_update_gain.why: Converts the generic 'rating with uncertainty' into time-varying numbers for every season-level contract.

nba.tiebreak_ledger.label: Head-to-head, division and conference record ledger for tiebreaker evaluation
nba.tiebreak_ledger.mechanism: Seeds and division winners are decided by the league's tiebreak hierarchy (head-to-head, division winner, conference record and so on), so exact ties are resolved by information that accumulates over the season.
nba.tiebreak_ledger.rationale: Simulating only win totals misses the probability that a tie is broken in a team's favor; at seed boundaries (6th vs 7th, 10th vs 11th, play-in cutoff) a tie occurs in about 8-15% of final standings and the tiebreak ledger is partly known before the season ends.
nba.tiebreak_ledger.measurement: For each team pair keep season-to-date head-to-head, division and conference records, record vs playoff-eligible teams in each conference, and net points, updated nightly. In the simulation apply the league order (NBA.com standings page): two-team ties - head-to-head, division leader over non-leader, division record (same division only), conference record, record vs playoff-eligible own-conference teams, record vs playoff-eligible other-conference teams, net points; three or more teams - division leader, head-to-head winning percentage among all tied teams, division record (all same division), conference record, record vs playoff-eligible own-conference teams, net points (no other-conference step). Whether a reduced multi-team tie re-enters the two-team procedure is not confirmed: compute both variants and report the difference, and re-read the 2026-27 standings page text. Output P(win tie) per pair and seed. As-of: nightly after final scores.
raw_data: game results by team pair, schedule
nba.tiebreak_ledger.why: Decides the six division winners, conference 1 seeds and seed contracts whenever simulated records tie at a boundary.

nba.playoff_star_health_hazard.label: Time-resolved probability that each rotation star is healthy for each playoff round
nba.playoff_star_health_hazard.mechanism: Title and conference odds are convex in star availability, and the relevant availability is in April-June, not the regular-season games-missed average.
nba.playoff_star_health_hazard.rationale: Games-missed expectations average over a season; the quantity that matters for round-reach contracts is the probability of being healthy at tip of each playoff series, which depends on current injury state, history, age and minutes load.
nba.playoff_star_health_hazard.measurement: For each player in the top-3 of each contender (by minutes x impact) fit a discrete-time hazard (logistic per game) for the event 'misses the next game with an injury-coded absence' on 10 seasons of regular-season and playoff data, covariates: age, prior-season games missed, minutes per game, current report status (none/probable/questionable/doubtful/out) from the as-of vintage, days since last injury absence. Output P(available at game 1 of the playoffs) and P(available for the first game of round k | available at the start) by chaining per-game survival over the expected playoff games, plus the expected strength loss = impact x minutes share. Shrink player-specific intercepts to the age bucket mean with k=40 games. As-of: latest injury report vintage; never use post-hoc game logs for the current state.
raw_data: injury report vintages (official report 2021-22 onward, Pro Sports Transactions earlier)
player age, minutes, games missed by season
nba.playoff_star_health_hazard.why: Converts star health into a probability mixture for the series simulation, which is what makes title odds convex. Role lowered to secondary: the 10-season injury history it needs is not available as a clean public dataset (sf-injury-data), so its reliability is unproven.

nba.award_vote_and_cowinner_model.label: Voting-panel and nominee model for award contracts, including the probability of multiple co-winners
nba.award_vote_and_cowinner_model.mechanism: Award contracts such as the Social Justice Champion, Finals MVP, conference finals MVP and Cup All-Tournament selections are decided by a panel or vote among nominees, not by team simulation, so the relevant quantities are the nominee set, the historical winner profile and the chance of several winners.
nba.award_vote_and_cowinner_model.rationale: For KXNBASJC the sampled rules split the payout $1/N among multiple awardees, so P(multiple winners) and the winner's profile (community work and nominee status) matter more than basketball production. For Finals and conference finals MVPs the winner is chosen from the winning team after the series by a panel, so the team simulation only gives the first factor. Panels are small, so narrative and series stats can dominate and the winner is a discrete choice among a few candidates.
nba.award_vote_and_cowinner_model.measurement: Build an award history table (at least 15 seasons) of nominees or finalists, winner(s) and the number of awardees. Fit a conditional logit for P(winner | nominee) on prior finalist or winner status, team success, and for series MVPs on series points rank and best-player indicator, with ridge regularisation and a prior weight of 10 award-years. Estimate P(more than one awardee) as the historical frequency with a beta(1,10) prior, and the expected payout as P(win) x E[1/N | win] rounded down to the cent. For game-based MVPs multiply by P(team wins the series) from nba.series_model. As-of: before announcement, updated when finalists are published.
free_sources: NBA.com award announcements and press releases
raw_data: Winners and number of awardees by year
nba.award_vote_and_cowinner_model.why: KXNBAMVPCHAMP needs P(player is regular-season MVP) jointly with his team's title probability, and the Cup All-Tournament series is a panel selection; this is the only vote model in the archetype after the award series moved to awards_draft.

nba.standings_motivation.label: Standings, clinch/tank incentives and late-season motivation
nba.standings_motivation.mechanism: Teams out of contention or with locked seeds rest stars or play young players, changing availability and minutes distribution late in the season.
nba.standings_motivation.rationale: Late-season and post-clinch games show elevated load management and unpredictable rotations, making both sides and player props noisier and shifting minutes to bench players. Subtle: announcements arrive late (game-day), and tanking incentives (lottery odds) differ from effort incentives; play-in positioning and in-season Cup stakes alter incentives too.
nba.standings_motivation.measurement: For each team-game compute leverage = E[|change in seed-weighted value|] from nba.standings_sim: V = sum over seeds of P(seed) x value(seed) with value(seed) = P(series win) for playoff seeds and lottery odds term for non-playoff; leverage = V(win) - V(loss) from the simulation conditional on the game outcome. Flags: clinched seed, eliminated, and games remaining. Estimate the effect of leverage and clinch flags on starter minutes and rest probability by regression on 5 seasons of late-season games (April/final 15 games), interacting with age and minutes load, with ridge shrinkage. As-of: after the previous game's final score.
raw_data: historical late-season minutes and rest patterns
nba.standings_motivation.why: KXNBARECORD (worst record, rules-verified) depends on tanking and late-season rest by lottery-bound teams, which pulls their win probabilities below rating-implied values.

nba.play_in_path_model.label: Play-in bracket path probabilities given pre-play-in seed and relative strength
nba.play_in_path_model.mechanism: The play-in tournament maps seeds 7-10 to final seeds 7 and 8 through a fixed bracket, so the playoff qualification and the post-play-in seed differ from the regular-season seed; Kalshi's seed contracts are measured before the play-in.
nba.play_in_path_model.rationale: KXNBASEEDOU resolves on the regular-season seed before the play-in while qualification/play-in series depend on play-in outcomes; the same team has different probabilities for 'seed 8 or better' depending on which definition applies.
nba.play_in_path_model.measurement: Encode the bracket (7v8 winner gets the 7 seed; 9v10 loser is out; loser of 7v8 plays winner of 9v10 for the 8 seed), compute per-game win probabilities with home-court from team ratings and rest, and convolve to P(final seed 7, 8, out | pre-play-in seed, opponents); estimate the distribution of opponents from the standings simulation. As-of: nightly; rules versioned by season.
raw_data: Standings and seeds before the Play-In
nba.play_in_path_model.why: Maps seeds 7-10 into playoff qualification and exact 7/8 seeds for KXNBAPLAYOFF, KXNBASEED and KXNBAPIADVANCE; KXNBAPLAYIN and KXNBASEEDOU stop before it.

nba.team_record_head_to_head_linkage.label: Dependence between teams' records via head-to-head games and conference schedule overlap
nba.team_record_head_to_head_linkage.mechanism: Records of contending teams are not independent: when two top teams play each other, one gains what the other loses, and shared opponents create correlation in schedule luck.
nba.team_record_head_to_head_linkage.rationale: Best-record and most-wins markets are about the maximum over teams, so the covariance of wins across teams matters; ignoring head-to-head linkage and common opponents misstates the extreme's distribution.
nba.team_record_head_to_head_linkage.measurement: From the remaining schedule compute pairwise numbers of head-to-head games and common-opponent overlap; in the simulation draw correlated team-strength shocks and enforce zero-sum head-to-head results; estimate the covariance of final win totals across the top-8 contenders by simulation; output distribution of the maximum and the probability of ties (tie handling per rule). As-of: nightly.
nba.team_record_head_to_head_linkage.why: KXNBAH2HWINS, division races and the extreme-record contracts depend on how head-to-head games make two teams' totals negatively dependent.

nba.series_length_distribution.label: Series-length distribution from per-game win probabilities
nba.series_length_distribution.mechanism: The number of games in a best-of-seven series is a function of per-game win probability, home pattern and dependence between games; this is the per-series kernel that nba.title_path calls inside each bracket draw.
nba.series_length_distribution.rationale: KXNBASERIESGAMES counts games, not points; the draft has no input for it except a generic series model reference outside the archetype.
nba.series_length_distribution.measurement: Per-series kernel: P(series ends in k games) by dynamic programming over home pattern 2-2-1-1-1 with per-game win probabilities from own-model playoff ratings and a series dependence parameter (game-to-game correlation about +0.05 on margin, estimated from 2000-2025 playoff series), injuries as of the as-of date; output P(4..7) and P(win). For a set matchup this is used directly; for bracket-level contracts the same kernel is evaluated inside nba.title_path draws, so lengths and advancement are consistent across archetypes.
raw_data: playoff series results by game with venue
own team ratings and injury status
nba.series_length_distribution.why: Playoff-win ladders (KXNBAPLAYOFFWINS) count wins across series, which depend on series lengths, not only on advancement.

nba.ratings.reason: Team rating is the backbone of every futures contract; the existing text promises a preseason prior and uncertainty but gives no way to compute either, and in-season updating weights are unspecified.

nba.lineup_adj_rating.reason: Availability-adjusted strength is what projects the rest of the season; for futures it must be integrated over the distribution of who plays, not evaluated at tonight's active set.

nba.player_impact.reason: Player-level impact values are the way to project a team after trades and injuries; subject to aging and role-change error, and noisy for rookies and new acquisitions.

nba.standings_sim.reason: The simulation is the actual evaluator for win totals, seeds, play-in and round reach; value depends on the tiebreaker implementation and on drawing correlated rating shocks across teams. Note: this is a model component, not a raw input; it consumes nba.ratings (with rating uncertainty), nba.rating_update_gain, nba.sos_remaining, nba.rest_travel and nba.tiebreak_ledger, which are listed separately and fed by the game-results and schedule datasets.

nba.sos_remaining.reason: Remaining schedule strength matters for win-total and seed markets mid-season; early in a season (about ten games played) it is a minor effect compared with rating uncertainty.

nba.pythag_residual.reason: Wins above point-differential expectation partly regress; but clutch luck is mostly noise so the weight on it should be small and estimated from backtests.

nba.injury_risk_season.reason: Star availability distribution drives title convexity; but it needs to be time-resolved (probability healthy in April) not just games-missed expectation.

nba.load_mgmt.reason: Rest policy for stars lowers regular-season wins in a known way; matters for win-total and seed markets but not for playoff-only contracts.

nba.title_path.reason: Bracket path and home-court structure matter for round-reach and title; modest compared with team strength except for specific matchups.

nba.series_model.reason: Best-of-seven conversion of per-game probability to series result is central to all playoff round markets and is strongly non-linear in the per-game edge. Note: this is a model component, not a raw input; it consumes nba.ratings (with rating uncertainty), nba.rating_update_gain, nba.sos_remaining, nba.rest_travel and nba.tiebreak_ledger, which are listed separately and fed by the game-results and schedule datasets.

nba.playoff_rotation.reason: Playoff minute concentration raises star-heavy teams' strength relative to regular-season ratings; effect size is modest (a few percent of net rating) but systematic.

nba.news.reason: Trades and coaching changes are event signals that move rating and uncertainty with a lag; useful as triggers, but the quantity needed is a re-estimate of rating, which is player-impact driven.

nba.rest_travel.reason: Rest and travel effects are tiny at the season-aggregate level and are already in schedule-aware ratings; including them as a season-futures input mostly double counts.

nba.cup_format.reason: The Cup champion contract left for series_and_cup; here the Cup matters only because games before the Cup final count in regular-season records (KXNBAPOSTASREC text) and add filler games to the schedule.

m.quote_history.reason: Futures price path measures information arrival and staleness; a market series, not a team-strength driver.

m.rules_text.reason: Rules differ across the 23 series: regular-season-only windows with Cup games counted, 1/N ties for streak and All-Star-break record, tiebreak-decided division, exact Finals pairing and franchise lists; 19 have rules text, including 50/50 head-to-head ties and 1/N worst-record dead heats.

m.external_lines.reason: De-vigged sportsbook futures are the consensus benchmark; including them as an input would reproduce the market.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Coherence across win-total and seed rungs is a quote-quality check; a simulation's own ladder is monotone.

m.orderbook_depth.reason: Depth limits tradable size on thin futures books; execution realism only.

m.strike_hit_rates.reason: With one season per label the realised hit-rate history is too thin to calibrate rare events, and it is a label set not a driver.

m.fees.reason: Fee schedule and capital lockup affect expected return of long-dated positions, not the probability of the event.

nba.market_calibration_bias.reason: Favorite-longshot bias in the Kalshi futures book is an overlay on model probabilities; it is not an input to team strength.

nba.finals_viewership_drivers.reason: Built for KXNBAFINALSVIEWER and KXNBAFINALSVIEWERGAME7, which the reconciliation classified OUT_OF_SCOPE (audience_viewership); no remaining series in this archetype settles on audience, so it is removed from stage s7 and the awards dataset feed.

nba.finals_mvp_given_title_share.reason: Built for Finals and conference-finals MVP series, which the reconciliation moved to awards_draft; the remaining KXNBAMVPCHAMP concerns the regular-season MVP, which needs the MVP vote model, not a Finals-MVP share, so it is removed from stages, coverage and feeds.

nba.longest_streak_max_and_tie_model.reason: Built for KXNBATEAMWINSTREAK, which the reconciliation moved to season_stat_markets (defined there); no streak contract remains in this archetype, and KXNBAMOSTWINS is a maximum of win totals, not of run lengths.

interactions.mechanism: Title and conference probability are convex in team strength and in star availability: a healthy-star scenario multiplies title odds several-fold while the injured scenario nearly eliminates it, so the correct estimate is a mixture over star-health states, not the rating at the mean health.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare title probability from a mixture over star-health states with that from average rating; check calibration on historical contenders.

interactions.mechanism: Seed and division contracts flip at exact ties; teams within one win of a cutoff have probabilities controlled by the tiebreak ledger (head-to-head, division record), which is a discontinuous rule on top of continuous win totals.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute the share of simulated seed outcomes decided by tiebreakers and the sensitivity to head-to-head ledger perturbations.

interactions.mechanism: Early in the season the posterior is dominated by the prior; as games accumulate the weight shifts to results. The optimal weighting depends on roster continuity: teams with many new players update faster because the prior is less reliable.
interactions.how_to_test: Backtest end-of-season margin against prior and current margin separately for high- and low-continuity teams.

interactions.mechanism: Playoff rotation tightening raises star-heavy teams' strength in exactly the games that decide titles, so the bracket path matters differently for deep teams versus top-heavy ones; a bracket in which a deep team faces a star team early changes round probabilities beyond the rating difference.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate playoff net rating minus regular-season net rating by roster concentration and test its interaction with opponent type.

interactions.mechanism: A trade changes team strength and uncertainty with a lag of 10-20 games because the integration of a new player lowers early effectiveness; the rating update should widen variance at the time of the trade and then narrow.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare team net rating in games 1-10 versus 11-30 after a major trade relative to the player-impact prediction.

interactions.mechanism: Once a team is out of Play-In contention its incentive flips toward lottery position, and its late-season win probability drops below the rating-implied value; the worst-record contract is decided in this regime, so simulating the last 15-20 games with regular-season ratings overstates the weakest teams' wins.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare rating-implied and realised win rates over the last 20 games for teams eliminated from Play-In contention, over 10 seasons.

interactions.mechanism: Playoff qualification is near-certain for seeds 1-6, roughly 55-75% for seeds 7-8 and 20-35% for seeds 9-10 through the Play-In, and zero below; P(KXNBAPLAYOFF) is therefore a piecewise function of the simulated seed distribution with jumps at 6/7 and 10/11, while KXNBAPLAYIN is an indicator of seeds 7-10.
interactions.how_to_test: Tabulate realised qualification by pre-Play-In seed since the Play-In began and compare with simulated piecewise probabilities.

interactions.mechanism: Two teams that meet three or four times have negatively dependent win totals, which raises the variance of their difference and lowers the chance of equal wins relative to independent draws; KXNBAH2HWINS and division titles both sit on that difference.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare simulated equal-wins frequency for pairs with 4 versus 2 meetings against historical pairs over 10 seasons.

nonlinearities.shape: steep S-shape: series win probability versus per-game win probability
nonlinearities.why: Per-game probability of 55% gives about 61% series, 60% gives about 71% and 65% gives about 80%, so small rating differences are amplified by the best-of-seven structure.

nonlinearities.shape: logistic around threshold-like contracts: P(60+ wins) as a function of mean wins
nonlinearities.why: With a win-total sd of about 6-7 the probability of reaching 60 moves from about 5% at 52 expected wins to 50% at 60 wins, and the slope is largest near the strike.

nonlinearities.shape: convex/mixture: title odds jump discretely when the star is healthy in the playoffs
nonlinearities.why: Title probability is not linear in expected games missed; it depends on a bimodal health state at playoff time, and losing the top star removes most title chance for a top-heavy team.

unresolved.what_would_resolve: Read the league's 2026-27 Cup and schedule-completion rules and version the remaining schedule when filler games are announced.
