unresolved.description: Division, 1-seed and seed contracts defer to 'the governing league's official tie-breaking rules' without listing them; the 2026-27 two-team and multi-team order is assumed from past seasons. Five division contracts arrived from the unregistered record, which modelled them with nba.division_race_tiebreak_state, a duplicate of nba.tiebreak_ledger used here.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Code the league's 2026-27 tiebreak document into nba.tiebreak_ledger, test on past tied divisions and mark nba.division_race_tiebreak_state DUPLICATE_OF it in the catalog.

unresolved.description: KXNBAEAST1SEED/KXNBAWEST1SEED and KXNBASEEDOU state no tie rule of their own (division texts explicitly defer to league tiebreaks); the record assumes the official seed after tiebreaks, and KXNBAPLAYOFFWINS states no treatment of a series not completed.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Confirm on a settled seed market from a season with a tie at the boundary that the official tiebroken seed was used.

contract.settlement_definition: Twelve 2026-27 regular-season series are filed here, ten with sampled rules. Player forms: per-game average at or above a strike (KXNBASTATAVG: no qualification minimum, zero games played means an average of zero, rounded figure from the Source Agencies), at least one made three in the season (KXNBAONE3PT), a single game at or above a points threshold including overtime (KXNBAPLAYERHIGHSCORE), the first player to a 50-point game (KXNBAFIRST50PTS: same-day firsts split $1/N), and league leader in total plus/minus (KXNBASTATLEADER: traded players' totals combined, ties $1/N). League-wide forms: any game with 325+ combined points including overtime (KXNBAGAMEHIGHSCORE), any player with 15+ steals plus blocks in a game (KXNBAGAMESPECIALS), any team with a 20+ game win streak (KXNBAWINSTREAK), the team with the longest win streak with ties paid $1/N (KXNBATEAMWINSTREAK) and the last undefeated team by calendar day of first loss with same-day ties $1/N (KXNBALASTTOLOSE). All count only regular-season games: preseason, Play-In, playoffs, the All-Star Game and the Cup final are excluded and Cup games before the final count. KXNBAHIGHESTSCORING and KXNBAPLAYERSPECIALS are TITLE_ONLY.

rules_evidence.quote: League minimum qualification thresholds do not apply.
rules_evidence.establishes: No games-played cliff for the average contract: a player with a few games can clear the strike, so availability enters smoothly through the denominator.

rules_evidence.quote: If two or more players record the first 50+ point game of the 2026-27 Pro Basketball regular season on the same day
rules_evidence.establishes: First-to-50 is a calendar-day race across all players with same-day ties split 1/N, not a per-player season probability.

rules_evidence.quote: If a player is traded or otherwise plays for more than one team during the season, his statistics from all teams are combined.
rules_evidence.establishes: Leader totals sum across teams after a trade, so a mid-season move changes the on-court margin rate but not eligibility.

rules_evidence.quote: If there is a game (including overtime) with at least 325 total points scored in the 2026-27 Pro Basketball regular season, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: League-wide union over all regular-season games of an extreme combined total with overtime points counted, so OT periods are part of the tail.

rules_evidence.quote: NBA Cup games before the Championship game are part of the regular season and do count towards a winning streak.
rules_evidence.establishes: Cup group and knockout games count in streaks; only the Cup final and postseason are excluded.

rules_evidence.quote: measured by the day of their first loss (not exact time)
rules_evidence.establishes: Last-undefeated is judged by calendar day, so same-day first losses are ties paid 1/N.

rules_evidence.quote: Only a made three-pointer in regular season games count.
rules_evidence.establishes: A season-long first-event contract on a low-volume shooter: the probability of at least one make over his regular-season attempts.

rules_evidence.quote: If any player records 15+ steals and blocks combined in any individual game during the 2026-27 Pro Basketball regular season, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: League-wide union over player-games of an extreme defensive count; the per-game tail, not the mean, sets the price.

rules_evidence.quote: If Victor Wembanyama scores at least 54 points in any game (including overtime)
rules_evidence.establishes: Single-game threshold in any regular-season game with overtime points counted; resolves YES as soon as it happens.

rules_evidence.quote: If multiple teams are tied for the longest consecutive winning streak, “Yes” positions will pay $1/N (rounded down to the nearest cent), where N is the number of tied teams
rules_evidence.establishes: Longest-streak contract is an argmax over 30 teams' maximal run lengths with ties split 1/N, so the number of teams sharing the maximum must be modelled.

variants_and_edge_cases: No qualification cliff where rules are sampled: KXNBASTATAVG waives league minimums and sets a zero average for zero games, and KXNBASTATLEADER (total plus/minus, a counting total) has no minimum; a games-played cliff applies only to a leader contract with a minimum rule, none of which is sampled.

Ties: KXNBAFIRST50PTS (same calendar day of tip-off), KXNBALASTTOLOSE (same day of first loss) and KXNBASTATLEADER split $1/N; the average contract has no tie but resolves on the rounded published figure, so the effective strike is strike minus half a rounding unit.

Overtime is explicitly counted for KXNBAPLAYERHIGHSCORE and KXNBAGAMEHIGHSCORE, and a 325-point game almost always needs overtime, so the number of OT periods is part of the event; KXNBAGAMESPECIALS' secondary text notes that quarter-specific markets in that series exclude overtime.
Regular-season only, with Cup games before the final counted (stated for every sampled series); streaks span Cup knockout games but not the Cup final, and the Play-In is excluded.

Streak contracts with live series are team win streaks (KXNBAWINSTREAK, any team reaching 20) and the last undefeated team; no player consecutive-game series exists, so the player threshold-streak input is context only. KXNBATEAMWINSTREAK (longest team win streak) is filed here: ties are paid $1/N per the settlement text above, and its window follows the regular-season-only, Cup-knockout-games-counted convention stated for the other series in this archetype (its own sampled rules text is not separately stored, so its tie and window details are PARTIALLY_VERIFIED).
contract.settlement_data_source: Official league statistics via the 'Source Agencies' named in the full rules (not named in the sample); plus/minus and average figures as published, with the rounding procedure for averages unverified.

mechanism.summary: Season stat markets are long-horizon functionals of game-level production, decided by three layers: (1) how many games each candidate plays (injury, load management), which under the sampled rules scales totals and the number of chances smoothly rather than through a qualification cliff; (2) the per-game rate or per-game tail (minutes, usage, role, team margin), shrunk toward a preseason projection; and (3) the aggregation form: a rounded average, a leader maximum over correlated totals (plus/minus is mostly team margin times minutes), a first-passage race across players by calendar day, a union over the whole schedule of rare single-game events (54 points, 325 combined points with overtime, 15 stocks), team run lengths (any 20-game streak) or a survival race (last undefeated). Settlement details such as 1/N calendar-day ties, OT inclusion and rounding change the functional.

stages.name: Games played and qualification
stages.description: The number of games a candidate plays is a random variable with heavy mass near the full schedule and a left tail from injuries and load management. In the sampled contracts it acts smoothly: the average has no minimum and zero games gives zero, totals such as plus/minus and the chance of a 54-point or first-to-50 game scale with games played, and a low-volume shooter's chance of one made three grows with his games. Rest decisions concentrate in the second half for older stars.
stages.distribution: Mixture: most rotation players play 65-78 of 82 games with a long left tail; hazard rising with age and prior absences; no cliff under the sampled rules.

stages.name: Per-game rate trajectory
stages.description: A player's true per-game rate is a function of minutes, role, usage and age, which evolves through the season with teammates' availability and coaching decisions. Observed averages to date are noisy estimates of the true rate; shrinkage toward a preseason projection prevents overreaction to early results.
stages.distribution: Gaussian posterior for the true rate with sd shrinking with games played; role shocks (injuries to teammates) produce jumps.

stages.name: Aggregation into averages and leader races
stages.description: A season average has sampling variance falling with games played, and resolves on the rounded published figure, so the effective strike sits half a rounding unit below the stated one. A leader contract is the maximum over candidates whose totals are correlated: for total plus/minus, teammates share the same team margin and differ mainly in minutes, so the leader is set by team strength times durability rather than individual rate.
stages.distribution: Average: Gaussian-like posterior with a step at the rounding boundary; plus/minus leader: maximum over correlated totals with strong within-team dependence; ties 1/N.

stages.name: Streak and run-length processes
stages.description: The live streak contracts are team-level. Any-team-reaches-20 is a union over teams and over 20-game windows of products of game win probabilities, dominated by the strongest healthy teams and by stretches of weak opponents; the last undefeated team is a survival race by calendar day, decided within the first two weeks, with same-day losses tied. Run lengths across 30 teams and the tied count come from the same game-level simulation; the player threshold-streak input is retained only as a hypothesis with no live series.
stages.distribution: Run-length extremes over teams (right tail driven by rating uncertainty and star health); first-loss dates nearly geometric per team with heterogeneous win probabilities.

stages.name: Season simulation backbone for team run-length contracts
stages.description: The three team contracts here (any 20-game streak, the longest streak with 1/N ties, the last undefeated team) are read off one simulated regular season: game win probabilities from team strength with common rating shocks, head-to-head games that make one team's win another's loss, and Cup games before the final included in the sequence. Run lengths, the number of teams tied at the maximum and first-loss dates all come from the same paths, so they must be drawn jointly rather than from separate marginal models.
stages.distribution: Thirty correlated game-outcome sequences; extreme-value behaviour of the maximal run length with integer ties; first-loss day is discrete with same-day ties.

stages.name: League-wide extreme single-game events and first-passage races
stages.description: Several contracts are unions over the remaining schedule of rare single-game events: a named star's 54-point game, the first 50-point game by anyone, a 325-point combined game and a 15-stocks player game. Each per-game probability lives in the tail (hot shooting plus heavy minutes, overtime periods, unusual pace), and the season probability compounds across hundreds or thousands of games; the first-to-50 race also depends on the calendar order of candidates' games.
stages.distribution: Per-game generalised-Pareto exceedances with overtime as a discrete mixture; season probabilities are 1 - prod(1 - p_g), highly sensitive to tail shape; race outcomes are first-passage times with same-day ties.

stages.name: Season-long first event for low-volume players
stages.description: The one-made-three contract targets players who rarely shoot threes, often centers; the outcome is whether the season's attempts produce one make. Attempts per game are near zero and may be a coaching choice, so the probability is governed by games played times attempt rate (zero-inflated) and a position-level make prior, with role changes (a new coach encouraging stretch bigs) able to switch the rate regime.
stages.distribution: Zero-inflated Poisson attempts over the season; P(at least one make) = 1 - E[(1 - p3)^A] with A random; a point mass at zero for players who never attempt.

talent_strength.note: Player rate posterior, team strength for streaks and survival, and team-margin-driven plus/minus.

opponent_matchup.note: Season-long averages and records wash out single-opponent effects: the schedule's opponent mix enters through schedule strength in the simulation rather than through matchup-specific variables, so no matchup input is needed at this horizon.

role_personnel.note: Role and minutes trajectory, redistribution when teammates miss time.

availability_news.note: Games-played distribution, which scales totals, averages' denominators and the number of chances for single-game events.

coaching_scheme.note: Coaching changes that alter a star's role, minutes cap or rest policy are not quantified by any input in this archetype's list; the effect on a season stat leader could be large mid-season.

environment.note: Venue and altitude effects average out over 82 games and do not matter for season totals or streaks beyond what pace and team ratings capture.

game_context_script.note: Overtime is counted for the 54-point and 325-point contracts and is usually required for the latter; game script otherwise averages out over the season.

pace_volume.note: Per-game volume trajectory, three-point attempts for low-volume shooters, and game pace for extreme totals.

efficiency_conversion.note: Regression of early hot streaks in shooting-dependent stats toward talent.

distribution_variance.note: Variance of averages, team run-length and first-loss distributions, single-game exceedance tails and league-wide unions.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest incentives near eligibility thresholds and schedule density.

officiating_rules.note: Scorer-credit practices for steals and blocks (relevant to the 15-stocks contract) and the source agencies' rounding and correction policy for averages are not versioned in any input; referee crews themselves are irrelevant at season horizon.

settlement_contract.note: Rounded published average with no minimum, 1/N ties by calendar day or total, OT counted for single-game thresholds, regular season only with Cup games before the final.

nba.stat_rate_posterior.label: Shrunk posterior of a player's true per-game stat rate given games to date and preseason projection
nba.stat_rate_posterior.mechanism: A season-long average or leader race depends on the player's true rate, which is a weighted combination of the preseason projection and the noisy to-date average.
nba.stat_rate_posterior.rationale: Early-season averages overstate hot starts; the weight on results needs to be calibrated per statistic (scoring is more stable than rebounding and assists), and the posterior variance determines how much the leader gap is worth.
nba.stat_rate_posterior.measurement: Per stat s in {points, rebounds, assists, steals, blocks, 3PM} on a per-36-minute basis: prior mean = nba.preseason projection (last-two-season blend with aging adjustment). n_prior,s is estimated by backtest on 10 seasons as the value that minimises out-of-sample squared error of the next-20-game per-36 rate, via method of moments n_prior = sigma2_within/sigma2_between (report the estimate, not a fixed 25/35/40). Posterior mean = (n_prior x prior + n x observed)/(n_prior + n) using games with minutes weights; posterior sd = sqrt(sigma2_within/(n_prior + n) x overdispersion factor). Convert to per-game using projected minutes from nba.minutes. As-of: games before tip.
nba.stat_rate_posterior.why: Provides the leader-gap state in correct units, rather than raw season totals.

nba.qualification_probability.label: Probability a candidate meets the contract's qualification rule (games, minutes, or none)
nba.qualification_probability.mechanism: Leader and award-like markets require a minimum number of games or minutes; a player's chance depends on the distribution of games played and on strategic rest near the threshold.
nba.qualification_probability.rationale: A scoring leader who misses 25 games might be disqualified under a minimum-games rule or still counted if the rule says qualification thresholds do not apply; this is a cliff in the payoff and varies by contract.
nba.qualification_probability.measurement: For each candidate, qualification probability = P(GP_final >= G_min) where G_min is parsed from the contract text (0 if no threshold applies). GP_final = GP_to_date + sum over remaining team games of Bernoulli(a_g), a_g = (1 - h_g) x (1 - r_g): h_g from the injury hazard (nba.injury_risk_season, current status vintage) and r_g = rest probability fitted by logistic on 5 seasons (age, back-to-back, games missed, whether the team has clinched, whether the player is already above threshold), with the convolution computed exactly (Poisson-binomial). Output P(qualify), the conditional leader probability given qualification, and the slack = remaining games - (G_min - GP). Update after every game; use report vintages as of the as-of time only.
raw_data: games played to date, remaining schedule per team
nba.qualification_probability.why: Conditional only: no sampled series in this archetype has a games-played minimum (KXNBASTATAVG waives it); kept as context for any future leader contract with a minimum.

nba.streak_hit_persistence.label: Game-to-game persistence of threshold hits and streak-break hazard (DNP, rest, matchup)
nba.streak_hit_persistence.mechanism: A streak of N games meeting a threshold is a run-length process whose per-game hit probability varies with minutes and rest and which is broken by any DNP or rest night.
nba.streak_hit_persistence.rationale: Treating hits as independent with the season-average rate understates both streak and break risk; minutes and rest dependencies create positive autocorrelation within a stretch, and the specific rule (whether inactive games break the streak) changes everything.
nba.streak_hit_persistence.measurement: For each player estimate a logistic model of threshold hit on minutes projection, rest days, opponent defensive rating and lag-1 hit (to capture persistence beyond minutes) over a 3-season window; compute probability of a run of length at least N via a Markov chain with state = current run length and per-game hit probability from the model; add break hazard per game from injury/rest model. Adjust for the rule on inactive games (counts as break, skip, or void).
raw_data: player-game points and minutes with rest and DNP flags (3 seasons)
nba.streak_hit_persistence.why: Hypothetical: no player consecutive-game threshold series exists in the ledger (only team win streaks), so this is not a required input until such a contract is listed. Gives the actual structure of consecutive-game contracts, where the product of per-game probabilities is the wrong approximation.

nba.team_record_head_to_head_linkage.label: Dependence between teams' records via head-to-head games and conference schedule overlap
nba.team_record_head_to_head_linkage.mechanism: Records of contending teams are not independent: when two top teams play each other, one gains what the other loses, and shared opponents create correlation in schedule luck.
nba.team_record_head_to_head_linkage.rationale: Best-record and most-wins markets are about the maximum over teams, so the covariance of wins across teams matters; ignoring head-to-head linkage and common opponents misstates the extreme's distribution.
nba.team_record_head_to_head_linkage.measurement: From the remaining schedule compute pairwise numbers of head-to-head games and common-opponent overlap; in the simulation draw correlated team-strength shocks and enforce zero-sum head-to-head results; estimate the covariance of final win totals across the top-8 contenders by simulation; output distribution of the maximum and the probability of ties (tie handling per rule). As-of: nightly.
nba.team_record_head_to_head_linkage.why: Needed for record and winning-streak contracts of any team vs the league.

nba.longest_streak_max_and_tie_model.label: Distribution of the league-longest win streak and the number of tied teams (1/N payout), read from the shared nba.standings_sim path draws
nba.longest_streak_max_and_tie_model.mechanism: The league-longest streak is the maximum over 30 teams of the longest run of consecutive wins in each team's sequence, so a 'longest streak' contract depends on every team's game-by-game win probabilities, their serial dependence, and the chance that two or more teams share the maximum and split the payout. It is computed as a functional of the shared standings_sim paths so streak and win-total contracts are priced from the same draws.
nba.longest_streak_max_and_tie_model.rationale: KXNBATEAMWINSTREAK pays $1/N to each of N teams tied for the longest streak and only regular-season games (Cup games before the final included) count, so the value for one team is P(it holds the maximum) times E[1/N | it does]. Strengths matter through a convex path: the best team is not only more likely to have a long run but also faces a different set of opponents and rest games, and common rating shocks make streaks cluster in time and in teams. Ignoring ties overstates the value of a favourite when two strong teams reach the same length.
nba.longest_streak_max_and_tie_model.measurement: A view, not a separate simulation: read each team's game-by-game win/loss sequence from the stored paths of the single shared nba.standings_sim run (the same 20,000 season draws, with the same posterior rating draw, home court, rest and injury scenarios that price win totals, seeds and records), and compute on every stored path each team's longest run, with the streak carried in from completed games and counting Cup knockout games before the final but excluding the Cup final, play-in and playoffs. For each team report P(team has the strict maximum), P(team is in the tied set), the distribution of N and E[payout] = E[floor(100/N)/100 * 1{team in the tied set}] as frequencies over those same paths. Do not redraw ratings or games; if the stored paths lack game-level order, extend nba.standings_sim instead. Serial dependence beyond what the shared draw implies (common within-season rating shock) is checked, not re-simulated: compare the simulated league-longest-streak and tie-frequency distribution over the stored paths with the last 15 seasons of real streak lengths and, if they disagree, adjust the shared simulation's game-level dependence so win totals and streaks stay on one set of draws. As-of: nightly with nba.standings_sim; current run for each team carried in.
free_sources: nba_api leaguegamelog (game results by team and date)
raw_data: Team game results by date for current and 15 prior seasons
Remaining schedule with home/away and rest
nba.longest_streak_max_and_tie_model.why: Serves KXNBATEAMWINSTREAK (the team with the longest win streak, ties paid $1/N): the run-length maximum over 30 teams and the tie count, read from the stored nba.standings_sim season paths (not redrawn). KXNBAWINSTREAK (any team reaching 20 wins) uses nba.team_win_streak_hazard, a view of the same paths, and KXNBALASTTOLOSE uses nba.undefeated_start_survival.

nba.single_game_ceiling_tail.label: Per-game tail model for a player's maximum single-game points (exceedance of 50+/54+ and overtime contribution)
nba.single_game_ceiling_tail.mechanism: A highest-scoring-performance contract is the maximum over about 70 games of a heavy-tailed scoring distribution, with extreme nights requiring high minutes, hot shooting, free throws and often overtime.
nba.single_game_ceiling_tail.rationale: The mean scoring rate is nearly irrelevant for 54+; the exceedance probability per game is a tail quantity that must be estimated with a peaks-over-threshold model and then compounded over remaining games (1 - (1-p)^G).
nba.single_game_ceiling_tail.measurement: For each candidate fit a generalised Pareto to exceedances of points over u=35 (all games including OT, 3 seasons) with shape shrunk to the league value (prior weight 40 exceedances) and player-specific scale. P(game >= 35) = empirical share of the player's games with >=35 (shrunk to the league share given usage tier with k=30 games), computed over all games he plays (not only minutes >= 32) times an explicit minutes-mix term from nba.minutes. P(pts >= 54) = P(game >= 35) x GPD tail beyond 54 minus u; do not add a separate OT adjustment (already in the data); optionally condition on the opponent via own-model environment. P(at least one in remaining G games) = 1 - E[(1 - p)^G] with games-played uncertainty from nba.injury_risk_season; also store the season-to-date maximum (resolves YES if already met).
raw_data: player-game points, minutes, OT flag, season-to-date maximum
nba.single_game_ceiling_tail.why: KXNBAPLAYERHIGHSCORE (54+ in any game, OT counted) and the first-to-50 race both need the per-game exceedance tail of a scorer's points; moved here with the series from the counting-specials record.

nba.avg_rounding_and_games_state.label: Season-average state with rounding rule: unrounded to rounded threshold and remaining games
nba.avg_rounding_and_games_state.mechanism: The contract uses the rounded per-game figure from the source agencies, so the effective threshold on the unrounded average is half a rounding unit below the stated strike, and the average itself converges as games accumulate.
nba.avg_rounding_and_games_state.rationale: A 2.6+ three-pointers per game contract resolves on the rounded value, so a true average of 2.55 counts as 2.6 (at one-decimal rounding); ignoring the rounding shifts the threshold and its uncertainty is smaller as the season progresses; zero games played counts as an average of zero.
nba.avg_rounding_and_games_state.measurement: State = (makes to date, games played, games remaining); posterior of the player's rest-of-season average (shrunk) times remaining games plus makes to date gives the final average distribution; compute P(round(final_avg, d) >= strike) = P(final_avg >= strike - 0.5*10^-d) with d = 1 assumed from the strike precision and not confirmed by the rules (the text says only 'rounded figure as reported by the Source Agencies'; verify the decimal places and the half-up rule, sp-source-agencies), include the probability of playing zero games (settles at 0) and the denominator being games actually played. As-of: nightly after games.
raw_data: Player-game makes and games played to date
nba.avg_rounding_and_games_state.why: KXNBASTATAVG resolves on the rounded published average with no minimum and zero for zero games; this state-and-rounding input converts the rate posterior into the settlement probability.

nba.team_win_streak_hazard.label: Hazard of a team reaching a 20-game winning streak (run-length chain with heterogeneous game win probabilities)
nba.team_win_streak_hazard.mechanism: A 20-game win streak requires 20 consecutive wins; with game win probabilities of 75-85% for the best team, the chance depends on the full sequence of probabilities, their correlation through star health and schedule, and the number of teams that could qualify.
nba.team_win_streak_hazard.rationale: Averaging a team's win probability underestimates the chance because a streak concentrates in stretches of weak opponents and healthy rosters; the league-wide market is a union over 30 teams and 63 windows each (82 games minus 19).
nba.team_win_streak_hazard.measurement: View of the shared season paths: for each team, P(run of >= 20 consecutive wins at some point) = share of nba.standings_sim paths whose game sequence (current run carried in, Cup group and knockout games before the final counted, play-in and playoffs excluded) contains such a run; an exact dynamic-programming recursion on the same per-game probabilities (state = run length 0..19, absorbing 20) is the check for each team, and head-to-head games are consistent across teams because they come from the same path. As-of: nightly.
nba.team_win_streak_hazard.why: KXNBAWINSTREAK asks whether any team reaches 20 straight regular-season wins (Cup games counted); the per-window run-length chain gives each team's hazard directly.

nba.undefeated_start_survival.label: Survival probability of undefeated starts by calendar day (last remaining unbeaten team)
nba.undefeated_start_survival.mechanism: The last undefeated team is the one whose first loss comes latest, measured by the date of the first loss, so the market depends on survival functions of each team and ties by date.
nba.undefeated_start_survival.rationale: The product of win probabilities gives each team's survival, but the contract resolves by the day of the first loss and splits ties when several teams lose on the same day, so the probability of a team being last depends on ties and calendar clustering.
nba.undefeated_start_survival.measurement: For each team compute S_i(d) = product over games on days <= d of P(win) (from ratings, rest and home/away); P(team i is the last undefeated) = sum over days of P(i's first loss on day d and all others have lost by day d), with ties on the same day sharing 1/N; compute by simulation with dependence from shared opponents. As-of: nightly; early in the season (about 8-10 games played) the field is nearly resolved.
raw_data: schedule with dates, ratings, current records
nba.undefeated_start_survival.why: KXNBALASTTOLOSE is decided by the calendar day of each unbeaten team's first loss with same-day ties 1/N; no other input in this archetype models first-loss dates.

nba.three_volume.label: 3PA rate, catch-and-shoot share, 3P% shrinkage and opponent 3PA allowed
nba.three_volume.mechanism: Threes made equal attempts times make probability; attempts are driven by role, minutes and opponent scheme, and make% must be shrunk heavily.
nba.three_volume.rationale: A player's 3PA per minute is much more stable than 3P%; make% over a season reverts toward career and shot-quality-based expectation. Opponent 3PA allowed and pace/spacing change attempt volume. Subtle: attempts are overdispersed (game-to-game volume varies), so a binomial with fixed attempts understates variance.
nba.three_volume.measurement: 3PA per 36 minutes with exponential weights (half-life 20 games) shrunk to the player's prior-season rate with k=20 games; catch-and-shoot share from tracking splits when available; attempt count model = negative binomial with mean = 3PA/36 x projected minutes/36 x opponent index (opponent 3PA allowed per 100 / league mean, 20-game half-life) and dispersion estimated on 3 seasons. 3P% is not computed here; use nba.three_make_by_openness_prior. Output expected 3PA, sd and P(3PA >= k). As-of: games before tip.
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com (free, undocumented, rate-limited) leaguedashplayerptshot / shotchartdetail
PBPStats.com (free tier: on/off, lineup, possession-level splits)
nba.three_volume.why: KXNBAONE3PT asks whether a low-volume shooter makes at least one three all season; season attempts (rate x minutes x games) and a position-level make prior decide it.

nba.league_first_to_threshold_race.label: League-wide first-passage race to a single-game scoring threshold (first 50-point game) with same-day ties
nba.league_first_to_threshold_race.mechanism: The first 50-point game of the season is a race across all high-volume scorers: every game a candidate plays carries a small probability of 50+, and the winner is the candidate whose hit comes on the earliest calendar day, with same-day hits splitting the payout.
nba.league_first_to_threshold_race.rationale: A per-player 'scores 50 this season' probability is not the contract: the price depends on how many rival candidates exist, how early each plays and how often, and on same-day splits. Subtle: the race is usually decided in the first weeks or months, so early-season schedule density, minutes restrictions after the preseason and the number of credible candidates matter more than full-season rates.
nba.league_first_to_threshold_race.measurement: For each candidate i and remaining regular-season game g on date t_g: p_ig = P(points >= 50 | plays) from nba.single_game_ceiling_tail (generalised-Pareto exceedance above 35 points with the overtime adjustment) times P(plays g) from the availability inputs. Simulate 20000 seasons in date order: draw hits game by game, stop at the first date with any hit and split 1/N among same-date hitters. Candidates: players projected at 20+ points per game or with a 45+ game in the last 2 seasons; all others enter as a residual field with a league-wide per-game rate fitted on 10 seasons. As-of: nightly; resolved once a 50-point game occurs.
free_sources: nba_api player game logs (free, undocumented, rate-limited)
Basketball-Reference game logs and game finder (free, polite scraping)
raw_data: Player-game points and minutes with OT flag
nba.league_first_to_threshold_race.why: KXNBAFIRST50PTS (rules-verified) is a calendar race across players with 1/N same-day ties; neither the ceiling tail nor the rate posterior alone prices it.

nba.league_extreme_game_event_rate.label: League-wide probability of extreme single-game events over the remaining regular season (325+ combined points, 15+ steals plus blocks)
nba.league_extreme_game_event_rate.mechanism: 'Any game' and 'any player' contracts are unions over all remaining games of rare events whose per-game probability depends on both teams' pace and offense plus overtime periods (game totals) or on a few high-activity defenders (combined steals and blocks), so the season probability is 1 minus the product over games of (1 - p_g).
nba.league_extreme_game_event_rate.rationale: These events sit far in the tail: a 325-point game needs exceptional pace and shooting and usually more than one overtime, and 15+ steals plus blocks by one player is extremely rare. Per-game probabilities are tiny and governed by tail shape (count of OT periods, heavy-tailed defensive activity), so fits to means can be wrong by orders of magnitude, and the union over about 1,230 games compounds the error.
nba.league_extreme_game_event_rate.measurement: Game total: for each remaining game, regulation total = mean from both teams' opponent-adjusted pace and offensive ratings as of the game date plus an empirical residual with a generalised-Pareto tail above the 99th percentile (5 seasons); add overtime periods and combined OT points from nba.ot_prob_ratings_margin; P(total >= 325) by simulation. Steals plus blocks: per player-game, a bivariate negative binomial from shrunk per-36 rates (prior weight 1,000 minutes) times projected minutes, tail checked against 20 seasons of single-game maxima; P(any player >= 15) = 1 - product over player-games. Season probability = 1 - product over remaining games, Cup knockout games included and the Cup final excluded. As-of: nightly.
free_sources: Basketball-Reference game logs, line scores and player game finder (free, polite scraping)
raw_data: Game totals with overtime periods (5+ seasons)
nba.league_extreme_game_event_rate.why: KXNBAGAMEHIGHSCORE and KXNBAGAMESPECIALS (both rules-verified) are league-wide unions of tail events; no other input gives per-game tail probabilities summed over the schedule.

nba.season_plus_minus_projection.label: Season total plus/minus projection: on-court net margin rate times remaining minutes, combined across teams after trades
nba.season_plus_minus_projection.mechanism: Total plus/minus is the scoring margin while a player is on court summed over the season, so it equals on-court minutes times his lineups' net margin per minute; team strength and minutes dominate it, the player's own impact is a smaller part.
nba.season_plus_minus_projection.rationale: A plus/minus leader race is usually won by a heavy-minutes starter on the best team rather than the best individual player, and teammates on a dominant team compete with each other. Subtle: the rules combine a traded player's totals across teams, and games missed scale the total down linearly, so a durable starter on a 60-win team can beat a better player who misses 15 games.
nba.season_plus_minus_projection.measurement: For each candidate: remaining minutes = remaining team games x P(plays) x projected minutes per game (nba.injury_risk_season, nba.minutes). On-court margin per 100 possessions = team opponent-adjusted net rating (nba.ratings, as of date) + (1 - p_on) x on/off differential shrunk toward 0 with prior weight 3000 on-court possessions, where p_on = projected minutes share of 48 (this corrects the overlap between team net rating and on/off). Convert to points per minute using projected team pace (possessions per 48). Final total = official plus/minus to date (summed across teams for traded players) + remaining minutes x per-minute margin, simulated jointly with team season outcomes so teammates share team shocks; ties split 1/N. As-of: nightly, standings and plus/minus after final scores.
free_sources: Basketball-Reference player plus/minus pages (free, polite scraping)
raw_data: player season plus/minus and minutes to date (combined across teams)
nba.season_plus_minus_projection.why: KXNBASTATLEADER (rules-verified, total plus/minus) is decided by team margin times minutes, which the per-game stat-rate inputs do not represent.

nba.ot_prob_ratings_margin.label: Market-free overtime probability and overtime scoring increment from the ratings-implied regulation margin
nba.ot_prob_ratings_margin.mechanism: A game goes to overtime only if the regulation margin is exactly zero, so P(OT) is the mass at zero of the regulation-margin distribution, highest for evenly matched teams; each five-minute overtime then adds scoring at both teams' per-minute rates, and a further overtime follows with the tie probability of a five-minute period.
nba.ot_prob_ratings_margin.rationale: The catalog nba.ot_model conditions P(OT) on the closing-spread bucket (a market quantity) and says one OT adds about 10-12 points to totals, which is the per-team figure, not the combined one. A market-free version takes the regulation-margin distribution from team ratings and sizes OT correctly: roughly 11-13 points per team and 22-26 combined per period, with repeated overtimes possible. Subtle: the zero-margin mass is larger than a continuous normal approximation gives, because end-of-game tactics (holding for the last shot, fouling when ahead by three) cluster regulation margins between 0 and 3.
nba.ot_prob_ratings_margin.measurement: Step 1: regulation-margin mean mu from nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve (opponent-adjusted net ratings x expected possessions/100 + home advantage, as of tipoff, adjusted for confirmed inactives). Step 2: P(regulation tie) = logistic regression of the indicator "regulation margin = 0" on |mu| over the last 5 regular seasons (about 6,000 games; league base rate to be estimated), smoothed across 1-point |mu| bins. Step 3: per-team OT points = league points per team per OT period from play-by-play scaled by the team's opponent-adjusted pace and offensive rating relative to league; combined OT points = sum over both teams. Step 4: P(k-th OT | (k-1)-th OT) = pooled empirical tie rate of five-minute periods with prior weight 200 OT periods. Output P(OT), P(2+ OT), per-team and combined OT-points distributions. Only team ratings, pace and results enter.

nba.ot_prob_ratings_margin.why: KXNBAGAMEHIGHSCORE and KXNBAPLAYERHIGHSCORE count overtime; a 325-point game nearly always needs one or more overtimes, so the multi-OT probability from the ratings-implied regulation margin is part of the tail.

nba.season_stat_pace.reason: Current totals and per-game trajectory are the state variable of a leader race; but raw to-date averages must be shrunk toward a preseason projection, otherwise a 10-game hot start dominates.

nba.minutes.reason: Minutes per game is the dominant driver of per-game counting stats and changes with injuries, age and coach; needs a trajectory rather than a single projection.

nba.usage.reason: Role stability determines scoring per game, but for assists and rebounds leaders usage is far less relevant than touches or rebound chances; mislabelled as primary-level driver of all stat races.

nba.injury_risk_season.reason: Games played is the biggest source of variance in who leads a season stat; the existing label is a games-missed expectation, whereas qualification contracts need a distribution of the number of games played.

nba.load_mgmt.reason: Rest policy lowers games played and minutes for older stars and interacts with eligibility rules; moderate effect, concentrated in the second half.

nba.games_played_eligibility.reason: Demoted from primary: the sampled KXNBASTATAVG text says 'League minimum qualification thresholds do not apply', so for the live per-game average contract there is no games-played cliff. The input matters only if a leader contract with a minimum-games rule is later found, and the 2026-27 criteria are unconfirmed (ss-rules-versioning).

nba.stat_dist.reason: Game-level distributions matter for streak probability and for the variance of a season average; the effect on leader probability is secondary to the number of games.

nba.standings_sim.reason: A season simulation is what the team streak and last-undefeated contracts require (game-by-game outcomes with shared rating shocks); for individual averages it is only context.

nba.teammate_absence_shift.reason: Role shifts when teammates miss time affect rates, but the season-level horizon makes a game-by-game with/without split second-order.

nba.ratings.reason: Promoted from context: the any-team 20-game streak, last-undefeated and plus/minus leader contracts now in this archetype are driven by team strength, which sets game win probabilities and on-court margins.

m.quote_history.reason: A price series reflects information arrival; it is a market observable not a driver of stat totals.

m.rules_text.reason: Nine of eleven series have rules text and they differ materially (rounded average with no minimum, 1/N calendar-day ties, OT inclusion, traded totals combined); versioned rules are primary.

m.strike_hit_rates.reason: With one label per season per contract realised hit-rate history is too thin for calibration of rare events; context only.

interactions.mechanism: The probability of leading is a mixture over the number of games the candidate plays; a small current gap matters less than the chance that the leading player misses time, so leader probability falls faster than a gap-based normal calculation implies.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute leader probability from a model with random games played vs fixed games and compare calibration on historical season leaders.

interactions.mechanism: Applies only if a contract uses a minimum-games rule (none is sampled; KXNBASTATAVG waives it): then players near the threshold are managed to qualify, so expected games played is not independent of the rule and the leader probability steps at the threshold. Under KXNBASTATAVG the interaction collapses to a smooth average plus a mass at zero games.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare rest rates in the final 15 games by distance to the eligibility threshold.

interactions.mechanism: A 20-game team streak (KXNBAWINSTREAK) or the league-longest streak needs roughly six weeks of near-certain wins, which in practice requires the team's stars to be healthy for the whole window; a single absence lowers per-game win probability for several games and usually ends the run, so the streak probability depends on the joint health of the top players over a window, not on the season-average rating.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute historical run-length distributions split by whether the top two players by minutes missed any game in the window, and compare streak hazards from the simulation with and without star-absence draws.

interactions.mechanism: For the longest-streak and last-undefeated contracts, a head-to-head meeting between two teams on runs (or two unbeaten teams) ends one of the runs with certainty, so their run lengths and first-loss days are negatively linked; simulating teams independently overstates the chance that two teams share the maximum streak (1/N payout) or are both still unbeaten past a given day.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the league-longest streak, its tied count and first-loss days with and without zero-sum head-to-head games, and compare with the last 15 seasons of real streak ties and last-unbeaten dates.

interactions.mechanism: A teammate's long-term injury switches the player's role regime for the rest of the season, changing the posterior mean and variance at once; to-date averages from the earlier regime are misleading.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit rate models with a regime indicator for key-teammate absence and compare predictive error with and without it.

interactions.mechanism: A candidate's chance of being first to 50 falls with the number and early-season schedule of rival candidates, not only with his own tail: the same per-game exceedance gives a much lower race probability when three other scorers play more games in October and November, and same-day hits split the payout.
interactions.how_to_test: Back-test simulated first-to-50 winners and dates against past seasons; compare race probabilities with naive per-player season probabilities normalised to sum to one.

interactions.mechanism: Total plus/minus is team net margin per minute times minutes played, so a strong team's starter accumulates margin quickly while a missed month cuts his total proportionally; the leader race is therefore a product of team strength and durability, and teammates are positively correlated through the team term.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress season plus/minus totals on team net rating times minutes and on the player's on/off differential; check the share of variance explained by the product term.

interactions.mechanism: A 325-point game is out of reach in regulation for almost all matchups and becomes possible mainly through one or more overtimes, each adding roughly 22-26 combined points; the season probability therefore scales with the multi-overtime probability of high-pace, evenly matched games rather than with average totals.
interactions.how_to_test: Tabulate historical 300+ games by number of OT periods and compare the simulated share of 325+ outcomes with and without overtime.

nonlinearities.shape: cliff at the games threshold, conditional on a qualification-based contract (absent under KXNBASTATAVG)
nonlinearities.why: The payoff for a leader depends on meeting a minimum number of games, so the probability of leading jumps when a player's expected games cross the threshold; the response is a step smoothed by availability uncertainty.

nonlinearities.shape: exponential decay in run length (geometric) with minutes-dependent hazard
nonlinearities.why: The probability of N consecutive hits decays roughly as p^N, with p itself dependent on minutes; small errors in p are amplified exponentially in N.

nonlinearities.shape: saturating: weight on observed average rises as n/(n+n_prior)
nonlinearities.why: The influence of to-date results on the posterior mean follows a hyperbolic shrinkage curve, so early-season changes in average move the estimate little and late-season changes move it a lot.

nonlinearities.shape: union compounding: 1 - prod over about 1,230 games of (1 - p_g)
nonlinearities.why: Tiny per-game probabilities compound over the season, so a factor-of-two error in tail shape changes the season probability almost proportionally while it is small and saturates near one when the tail is fat; the response to tail parameters is far from linear.

nonlinearities.shape: linear in minutes, maximum over correlated candidates
nonlinearities.why: Each player's total grows linearly with minutes and team margin, but the leader probability is a maximum across correlated teammates and rivals, so it is steep in the gap between the top two projected totals.
