contract.settlement_definition: Twenty-four playoff-series and Cup series, 23 with rules text. Single series: winner (KXNBASERIES), total games over X.5 (KXNBASERIESGAMES), exact score (KXNBASERIESSCORE, KXNBAFINALSEXACT), games spread (named team wins by more than X.5 games), comeback after trailing by 2+ games (KXNBASERIESCOMEBACK: 0-2, 3-0 or 3-1 deficits count), any team winning a game after trailing by 30+ points (KXNBASERIESGCOMEBACK), exact number of road wins (a road win is a visiting-team win), no road win in the series (KXNBASERIESROADWIN), the champion clinching at home (wins the title in a home game) and a 40+ point margin in any Finals game (KXNBAFINBLOWOUT). Playoff-wide: any 3-0 series comeback (lose the first three, win four straight), at least N series going to Game 7, at least N sweeps or upsets in a round (an upset is a higher numerical seed beating a lower one), a team's exact playoff losses, a team going 16-0 and winning the title, and at least N home playoff games actually hosted in the home stadium (Play-In games excluded). Cup: champion, Finals qualifiers, group winners, any team of a group winning the Cup, and the Finals matchup, which resolves on qualification. No text addresses overtime, suspended games or relocated venues; KXNBAPLAYOFFHOMEGAMES is TITLE_ONLY.

rules_evidence.quote: the specified number of playoff games have to be actually hosted by Miami and played in their home stadium in order for the market to resolve Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Home-games count is of games actually played at the home arena; a scheduled but unplayed game (series ended) or a relocated game does not count, and Play-In games are excluded.

rules_evidence.quote: Resolution occurs immediately upon qualification, not when the game is actually played.
rules_evidence.establishes: Cup Finals matchup resolves when both semifinals are decided, so it is a bracket-progression event, not the final's result.

rules_evidence.quote: If any team in West Group C wins the Pro Basketball Cup in the 2026-27 Pro Basketball season, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Group-to-win is the sum of Cup-title probabilities of the group's teams, which share group-stage games and so are negatively dependent at the qualification step.

rules_evidence.quote: If either team is down 2-0, 3-0, or 3-1 in games and comes back to ultimately win the series, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Series comeback is a path event on the game sequence (any deficit of two games), not a function of the series winner or length alone.

rules_evidence.quote: meaning they lose the first three games of a series (going down 0-3), and then win four consecutive games to win the series 4-3
rules_evidence.establishes: Playoff-wide 3-0 comeback is a union over all series of a specific seven-game path, extremely rare and sensitive to game-to-game dependence.

rules_evidence.quote: either team must overcome a deficit of at least 30 points and win in any individual game within the series
rules_evidence.establishes: This is an in-game comeback from a 30-point deficit, unioned over the series' games, so it needs score-path data, not the series simulation.

rules_evidence.quote: If either team in the Pro Basketball Finals records a margin of victory of at least 40 points in any individual game in the 2026 Pro Basketball Finals, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Finals blowout is the maximum single-game final margin over the Finals games reaching 40, a tail event compounded over four to seven games.

rules_evidence.quote: A series upset occurs when a team with a higher numerical seed defeats a team with a lower numerical seed in a playoff series
rules_evidence.establishes: Upset counts depend on the seeds of the teams that actually meet in the round, so earlier rounds and the Play-In determine which series can be upsets.

rules_evidence.quote: The first road win in a playoff series is achieved the first time the home team loses and the away team wins
rules_evidence.establishes: Road-win contracts are defined on venue-specific game results under the 2-2-1-1-1 format, so home-court strength per game matters, not only series strength.

rules_evidence.quote: The market resolves to Yes if the 2026 Pro Basketball champion wins the championship in a home game.
rules_evidence.establishes: Clinch-at-home depends on which game ends the Finals: the higher seed can clinch at home only in games 5 or 7, the lower seed only in games 4 or 6.

rules_evidence.quote: needs to win the championship while going unbeaten (16-0)
rules_evidence.establishes: Undefeated run is four consecutive sweeps ending in the title, a product of four small probabilities.

variants_and_edge_cases: Strike construction differs: series games 'over 6.5', games spread 'more than 2.5 games', road wins and playoff losses 'exactly N' (KXNBAPOLOSE is titled 'exactly 7 losses' but carries strike_type greater_or_equal), Game 7 and sweep/upset counts 'at least N'.

Path events (2+ game comeback, 3-0 comeback, first road win, clinch at home) are functions of the ordered game sequence and venue pattern, so the series model must be simulated game by game with dependence, not collapsed to winner and length.

In-game extremes (30-point comeback win, 40-point margin) union a per-game tail over the series' games; the number of games is itself random and correlated with how even the teams are, which works in opposite directions for the two events.
Home playoff games count only games actually hosted in the home stadium; Play-In games do not count, and a game moved to a neutral site would not count.

Cup: the Finals matchup resolves when both finalists qualify, group-to-win sums title probabilities over a group, group winners and qualifiers depend on group tiebreakers including point differential, and the Cup final itself is not a regular-season game.

Upsets use numerical seeds after the Play-In, so a 7 or 8 seed that came through the Play-In beating a 2 seed is an upset; equal seeds cannot meet before the Finals, where seed numbers from different conferences make the definition ambiguous.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official playoff results, game-by-game scores and venues, play-by-play score paths (for 30-point deficits), the post-Play-In seeding, and the Cup standings and bracket; the sampled texts name no source agency.

mechanism.summary: These contracts are functionals of a playoff (or Cup) bracket simulated game by game. Per-game win probability comes from availability-adjusted strength, playoff-tightened rotations and the venue under the 2-2-1-1-1 pattern, with dependence between games of a series through injuries, adjustments and elimination-game effects. The ordered game sequence yields winners, lengths, exact scores, games spreads, comebacks from series deficits, road-win counts and clinch venues; concurrent series in a round yield counts of sweeps, upsets and Game 7s; and each team's run yields its losses, home games hosted and the rare 16-0 path. Two contracts need within-game score paths (a 30-point comeback, a 40-point margin). The Cup adds group tables with point-differential tiebreaks and a single-elimination knockout.

stages.name: Per-game win probability inside a playoff series
stages.description: Each game's win probability comes from playoff-strength ratings adjusted for who is available, rotation tightening that lifts star-heavy teams, and home court under the 2-2-1-1-1 pattern (higher seed at home in games 1, 2, 5 and 7). Within a series the probability drifts with injuries, matchup adjustments and the series state: a team facing elimination tends to perform above its rating and a team that has just lost at home adjusts, so games are not independent draws.
stages.distribution: Per-game probabilities typically 30-80%, alternating with venue; mild positive serial dependence plus regime switches when a star is injured mid-series.

stages.name: Ordered game sequence: length, score, spread, comebacks, road wins, clinch venue
stages.description: The ordered win/loss sequence of a best-of-seven determines the series winner, the number of games, the exact score, whether a games spread is covered, whether a team came back from 0-2, 1-3 or 0-3, how many road wins occurred, whether no road team ever won, and in which arena the clinching game was played. These are not functions of the winner alone: road-win and clinch-venue contracts depend on venue-specific probabilities, and comeback contracts on the dependence between consecutive games.
stages.distribution: Discrete distribution over the 70 possible win/loss sequences; length on {4,5,6,7} with mass moving to 6-7 for even matchups; road wins on {0..7}; comeback paths have low single-digit probabilities.

stages.name: Round counts and whole-run totals across the bracket
stages.description: Playoff-wide contracts aggregate over concurrent series and over a team's run: the number of Game 7s, sweeps or upsets in a round depends on the seed gaps of the pairings that actually occur (set by earlier rounds and the Play-In); a team's exact playoff losses, its home games actually hosted and the 16-0 title run are sums or products over the rounds it reaches. Common shocks such as officiating emphasis or a league-wide injury wave make concurrent series dependent.
stages.distribution: Counts over four to eight concurrent series (Poisson-binomial with dependence); team losses and home games are lumpy sums over rounds; the 16-0 path is a product of four sweep probabilities, well under 1%.

stages.name: Within-game score extremes compounded over a series
stages.description: KXNBASERIESGCOMEBACK pays if any game in the series is won by a team that trailed by 30 or more, and KXNBAFINBLOWOUT if any Finals game ends with a 40-point margin. Both need the score path or final margin distribution of playoff games, conditional on the strength gap and pace, compounded over a random number of games. Even matchups produce longer series (more chances) but fewer huge leads; uneven ones produce blowouts but end sooner, so the series length and the per-game tail interact. These two series are deliberately kept with the series contracts but staged separately, fed by play-by-play score paths (required_data 3), because the compounding over series length is what couples them to the bracket.
stages.distribution: Per-game P(margin >= 40) and P(win after trailing by 30+) are well below 1% for even playoff teams; union over 4-7 games with dependence through matchup and pace.

stages.name: Cup group stage and knockout
stages.description: Cup group winners and qualifiers are determined by group record and tiebreakers (including point differential), and the knockout stage is single-elimination. The Finals-matchup contract resolves when both finalists are known, so it is the joint probability of two bracket paths, group-to-win sums title chances of teams that played each other in the group, and the champion contract is three knockout wins after qualification. Incentives in the last group games depend on the standings state, and margin matters for tiebreaks. Filing decision (resolver, 8 Nov 2026): the Cup contracts stay in this archetype as this separate stage with their own inputs and data set (Cup schedule and group tables) rather than a new archetype, because they share the team-strength and single-elimination machinery but none of the best-of-seven inputs. 2026-27 format: group winners and one wild card per conference make conference-split quarterfinals hosted by the higher seed, semifinals at the higher seed's arena, final at Hinkle Fieldhouse.
stages.distribution: Small group tables with discrete outcomes; margin enters via the tiebreak; knockout rounds are single games with win probability near rating-implied values.

talent_strength.note: Availability-adjusted playoff strength for per-game and Cup game probabilities.

opponent_matchup.note: Bracket matchup and series conversion for playoff-count contracts; Cup group opponents by schedule.

role_personnel.note: Playoff rotation tightening (stars' minutes) shifts per-game strength inside series.

availability_news.note: Star availability vintages inside series and between rounds.

coaching_scheme.note: Coach-specific playoff rotation shortening, in-series adjustments and Cup tiebreak management (running up margin) are not represented by a dedicated input; their effect on series paths is unquantified.

environment.note: Home-court and travel structure inside series and the Cup.

game_context_script.note: Series-state effects, in-game deficit comebacks and Cup margins.

pace_volume.note: Possession counts are irrelevant for these advancement, series-path and Cup contracts beyond their contribution to team ratings; no pace or volume variable has independent influence on a series length, a series path or a Cup bracket outcome.

efficiency_conversion.note: Shooting efficiency regression matters inside team ratings but these contracts depend on standings and format outcomes; no stand-alone efficiency input improves them.

distribution_variance.note: Series-sequence pmf, round counts, final-margin tail and home-games count.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Elimination-game effects, Cup group incentives and rest between games.

officiating_rules.note: Format rules: 2-2-1-1-1, post-Play-In seeds for upset counting, Cup tiebreakers and bracket (rules, not referees).

settlement_contract.note: Exact versus at-least strikes, path definitions (2+ game and 3-0 comebacks, first road win, home clinch), seed-based upsets, games actually hosted, Cup matchup on qualification.

nba.play_in_path_model.label: Play-in bracket path probabilities given pre-play-in seed and relative strength
nba.play_in_path_model.mechanism: The play-in tournament maps seeds 7-10 to final seeds 7 and 8 through a fixed bracket, so the playoff qualification and the post-play-in seed differ from the regular-season seed; Kalshi's seed contracts are measured before the play-in.
nba.play_in_path_model.rationale: KXNBASEEDOU resolves on the regular-season seed before the play-in while qualification/play-in series depend on play-in outcomes; the same team has different probabilities for 'seed 8 or better' depending on which definition applies.
nba.play_in_path_model.measurement: Encode the bracket (7v8 winner gets the 7 seed; 9v10 loser is out; loser of 7v8 plays winner of 9v10 for the 8 seed), compute per-game win probabilities with home-court from team ratings and rest, and convolve to P(final seed 7, 8, out | pre-play-in seed, opponents); estimate the distribution of opponents from the standings simulation. As-of: nightly; rules versioned by season.
raw_data: Standings and seeds before the Play-In
nba.play_in_path_model.why: Sets which teams enter as the 7 and 8 seeds, which defines which first-round results count as upsets for KXNBAUPSET-type contracts.

nba.playoff_home_games_distribution.label: Distribution of the number of home playoff games by seed and path
nba.playoff_home_games_distribution.mechanism: A team's total home playoff games is the sum over rounds of home games in each series, which depend on home-court status (seed), series length and advancement.
nba.playoff_home_games_distribution.rationale: KXNBAPLAYOFFHOMEGAMES and KXNBAPLAYOFFHOST count games rather than winners; probability mass depends on the series-length distribution (4-7 games) and on losing in an early round with few home games.
nba.playoff_home_games_distribution.measurement: For each team and round compute P(reach round) and P(home-court | reach) from nba.title_path (better record hosts; Finals by record). Given series length L, home games are fixed by the 2-2-1-1-1 pattern: the higher seed hosts games 1,2,5,7, so it has 2,3,3,4 home games for L=4,5,6,7; the lower seed hosts games 3,4,6, so it has 2,2,3,3 home games for L=4,5,6,7. Draw L from nba.series_length_distribution conditioned on home status, then convolve per-round home-game counts across rounds into a pmf of total playoff home games. Output two pmfs: including play-in home games and excluding them; the contract wording selects which applies. As-of: nightly during the playoffs, conditioning on completed games.
free_sources: Computed from the series model and NBA schedule format
raw_data: bracket simulation outputs: P(reach round), opponent seed, series length pmf
home-court determination rule (better regular-season record, tiebreaks)
nba.playoff_home_games_distribution.why: Directly constructs the target pmf for the home-games series.

nba.cup_group_tiebreak_state.label: Cup group standings state with point-differential tiebreak and remaining-games simulation
nba.cup_group_tiebreak_state.mechanism: Cup group qualifiers are decided by group record then tiebreakers (head-to-head, point differential and so on), so the state is a table with a margin component that rewards running up scores in some games.
nba.cup_group_tiebreak_state.rationale: Group-winner and qualifier contracts depend on remaining games, but also on margin of victory in each game because the point-differential tiebreak influences outcomes; a win/loss-only simulation misses this.
nba.cup_group_tiebreak_state.measurement: From the Cup schedule compute standings, point differential and head-to-head results to date; simulate the remaining group games with margin distributions from team ratings (sd about 13 points per game) and apply the official group tiebreak order and wildcard rule to produce P(group winner), P(qualifier by wildcard); update after each Cup game. As-of: nightly; rules versioned by season.
raw_data: Cup schedule and results with margins
nba.cup_group_tiebreak_state.why: Needed for KXNBACUPQUAL and KXNBACUPGROUP contracts, which sit in this archetype.

nba.single_game_margin_pmf.label: Market-free single-game margin distribution for Cup group games (ratings-implied mean, compressed tails)
nba.single_game_margin_pmf.mechanism: The Cup point-differential tiebreak needs the distribution of each remaining group game's final margin, which is a ratings-implied mean plus a spread that is compressed in blowouts when starters sit and widened by overtime-free tails.
nba.single_game_margin_pmf.rationale: The existing nba.score_resid is a residual against market lines, which is a book calibration, not an input. The tiebreak value of a margin depends on the raw margin pmf: a 20-point win counts the same in the tiebreak sum whether or not it was needed, but coaches ease off, so the margin tail is lighter than a normal distribution. The pmf is built from scores and ratings only.
nba.single_game_margin_pmf.measurement: For each remaining group game: mean margin mu = (NetRtg_home_adj - NetRtg_away_adj) * expected_possessions/100 + home_adv from nba.off_rtg and nba.def_rtg (opponent-adjusted, as-of tipoff); spread = empirical distribution of final-margin residuals (final margin minus mu) from the last 5 seasons of regular-season games, giving a pmf on integer margins with sd of about 12-13 points (to be estimated, not assumed); apply the blowout compression curve from nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve to the tail. Sum margins over a team's remaining group games by convolution and rank teams with the official tiebreak order. No closing line or other price is used.
raw_data: team game results with final margins (5 seasons)
nba.single_game_margin_pmf.why: Replaces the weak, market-referenced nba.score_resid in stage s4 with a raw margin pmf for the Cup point-differential tiebreak.

nba.cup_finals_pair_probability.label: Probability of a specific Cup Finals pairing as the product of two conference bracket outcomes
nba.cup_finals_pair_probability.mechanism: The Cup Finals pair is formed by the two semifinal winners, one from each conference bracket (the knockout bracket is split by conference), so the pair probability is a product of two independent single-elimination outcomes.
nba.cup_finals_pair_probability.rationale: The matchup contract resolves immediately upon qualification, not when the game is played; its probability depends on group results and quarterfinal and semifinal games hosted by the higher seed (2026-27), so seeding matters through home court; East and West halves share no games before the final.
nba.cup_finals_pair_probability.measurement: P(team reaches final) = P(qualifies as group winner or wild card) x P(wins quarterfinal) x P(wins semifinal), from team ratings with home-court advantage for the higher seed in both the quarterfinal and the semifinal (2026-27: semifinals at the higher seed's arena, verified), with rest-days adjustment; East and West brackets are disjoint until the final, so P(pair) = P(A reaches final) x P(B reaches final) with no shared-venue correlation; the final itself is at neutral Hinkle Fieldhouse. Re-read the season's Cup rules each year; as-of nightly during the Cup.
nba.cup_finals_pair_probability.why: KXNBAMATCHUP (rules-verified) resolves on the named Cup Finals pair qualifying; this archetype had no input for the joint bracket-reach probability of two teams.

nba.series_length_distribution.label: Series-length distribution from per-game win probabilities
nba.series_length_distribution.mechanism: The number of games in a best-of-seven series is a function of per-game win probability, home pattern and dependence between games; this is the per-series kernel that nba.title_path calls inside each bracket draw.
nba.series_length_distribution.rationale: KXNBASERIESGAMES counts games, not points; the draft has no input for it except a generic series model reference outside the archetype.
nba.series_length_distribution.measurement: Per-series kernel: P(series ends in k games) by dynamic programming over home pattern 2-2-1-1-1 with per-game win probabilities from own-model playoff ratings and a series dependence parameter (game-to-game correlation about +0.05 on margin, estimated from 2000-2025 playoff series), injuries as of the as-of date; output P(4..7) and P(win). For a set matchup this is used directly; for bracket-level contracts the same kernel is evaluated inside nba.title_path draws, so lengths and advancement are consistent across archetypes.
raw_data: playoff series results by game with venue
own team ratings and injury status
nba.series_length_distribution.why: Series-games, exact-score, Game 7 and games-spread contracts are direct functionals of the length distribution.

nba.series_game_conditional_state.label: Playoff-series game-conditional state
nba.series_game_conditional_state.mechanism: In a series, a game's mean margin depends on series score, rest days between games, accumulated injuries and coaching adjustments.
nba.series_game_conditional_state.rationale: Single-game ratings treat games as independent; series markets (home clinch, game 7, comeback) depend on the dependency between games and on elimination-state minutes tightening.
nba.series_game_conditional_state.measurement: Model for game g of a series: margin_residual = actual margin - own-model pre-game expected margin (ratings plus home advantage, as of tipoff, from nba.ratings) regressed on rest days since the last game, elimination-game indicator for the trailing team, injury-status change since game 1 (minutes-weighted impact of newly absent players), previous game's margin (shrunk) and games played, on playoff series 2000-2025 with a series random intercept; estimate the sd of the random intercept by REML (do not assume 2 points) and report its posterior. Update the series effect after each completed game by a normal-normal step. Output a mean shift and sd for the next game. As-of: last completed game and the injury report vintage.
raw_data: series game logs with margin, minutes, rest days
nba.series_game_conditional_state.why: Comebacks from 0-2/3-1/0-3 and road-win counts depend on how the next game's probability moves with the series score and the previous result.

nba.final_margin_pmf_empirical.label: Empirical final-margin pmf by own-model mean and sd
nba.final_margin_pmf_empirical.mechanism: The final margin has non-smooth pmf structure (hole at zero, OT bump, late-game parity) that a normal density does not reproduce.
nba.final_margin_pmf_empirical.rationale: The draft names score_resid as the margin density by spread bucket, but spread buckets from market lines are circular and the pmf structure lives at the integer level; band edges at 5/6 and 10/11 fall exactly on such structure.
nba.final_margin_pmf_empirical.measurement: Collect 15 seasons of final signed margins; standardise z = (margin - mu_own)/sigma_own using own-model mean and sd; estimate the pmf of the integer margin by kernel smoothing of the z-density plus an explicit multiplicative correction per integer margin in [-12, 12] (ridge-shrunk to 1); validate by log-loss of band probabilities in 2 held-out seasons; recompute annually.
raw_data: Walk-forward own-model mu and sigma per game
nba.final_margin_pmf_empirical.why: Gives the per-game probability of a 40-point final margin that KXNBAFINBLOWOUT compounds over the Finals games.

nba.playoff_max_deficit_comeback_rate.label: Probability of winning a game after trailing by D or more points (max-deficit comeback rate)
nba.playoff_max_deficit_comeback_rate.mechanism: A team wins after trailing by D only if the leader's in-game margin path reaches D and then reverses fully; large leads trigger starter rest and slower pace by the leader, so reversals from 30+ are rare and depend on when the lead was built.
nba.playoff_max_deficit_comeback_rate.rationale: KXNBASERIESGCOMEBACK settles on any series game won after a 30-point deficit, a path event that no final-score model sees: a game can end close after a 30-point swing. Both the chance of a 30-point lead and the chance of reversing it depend on the strength gap, pace and how coaches manage big leads in the playoffs.
nba.playoff_max_deficit_comeback_rate.measurement: From play-by-play for 15 seasons compute for each game the maximum deficit faced by the eventual winner, M. For each threshold D in {20,25,30,35} fit separately a logistic model P(M >= D) = f(own-model pregame margin mu, own-model margin sd, pace, playoff flag), pooling D by an ordinal-logit if counts are below 40 events, and shrink the playoff coefficient to the regular-season value with prior weight 200 playoff games. Output per-game P(winner trails by >= D) for each side as a function of mu. Series union = 1 - E[prod over games (1 - p_g)] using series length draws and the per-game mu; add a shared series random effect on the log-odds (variance estimated from playoff series) rather than assuming independence. As-of: before game 1 and after each game using realised results.
raw_data: play-by-play score after every scoring event with game clock and period (15 seasons)
own-model pregame margin mean and sd
nba.playoff_max_deficit_comeback_rate.why: The only input that prices KXNBASERIESGCOMEBACK; series simulations and final-margin distributions cannot see a 30-point deficit that was erased.

nba.playoff_round_event_counts.label: Joint distribution of round-level series event counts (sweeps, upsets, Game 7s) and team playoff losses
nba.playoff_round_event_counts.mechanism: Counts of sweeps, upsets and Game 7s in a round, and a team's total playoff losses, are sums over series whose pairings depend on earlier rounds and whose outcomes share common shocks.
nba.playoff_round_event_counts.rationale: KXNBASWEEP, KXNBAUPSET, KXNBAGAME7, KXNBAPOLOSE and KXNBAUNBEATEN settle on counts or exact totals; multiplying independent series probabilities ignores that second-round pairings and seed gaps are random, and that league-wide shocks (injury waves, officiating emphasis) make concurrent series dependent, which fattens the tails of the count.
nba.playoff_round_event_counts.measurement: Simulate the full bracket 50,000 times from nba.title_path with per-game probabilities from the series model, including a common per-round shock to home-court advantage (sd estimated from 20 seasons of round-level home win rates); record per round the number of sweeps, upsets (higher numerical seed beats lower, post-Play-In seeds) and Game 7s, and per team the total losses and the 16-0 indicator; output the joint pmf and marginal P(count >= N), P(losses = k). As-of: nightly during the playoffs; before the playoffs from the seed distribution.
raw_data: playoff series results with seeds and game-by-game outcomes (20 seasons)
nba.playoff_round_event_counts.why: Prices the round-count and team-total contracts (sweeps, upsets, Game 7s, exact losses, 16-0) whose payoffs depend on the joint distribution across series.

nba.series_model.reason: Needed for home-games-hosted, Game 7, series-length, clinch-at-home, Finals exact score and undefeated contracts; game-to-game correlation and the venue sequence drive the series-path distribution.

nba.lineup_adj_rating.reason: Availability-adjusted strength moves per-game probabilities inside a series when a star is out; for Cup group games it matters only for the game-night active set.

nba.ratings.reason: Team strength drives per-game probabilities in every series and Cup game; a playoff-rotation version (top-8 health) is needed for series contracts, the regular-season version for the Cup.

nba.playoff_rotation.reason: Playoff minutes tightening raises star-heavy teams' per-game strength inside series; it shifts series-length and Game 7 probabilities but is second-order to team strength.

nba.injuries_pit.reason: Star availability moves seed, qualification and series odds; the vintage and expected return timeline are central.

nba.venue.reason: Home-court worth about 2-3 points per game is the sole structural asymmetry in the series and determines home playoff games; a fixed constant plus team-specific deviations, small.

nba.cup_format.reason: Cup group qualifier and group winner contracts are decided by the group tiebreak hierarchy and wildcard rules; but the input is a rule description and has to be turned into a state-aware simulation.

nba.rest_travel.reason: Rest between games in a series and Cup travel are second-order next to rating and availability; the series home/away pattern already encodes most of it.

nba.standings_motivation.reason: Seed, Play-In and qualifier series moved to season_futures_team; here end-of-season incentives only shape which pairings occur, and Cup group incentives are carried by nba.cup_group_tiebreak_state.

nba.title_path.reason: Bracket path determines which pairings occur in each round, and so the upset, sweep and Game 7 counts, team losses, home games hosted and the Cup pair; only context for a single named series.

nba.score_resid.reason: Defined as the residual of margin and total around closing lines, so it is a calibration of the book (market-derived) and must not be an input; the Cup point-differential tiebreak uses the market-free nba.single_game_margin_pmf instead.

m.quote_history.reason: A price path measures information arrival, not standings, series or bracket outcomes.

m.rules_text.reason: Seed contracts are defined before the play-in ('Results of Play-In games do not affect the outcome'); the exact definition changes the probability, and the other series rules are unknown.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook futures are the consensus comparison; not inputs to a model.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Coherence across seed thresholds (e.g. #10 or better, #8 or better) is a quote-quality diagnostic; model ladders are monotone by construction.

nba.draft_lottery_odds_table.reason: Built for KXNBATOP3 and the draft-pick-range series, which the reconciliation moved to awards_draft; no draft series remains in this archetype, so it is removed from stages, coverage, interactions, nonlinearities and feeds.

nba.pick_ownership_ledger.reason: Needed only for draft-position contracts, which the reconciliation moved to awards_draft; none of the 19 remaining series depends on pick ownership.

nba.prospect_slot_probability_model.reason: Built for KXNBADRAFTTOP5/10/15/20/30 and KXNBATOP5ROTY, all moved to awards_draft by the reconciliation; it remains a market-free definition for that archetype but has no contract here.

nba.playoff_triple_double_rate.reason: Built for KXNBAPLAYOFF3D, which the reconciliation moved to player_milestones; no playoff player-stat series remains in this archetype.

interactions.mechanism: A star injury during a series makes later-game outcomes positively correlated, so independent-game models overstate sweep probability and the chance of an undefeated run; a healthy and an injured regime have different per-game probabilities and the lengths differ accordingly.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare the distribution of series length conditional on a star injury during the series with an independent-game model.

interactions.mechanism: Group tiebreakers on point differential give incentives to run up scores in some games and rest stars in others; the value of margin is non-linear because it matters only if the team ends tied on record, and the probability of a tie depends on the state of the group.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the group with and without margin-based tiebreaks and compare qualification probabilities; check late-game garbage-time scoring when the margin matters.

interactions.mechanism: Total home games is a convex function of advancement because deep runs add rounds each with up to four home games, while early exits produce few; the distribution is right-skewed and its mean is dominated by the probability of reaching the third and fourth rounds.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare simulated home-games pmf by seed with historical outcomes.

interactions.mechanism: The pair probability is the product of two bracket-reach probabilities only after the groups are settled; before that, each team's path depends on which wildcard slots open, and a margin-driven tiebreak in one group can move a team into the other half of the bracket, changing which pairs are even possible.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate group stages with and without point-differential tiebreaks and compare each team's reach-final and East x West pair probabilities; check against past Cups that finalists have been one per conference and that same-conference pairs have never occurred (to be verified, not assumed).
interactions.hypothesis: The pair probability is the product of two conference bracket-reach probabilities: East and West halves are disjoint until the Hinkle final, so any East x West pair is possible and a same-conference pair is exactly zero. A group tiebreak cannot move a team into the other half; before the groups settle, what a margin-driven tiebreak changes is a team's seeding inside its own conference (group winner versus wild card, which sets who hosts the quarterfinal and semifinal), so reach probabilities move through home court and path difficulty and are correlated only for teams of the same conference.

interactions.mechanism: Clinch-at-home depends on the venue sequence: under 2-2-1-1-1 a higher-seed winner clinches at home only in games 5 or 7, a lower-seed winner only in games 4 or 6, so the probability is a path functional; a larger home-court edge makes home teams win more of their games, which lengthens series between even teams (more 2-2 and 3-3 states) and shifts clinches toward the higher seed's games 5 and 7.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare simulated series-length and clinch-location frequencies with a venue-free model on 20 seasons of playoff series, split by seed gap.

interactions.mechanism: If teams facing elimination play above their rating and teams up 3-0 relax, series lengthen and 2+ game comebacks become more frequent than independent games imply; the effect exists only in specific series states, so it shifts the tails of the sequence distribution, not the winner.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare observed frequencies of 6-7 game series and 0-2/1-3 comebacks over 25 seasons with an independent-games model and with the state-dependent model.

interactions.mechanism: A 40-point Finals margin is likelier in uneven matchups, which also end in fewer games, so the per-game tail and the number of games are negatively linked; treating them as independent overstates the blowout probability for lopsided Finals and understates it for even ones.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate Finals with per-game margins drawn from the same strength gap that sets series length and compare the union probability with the independent product on historical Finals.

interactions.mechanism: Second-round upset and sweep counts depend on which pairings survive round one: chalk first rounds produce even 1-4/2-3 matchups (few sweeps, few upsets by definition), while first-round upsets create mismatched or seed-inverted pairings, so round-two counts switch regime with round-one results.
interactions.how_to_test: Condition historical second-round sweep and upset counts on the number of first-round upsets and compare with unconditional rates.

nonlinearities.shape: multiplicative in two bracket-reach probabilities, with a zero floor for pairs in the same bracket half
nonlinearities.why: A specific pair needs both teams to win their halves; the pair probability is the product of two small numbers and is exactly zero for teams that the bracket places in the same half, so it is far more sensitive to bracket structure than either team's title odds.

nonlinearities.shape: product structure: undefeated-playoffs probability is a product of four sweep probabilities
nonlinearities.why: Each sweep needs about 60-80% for the favorite, so the product is a few percent; small errors in per-game probability multiply across 16 games.

nonlinearities.shape: inverted-U of P(7 games) in the per-game edge
nonlinearities.why: P(series reaches Game 7) is maximal (about 31%) when teams are even and falls steeply as the per-game edge grows, so Game 7 counts depend on how many even pairings the bracket produces, not on average strength.

contract.settlement_definition: Binary ladders on one player's official counts in the named game: blocks at or above N (e.g. 3+ blocks, floor_strike 2.5), steals at or above N (3+ steals) and combined steals plus blocks at or above N (4+, floor 3.5). Inactive players and players who never take the court settle at a fair price; once a player enters, the market settles on his recorded steals/blocks/combination. A postponed game that starts within 48 hours stays open, otherwise all markets resolve at a fair price. No turnover series is present in the ledger despite the archetype name; overtime treatment is not stated in the sampled text.

rules_evidence.quote: Once a player enters the game the market settles based on the player's blocks recorded.
rules_evidence.establishes: Block ladder settles on actual blocks once the player enters; no early-exit protection.

rules_evidence.quote: Once a player enters the game the market settles based on the player's steals recorded.
rules_evidence.establishes: Steal ladder settles on actual steals once the player enters.

rules_evidence.quote: This market resolves based on the number of combined steals and blocks recorded by Day'Ron Sharpe.
rules_evidence.establishes: Stocks contract counts the sum of steals and blocks, so the dependence between components matters.

variants_and_edge_cases: Strike construction: the sampled rungs are tails for the named players (Shai Gilgeous-Alexander 3+ blocks, Jrue Holiday 3+ steals), i.e. low-probability events in the 3-8% range, so dispersion and credit noise dominate the mean.
Combined stocks (4+, floor 3.5) is a sum of two overdispersed counts; the right-tail probability depends on the covariance and on archetype (a rim protector's stocks are mostly blocks).
Turnovers (the archetype name includes them) have no live series in the ledger, so a turnover contract's rules (assist-to-turnover, team turnovers) are unverified.

Overtime is not mentioned in the sampled rules; if the contract uses the official final box score, steals and blocks would include OT minutes (about five minutes in roughly 6% of games), but this is an assumption: the sampled rules do not say whether overtime counts (sbt-ot-inclusion).

Scope: no turnover series is live, so this record's inputs price steals, blocks and steals-plus-blocks only; any future player-turnover contract would need an own-turnover mechanism that is not defined here.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official box-score steals and blocks as named in the full rules; the sample is truncated before naming source agencies, so the exact source and correction policy are unverified.

mechanism.summary: Steals and blocks are rare counts (typically 0-3 per game) generated by a Poisson-like event process whose rate is the product of minutes, the supply of opportunities and the defender's conversion: steals need live-ball turnovers by opponents and the defender's deflection activity; blocks need opponent rim attempts while the defender is the rim anchor and his contest-to-block conversion. Both are overdispersed because supply varies by opponent style and lineup and because minutes are a mixture, and both carry an additional layer of noise from official-scorer credit decisions. At strikes of 0.5, 1.5 and 2.5 the probability depends more on dispersion and the tail of supply than on the mean, and the stocks contract sums two counts with archetype-specific dependence. The existing catalog uses generic matchup variables; the dominant missing pieces are hustle-based deflections, rim-protector supply, and the sum dependence.

stages.name: Participation and minutes mixture
stages.description: Low-count events scale with court time, so the minutes mixture sets the rate: a blowout cuts the starter's minutes but may raise bench players' attempts to press, and foul trouble affects aggressive defenders. Early exits settle on actual counts because the contract voids only inactive players.
stages.distribution: Mixture over minutes scenarios; the effect on a Poisson rate is multiplicative and dominates at the 2.5 strike.

stages.name: Supply of blockable shots and stealable turnovers
stages.description: Blocks require opponent shots at the rim contested by the player; the supply is the opponent's rim frequency while the player is on court and his share of contests. Steals require live-ball turnovers by opponents, with supply set by the opponent's careless handlers and style. Pace scales both supplies but is second-order to the opponent's shot and turnover mix.
stages.distribution: Supply counts overdispersed relative to Poisson with team-pair dependence (e.g. rim attempts per game vary with sd about 5 around a mean near 28).

stages.name: Defender conversion: deflections, contests and scheme
stages.description: The defender converts opportunities at a stable personal rate: steals per deflection and blocks per contest, modulated by scheme (blitz and zone raise deflections, drop coverage anchors the center near the rim). Rates are persistent but samples are small, so shrinkage towards role priors is needed.
stages.distribution: Thinned Poisson per opportunity with player-specific rates; sampling noise dominates a single-game count.

stages.name: Credit noise and dependence for stocks
stages.description: Official scorers decide steal and block credit, with arena-level tendencies and post-game video review corrections, which adds dispersion at the 0.5/1.5 strike. The stocks contract adds steals and blocks whose dependence differs by archetype: activity-driven for versatile wings, nearly independent for rim anchors.
stages.distribution: Count noise inflated by credit decisions (assumed extra dispersion index of 0.1-0.2 (hypothesis, unverified)); bivariate dependence with archetype-specific correlation 0-0.3.

stages.name: Threshold crossing and settlement
stages.description: The ladder rung is a threshold on an integer count with a small mean, so the probability of 3+ is a tail event highly sensitive to the dispersion assumption: a mean of 0.9 blocks gives 3+ probability of roughly 5% under Poisson and noticeably more with overdispersion. Settlement uses the official box score and refunds only inactive players.
stages.distribution: Tail of a negative binomial with mean 0.5-3; rung probabilities highly convex in the dispersion parameter.

talent_strength.note: Defender's persistent steal/block skill expressed as conversion of deflections and contests.

opponent_matchup.note: Opponent rim and live-ball turnover supply; the key matchup inputs.

role_personnel.note: Who is the rim anchor and who handles the ball for the opponent.

availability_news.note: Own and opposing handler and rim-protector status.

coaching_scheme.note: Pressure and drop schemes change gamble and rim-contest profile.

environment.note: Arena and altitude effects on steals and blocks are negligible beyond the scorer-credit effect handled under officiating; no separate environment variable is justified for these counts.

game_context_script.note: Blowout minutes changes and garbage-time pressing.

pace_volume.note: Opportunity counts scale with possessions but supply is more specific than pace.

efficiency_conversion.note: Conversion of deflections and contests to steals and blocks.

distribution_variance.note: Overdispersed counts and the dependence for the sum.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Back-to-back fatigue (lower activity) and minutes ramp-ups after injury affect deflection and contest effort but no input represents them; the size for low-count events is unknown.

officiating_rules.note: Credit decisions, corrections and foul environment.

settlement_contract.note: Fair-price void for inactive players; sum for stocks; no early-exit protection.

nba.deflection_rate.label: Deflections and steal-conversion rate per 36 minutes (hustle stats)
nba.deflection_rate.mechanism: A steal is a conversion of a deflection or a pass interception; deflections are a more stable measure of defensive activity than steals and predict future steals better than past steals do.
nba.deflection_rate.rationale: Steal counts are 0-3 per game with huge sampling noise; a player's deflection rate and his conversion rate (steals per deflection) separate persistent skill from luck and respond to scheme (gamble-heavy teams generate more of both).
nba.deflection_rate.measurement: Per player over the last 2 seasons (45-game half-life, games before tip only): deflections per 36 minutes with prior weight 500 minutes toward the position mean; steals per deflection shrunk to the league mean (about 0.20, re-estimated each season) with prior weight 80 deflections. Expected steals per minute = deflection rate per minute * shrunk conversion * (opponent live-ball turnovers per 100 / league average, itself shrunk with 20 games), capped at 2x the unadjusted value. As-of: games completed before tip.
free_sources: nba_api hustle stats (leaguehustlestatsplayer, game-level boxscorehustlev2; SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for per-game availability)
raw_data: Hustle: deflections, steals, minutes per game
nba.deflection_rate.why: Gives a stabler, scheme-aware rate for the 0.5/1.5/2.5 steal rungs than season steals per minute. Role lowered to secondary: per-game vintages of hustle and rim-defense data are SOURCE_UNVERIFIED (sbt-hustle-access) and may exist only as season aggregates or paid tracking.

nba.rim_contest_volume_on_court.label: Opponent rim attempts faced while the player is the on-court rim protector, and contest/block rate
nba.rim_contest_volume_on_court.mechanism: Blocks equal opponent rim attempts faced times the player's contest share times block rate per contest, so block supply depends on who is the anchor and how many shots the opponent takes at the rim while he is on court.
nba.rim_contest_volume_on_court.rationale: Total FGA or team pace is a poor supply measure: a drop-coverage center faces 20+ rim attempts, a switching center fewer; opponent rim frequency while the player is on court, and the share of contests that are his, move block expectation more than his season blocks per minute.
nba.rim_contest_volume_on_court.measurement: Per player and season-to-date (games before tip): opponent rim attempts faced per 100 on-court possessions = rim FGA allowed while on court / on-court possessions x 100 (PBPStats on/off or dashboard), contest share = his rim contests / team rim contests when on court, block rate per contest = blocks / contests, each shrunk to the role prior with k=150 contests. Projection for tonight = (opponent rim FGA per 100 against teams with similar pace/style) x projected possessions while on court (nba.minutes x game possessions/48) /100 x contest share x block rate; do not multiply by minutes share again. Adjust the opponent rate when another rim protector is out. As-of: tipoff, injury vintage.
free_sources: nba_api defensive dashboard (shots defended at rim, SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for per-game)
raw_data: defense dashboard: DFGA at rim, contests, blocks per player (date-window splits)
nba.rim_contest_volume_on_court.why: Gives the supply side of blocks with the relevant matchup, which pace and total shots miss. Role lowered to secondary: per-game vintages of hustle and rim-defense data are SOURCE_UNVERIFIED (sbt-hustle-access) and may exist only as season aggregates or paid tracking.

nba.live_ball_turnover_profile.label: Opponent live-ball turnover rate and primary handler carelessness
nba.live_ball_turnover_profile.mechanism: Steals mostly come from live-ball turnovers (bad passes, dribbles stripped); the opponent's rate of live-ball versus dead-ball turnovers and the quality of its primary handlers set steal supply.
nba.live_ball_turnover_profile.rationale: Total opponent turnovers per game include offensive fouls, shot-clock and out-of-bounds events that cannot be stolen; the live-ball share and the primary handler's turnover rate are the supply for the steal contract.
nba.live_ball_turnover_profile.measurement: From play-by-play classify opponent turnovers as live-ball (steal-credited or bad-pass) or dead-ball; compute live-ball turnovers per 100 possessions for the opponent over last 40 games (half-life 20), shrink to league mean with prior weight 20 games; add the turnover rate of the expected primary ball handlers (from lineup) and adjust for opponent's pace. As-of: injury report.
raw_data: PBP turnover types, steal credit, lineups
nba.live_ball_turnover_profile.why: Targets the portion of opponent turnovers that a defender can steal.

nba.stocks_dependence_by_archetype.label: Dependence between steals and blocks for combined stocks, by player archetype
nba.stocks_dependence_by_archetype.mechanism: Combined steals+blocks sums two counts whose dependence depends on defensive archetype: wings with deflection-based steals and bigs with rim blocks have small correlation, while versatile defenders have positive correlation through minutes and activity.
nba.stocks_dependence_by_archetype.rationale: The 4+ stocks rung needs the distribution of the sum; assuming independence or perfect minutes-driven correlation misstates variance, and the covariance is archetype specific.
nba.stocks_dependence_by_archetype.measurement: Compute the within-player correlation of steal and block counts after controlling for minutes (Pearson on Pearson residuals) over 3 seasons by archetype (guard, wing, forward, center), with Fisher-z shrinkage to archetype mean (prior weight 60 games); model sum distribution via bivariate negative-binomial or Gaussian copula with these parameters; output P(S+B >= k) for k=2..6.
nba.stocks_dependence_by_archetype.why: Provides the dependence parameter needed for KXNBASTOCK that the independent components cannot.

nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.label: Ratings-based blowout probability and starter-minutes-vs-margin curve (market-free)
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.mechanism: Rebuilds the blowout risk from team strength and rotation history instead of the closing spread: a ratings-implied expected margin and margin spread give P(large lead), and a coach/player minutes-versus-margin curve converts each margin path into expected minutes lost by starters and gained by bench players.
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.rationale: The catalog input nba.garbage is defined from the closing spread, which is a market price and so a benchmark, not an input. The causal quantity is the chance that the margin passes the coach's pull threshold early enough to matter, and how much playing time each player then loses. Subtle: the loss depends on when the lead arrives (a 20-point lead entering Q4 removes far more starter minutes than one reached with 3 minutes left), on the coach, and on whether the trailing team also pulls starters, so the curve must be conditional on the margin path and not only on the final margin.
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.measurement: Step 1, expected margin: mu = (NetRtg_home_adj - NetRtg_away_adj) * expected_possessions/100 + home_adv, where NetRtg_adj is the as-of-tipoff opponent-adjusted net rating from nba.off_rtg and nba.def_rtg (ridge regression on game point differential, half-life about 25 games, shrunk to the preseason prior with n_prior about 20 games as a placeholder to be fitted), adjusted for the confirmed unavailable players via nba.lineup_adj_rating, home_adv fitted on the last 5 seasons (about 2 points). Step 2, margin spread: sd_margin fitted on 5 seasons of residuals of final margin versus mu (league-wide roughly 12-13 points, to be estimated, with a heavier empirical tail than normal). Step 3: P(final |margin| >= 15/20/25) and P(|lead| >= 15/20 entering Q4) from the empirical residual distribution around mu. Step 4, minutes curve: from play-by-play stints, per team-season, expected minutes of each rotation player conditional on margin entering Q4 in bins (0-9, 10-14, 15-19, 20+), shrunk toward the league curve with k about 30 blowout games. Output per player: expected minutes lost and the probability of falling below a stated minutes level. No closing line or other price is used; the spread is retained only to benchmark calibration of step 3.
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com leaguegamelog (team game logs, free, undocumented, rate-limited)
cdn.nba.com liveData playbyplay JSON (substitutions with score, free, unofficial)
Basketball-Reference game logs and play-by-play (free, polite scraping)
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.why: Steals and blocks are low-count events that scale with minutes, so starter minutes lost in a blowout move the mean and the zero mass directly.
raw_data: team-game final margins and opponent-adjusted ratings as of tipoff (5 seasons)
play-by-play substitution stints with margin entering Q4

nba.minutes.reason: Low-count events scale with court time; for blocks the minutes that matter are those alongside particular opponents' rim attackers, and a blowout cut matters little at a 0.5 strike but a lot at 2.5.

nba.steal_block_rates.reason: Per-minute rates are stable for blocks and moderately stable for steals; but the label bundles the player's own skill with opponent turnover and rim-attempt rates, which should be separated to be measured.

nba.turnover_pressure.reason: Ball-handling load and opponent pressure are the two halves of turnovers; deflections are the best proxy for pressure but need a hustle-stat source; no turnover series appears in the ledger, so this input mostly serves steals through opponent carelessness.

nba.usage.reason: Touches and usage scale turnovers for the player; for steals and blocks it is irrelevant, so should only be attached to the turnover form.

nba.opp_def_pos.reason: Allowed-by-position tables for turnovers and rim attempts blend scheme, pace and the individual opponent's role; noise dominates at the 1-3 count scale.

nba.def_scheme.reason: Blitz, zone and full-court pressure change gamble rates and so steals and deflections; drop coverage keeps the big at the rim and increases blocks; categorical labels need the player's role interaction.

nba.pace.reason: Possessions scale all events, but for blocks the relevant volume is opponent rim attempts and for steals opponent live-ball turnovers; pace is second-order.

nba.shot_profile.reason: Opponent rim attempts and rim share are the supply for blocks; stronger than pace and total FGA, and should be matched to the blocker's rim-protection minutes.

nba.scorer_bias.reason: Arena-level credit for steals and blocks has documented home-side tendencies; effect is modest but adds dispersion at 0.5-1.5 strikes; the size estimated by arena needs many seasons.

nba.garbage.reason: Catalog definition is "blowout probability from spread", a closing-line quantity, so it is a market benchmark and not an input. Removed from stages, coverage, interactions and data feeds; replaced by the market-free nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve built from ratings and rotation history. Prior note: Minutes loss in blowouts matters; but steals can rise in garbage time when bench players press, so sign is role dependent; rebuild from ratings not the spread.

nba.foul_rates.reason: Aggressive shot-blockers pick up fouls and sit; the real link is the interaction with block attempts, not a standalone effect.

nba.injuries_pit.reason: Availability of own rim anchors (who else blocks shots) and of the opponent's ball handlers changes event supply directly; vintage matters.

nba.stat_dist.reason: Overdispersed Poisson with minutes mixture is the right base, and for 0.5/1.5/2.5 strikes the dispersion matters more than the mean.

m.quote_history.reason: Price path is market state, not a driver of steals or blocks.

m.rules_text.reason: Rules fix that inactive players are voided at a fair price while entering players settle on actual counts; the stocks contract sums two categories.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook prop lines are benchmarks, not inputs; low-count lines are a favourite-longshot battleground.

m.strike_hit_rates.reason: Realised frequency by rung is calibration history; for these low-count events the rung hit-rates are the main reality check of dispersion.

nba.market_calibration_bias.reason: A Kalshi-specific overlay on probabilities, not an input to steals and blocks production.

m.volume_oi.reason: Open interest has no mechanism link to blocks or steals and mostly tracks popularity of the player.

m.trade_tape.reason: Order flow is market microstructure; no causal content for the count process.

m.settlement_truth.reason: Settled values are labels; for steals and blocks the official score sheet credit decisions make reconciliation necessary.

nba.stat_corrections.reason: Block and steal credits are among the most frequently revised box-score items after video review; matters for exact-threshold outcomes.

nba.late_game_script.reason: Intentional fouling affects free throws more than steals and blocks; minor effect here, retained only as context.

interactions.mechanism: Mean events equal rate times minutes, but rung probability at 2.5 or 3.5 is convex in the mean for a low-count process, so a small minutes increase raises the tail probability proportionally more than the mean; the effect is largest for a player whose mean sits near 1.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute P(count >= k) over minutes bins for fixed per-minute rate and compare with Poisson and negative binomial tails.

interactions.mechanism: A rim protector who contests aggressively both blocks more and fouls more, so the same behaviour that raises block supply raises foul-trouble risk and minute loss; this makes blocks and minutes negatively dependent in the tail.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate correlation between block count and minutes shortfall in games where the player had >=3 first-half fouls.

interactions.mechanism: A blitz or full-court scheme raises opponent live-ball turnovers only against careless handlers; against a low-turnover primary handler the extra pressure yields deflections without steals, so the effect of scheme on steals is conditional on the opponent handler's turnover rate.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact opponent handler turnover rate with scheme labels in a Poisson regression on team steals.

interactions.mechanism: Official-scorer credit adds count noise and an arena-specific shift of a few percent of rate (both unverified), which matters most where the count distribution is dense near the threshold: a rate shift of a few percent moves P(3+) for a mean near 1 much more than for a mean near 0.3, so the effect is a mean shift whose impact depends on the distribution shape, not only extra dispersion.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate arena fixed effects on steal and block rates (mean shift) and separately on dispersion over 5 seasons, and check whether the mean shift moves rung hit rates by the amount the shape of the count distribution implies.

interactions.mechanism: The stocks sum has variance equal to the sum of variances plus twice the covariance; for versatile wings positive covariance raises the 4+ tail relative to independent components, while rim anchors have near-zero covariance.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare P(S+B >= 4) from independent components versus a copula by archetype against realised frequencies.

nonlinearities.shape: convex tail probability in the dispersion parameter
nonlinearities.why: At mean about 1 the probability of 3+ rises from roughly 8% to 12% when the negative-binomial dispersion index moves from 1.0 to 1.4, so rung probability is more sensitive to dispersion than to a 10% change in the mean.

nonlinearities.shape: saturating: shrinkage weight toward the role prior is large
nonlinearities.why: Per-minute rates for steals have a small signal-to-noise ratio across games, so predicted rates should pull strongly toward the role mean; the effective weight on a player's own rate is below 50% for a full season of data.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold at 3-4 fouls triggering benching
nonlinearities.why: For aggressive shot-blockers minutes fall sharply once fouls reach a coach's threshold, so the effect on blocks is a step in minutes rather than a smooth function of the foul rate.
