contract.settlement_definition: The only live series is KXNBAPLAYOFFPTS (NBA Playoffs Player Points): YES if the named player records at least N points (sample: Paolo Banchero, 50) in any single playoff game of the 2026 Pro Basketball Playoffs; points are not summed across games. It is a union over the player's playoff games, so a player whose team misses the playoffs, or who is eliminated or injured before reaching N, simply runs out of chances. The text states no fair-price void for an inactive or traded player, does not say whether Play-In games are playoff games or whether overtime points count, and names no source agency.

rules_evidence.quote: If Paolo Banchero records at least 50 points in any playoff game in the 2026 Pro Basketball Playoffs, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: The event is a single playoff game with 50+ points by the named player at any point of the playoffs: a union over his playoff games, not a per-game ladder.

rules_evidence.quote: Cumulative stats across multiple games will not be considered.
rules_evidence.establishes: Totals or averages across the run are irrelevant; only the maximum single-game score matters, so the upper tail of the per-game points distribution drives the price.

variants_and_edge_cases: Strike: the sample uses 50 points (title '50+ points in a single game'); other players or editions may carry other N, and the per-game tail probability falls steeply with N.
Play-In: the text says 'any playoff game'; other NBA series exclude the Play-In explicitly, so a 50-point Play-In game probably does not count, but this is not stated here.
Overtime: not mentioned; official box-score points include overtime, which adds about five minutes for stars in roughly 6% of playoff games.
No void: unlike single-game player props, there is no fair-price settlement for an inactive player; an injured star loses games and the contract settles No if he never reaches N.
The sampled contract concerns the completed 2026 playoffs (status finalized); the mechanism applies unchanged to later editions, with the player list and strikes read per edition.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official playoff box scores (points per player per game); the sampled text names no source agency.

mechanism.summary: A single-game 50-point playoff performance needs three things at once: the player's team must be in the playoffs and keep playing (the number of games is set by qualification, Play-In and series advancement), the player must be on the floor for a full playoff workload, and one of those games must land deep in his scoring tail. Per-game P(50+) is a generalised-Pareto tail of points given minutes, usage, three-point volume and free-throw trips, pulled down in the playoffs by slower pace, tighter officiating and opponents who scheme a whole series against the star, and pushed up by longer star minutes and teammate absences that concentrate usage. The contract value is 1 - E[prod over games (1 - p_g)], with the games count and the star's health positively linked.

stages.name: Team playoff games available to the player
stages.description: The opportunity set is the number of playoff games the player's team plays: zero if it misses the playoffs or loses in the Play-In, four to seven per series, up to 28 for a finalist. It comes from the regular-season standings simulation, the Play-In bracket for seeds 7-10, and series-by-series advancement and length; deeper runs add the most games for the strongest teams, which also employ the most likely 50-point scorers.
stages.distribution: Lumpy on {0, 4..28}: point mass at zero for non-qualifiers, then sums of series lengths over rounds reached; right-skewed for contenders.

stages.name: Star availability through the playoff run
stages.description: The player has to be healthy for the games his team plays. A survival-type hazard of an availability-ending injury runs from the end of the regular season through each round, and a star playing through an injury carries a minutes restriction that removes him from the 50-point tail even when active. His health also moves his team's advancement, so games played and availability are positively dependent.
stages.distribution: Per-round probability of being healthy, decreasing over the run; bimodal per-game state (full workload versus out or restricted).

stages.name: Playoff minutes and usage regime
stages.description: Playoff rotations tighten to eight or nine players and stars gain two to four minutes, with 44+ minute nights in overtime or elimination games. Usage concentrates further when a co-star is out. Blowouts still truncate minutes, so lopsided series cut the tail. The relevant quantity is the probability of a heavy-minutes, high-usage game, not the average minutes.
stages.distribution: Minutes mixture with a heavy-minutes component (40+) whose weight rises in close and elimination games; usage shifts as a step when a teammate is absent.

stages.name: Single-game scoring tail against playoff defense
stages.description: Given a full workload, P(points >= 50) is the far tail of the per-game distribution: a generalised-Pareto exceedance over a high threshold fit on the player's history, raised by three-point volume and free-throw trips and lowered by the series opponent's primary defender, slower playoff pace and fewer fouls called. Single-game shooting is mostly luck, so the tail index must be shrunk to a league value; overtime adds a small extra chance.
stages.distribution: Heavy right tail: GPD above about 35 points with a shrunk shape parameter; per-game P(50+) typically 0.1-2% for the top scorers, near zero for others.

stages.name: Union over the run and settlement
stages.description: The contract pays if the maximum single-game score over the player's playoff games reaches N. With per-game probability p_g and a random number of games, P(YES) = 1 - E[prod (1 - p_g)], where the expectation runs jointly over team advancement, the player's health and a shared latent form factor that makes his per-game tails correlated within a run. No void applies, and Play-In and overtime treatment follow the open contract questions.
stages.distribution: Concave in the number of games; for small p roughly p x E[games played]; dependence through form and matchup makes the union smaller than the independent formula.

talent_strength.note: Player scoring ceiling and team strength for advancement.

opponent_matchup.note: Primary-defender effect within a series and which opponents the bracket produces.

role_personnel.note: Usage concentration and playoff rotation tightening.

availability_news.note: Health through each round and game-day status.

coaching_scheme.note: Opponent game plans against a hot scorer (blitzing pick-and-rolls, early doubles) and a coach's willingness to ride a star for 45+ minutes change the 50-point tail, but no input measures them.

environment.note: Home/away scoring differences for individual stars are about one point and are absorbed in the per-game distribution; no venue or travel variable moves a 50-point tail measurably.

game_context_script.note: Blowout truncation, overtime chance and heavy-minutes games.

pace_volume.note: Playoff pace per game and the number of playoff games.

efficiency_conversion.note: Shooting luck shrinkage and free-throw trips.

distribution_variance.note: Per-game tail shape and the union over a random number of correlated games.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Play-In path to qualification; elimination games raise star minutes.

officiating_rules.note: Free-throw trips under playoff officiating, which calls fewer fouls than the regular season.

settlement_contract.note: Single game, any playoff game, no cumulation, no stated void; Play-In and OT open.

nba.ratings.label: Team ratings / schedule strength for season markets
nba.ratings.mechanism: A season-level team rating (net rating plus roster talent plus health) feeds simulations for wins, seed, series and title.
nba.ratings.rationale: Season markets require a rating that combines prior-season performance, roster changes, current-season results and injury information; single-season net rating has meaningful luck variance. Subtle: ratings should reflect playoff-relevant strength (top-8 rotation health) rather than regular-season depth for title/series markets, and be uncertainty-aware.
nba.ratings.measurement: Team rating R_t(as-of) = posterior mean and sd from a Kalman-style update: prior = nba.preseason_roster_aging_prior (mean, sd); each completed game g updates with observed margin (capped at 15 after garbage-time exclusion, opponent and home-adjusted using the opponent's rating at game time) with gain w(n) from nba.rating_update_gain; roster-change adjustment = sum over minutes-weighted net change in nba.player_impact for players in/out since the last game. Produce two versions: regular-season (full rotation) and playoff (top-8 rotation, minutes from nba.playoff_rotation). Output mean and sd per team. As-of: games completed before the as-of time. Use only public non-price data; no market-implied rating.
free_sources: DARKO (darko.app, free web view; no official API)
Dunks & Threes EPM (free partial; no official API)
nba.ratings.why: Team strength sets qualification and advancement, and therefore how many playoff games the player gets.

nba.playoff_any_game_threshold_union.label: Probability a player reaches N points in at least one playoff game (union over a random, correlated run)
nba.playoff_any_game_threshold_union.mechanism: A playoff-long single-game threshold pays on the maximum game score over a random number of games whose length depends on advancement and the player's own health, with per-game tails correlated through form and matchup.
nba.playoff_any_game_threshold_union.rationale: Multiplying a regular-season per-game tail by expected games overstates the price: playoff pace and defense compress the tail, the number of games is zero with positive probability, health and advancement are linked, and a series against one elite defender correlates several games. The union must be computed jointly, not from marginals.
nba.playoff_any_game_threshold_union.measurement: Simulate 20,000 playoff runs: draw the team's qualification and series path from the bracket simulation (nba.title_path, nba.series_length_distribution, nba.play_in_path_model), the player's availability per game from nba.playoff_star_health_hazard, a run-level form factor (log-normal, sd fitted from the player's game-to-game residual autocorrelation, about 0.1), and per-game p_g = P(points >= N) from nba.single_game_ceiling_tail rescaled by playoff minutes (nba.playoff_rotation) and opponent defender shift (nba.playoff_matchup_assignment_shift); P(YES) = share of runs with at least one game >= N. Validate on historical playoff 40+ and 50+ games (rates too low for 50 alone). As-of: nightly from the end of the regular season.
raw_data: player-game logs (points, minutes, FGA, 3PA, FTA) regular season and playoffs
upstream model outputs: series path, availability, per-game tail
nba.playoff_any_game_threshold_union.why: The settlement functional of KXNBAPLAYOFFPTS; without it per-game tails and the games count are never combined.

nba.playoff_star_health_hazard.label: Time-resolved probability that each rotation star is healthy for each playoff round
nba.playoff_star_health_hazard.mechanism: Title and conference odds are convex in star availability, and the relevant availability is in April-June, not the regular-season games-missed average.
nba.playoff_star_health_hazard.rationale: Games-missed expectations average over a season; the quantity that matters for round-reach contracts is the probability of being healthy at tip of each playoff series, which depends on current injury state, history, age and minutes load.
nba.playoff_star_health_hazard.measurement: For each player in the top-3 of each contender (by minutes x impact) fit a discrete-time hazard (logistic per game) for the event 'misses the next game with an injury-coded absence' on 10 seasons of regular-season and playoff data, covariates: age, prior-season games missed, minutes per game, current report status (none/probable/questionable/doubtful/out) from the as-of vintage, days since last injury absence. Output P(available at game 1 of the playoffs) and P(available for the first game of round k | available at the start) by chaining per-game survival over the expected playoff games, plus the expected strength loss = impact x minutes share. Shrink player-specific intercepts to the age bucket mean with k=40 games. As-of: latest injury report vintage; never use post-hoc game logs for the current state.
raw_data: injury report vintages (official report 2021-22 onward, Pro Sports Transactions earlier)
player age, minutes, games missed by season
nba.playoff_star_health_hazard.why: The named star must be healthy in each round he would play; his health also drives his team's advancement.

nba.series_length_distribution.label: Series-length distribution from per-game win probabilities
nba.series_length_distribution.mechanism: The number of games in a best-of-seven series is a function of per-game win probability, home pattern and dependence between games; this is the per-series kernel that nba.title_path calls inside each bracket draw.
nba.series_length_distribution.rationale: KXNBASERIESGAMES counts games, not points; the draft has no input for it except a generic series model reference outside the archetype.
nba.series_length_distribution.measurement: Per-series kernel: P(series ends in k games) by dynamic programming over home pattern 2-2-1-1-1 with per-game win probabilities from own-model playoff ratings and a series dependence parameter (game-to-game correlation about +0.05 on margin, estimated from 2000-2025 playoff series), injuries as of the as-of date; output P(4..7) and P(win). For a set matchup this is used directly; for bracket-level contracts the same kernel is evaluated inside nba.title_path draws, so lengths and advancement are consistent across archetypes.
raw_data: playoff series results by game with venue
own team ratings and injury status
nba.series_length_distribution.why: Series lengths per round give the number of games, the volume over which the 50-point tail compounds.

nba.title_path.label: Playoff bracket path, matchup and home-court structure
nba.title_path.mechanism: Series winner and title probabilities depend on the bracket path (seed, opponent strength, home-court) and matchup-specific adjustments.
nba.title_path.rationale: Title odds are the product of series-win probabilities along a path that depends on which seed you are, who you face and the rest/injury states. A given team's path difficulty can differ substantially even for equal rating. Subtle: series outcomes are correlated through injuries to key players across rounds.
nba.title_path.measurement: Shared playoff bracket simulation for the bracket-level consumers attached to it (season_futures_team, series_and_cup, player_milestones for KXNBAPLAYOFF3D, the playoff single-game points archetype, awards_draft and parlay_combo): 50,000 draws; seeds from nba.standings_sim paths, play-in from nba.play_in_path_model, each series simulated game by game with the per-series kernel of nba.series_length_distribution (p_g from playoff ratings, 2-2-1-1-1 home court, injury state, series dependence); store per-path series lengths, venues and advancement so these consumers read the same draws. Single-series contracts whose matchup is already set (series cumulative points, per-series length markets) use the kernel directly; it equals title_path's conditional for that series. Output P(reach round r), P(title), opponents and games played per team. As-of: nightly.
nba.title_path.why: Advancement through the bracket sets how many rounds, and so how many games, the player gets.

nba.play_in_path_model.label: Play-in bracket path probabilities given pre-play-in seed and relative strength
nba.play_in_path_model.mechanism: The play-in tournament maps seeds 7-10 to final seeds 7 and 8 through a fixed bracket, so the playoff qualification and the post-play-in seed differ from the regular-season seed; Kalshi's seed contracts are measured before the play-in.
nba.play_in_path_model.rationale: KXNBASEEDOU resolves on the regular-season seed before the play-in while qualification/play-in series depend on play-in outcomes; the same team has different probabilities for 'seed 8 or better' depending on which definition applies.
nba.play_in_path_model.measurement: Encode the bracket (7v8 winner gets the 7 seed; 9v10 loser is out; loser of 7v8 plays winner of 9v10 for the 8 seed), compute per-game win probabilities with home-court from team ratings and rest, and convolve to P(final seed 7, 8, out | pre-play-in seed, opponents); estimate the distribution of opponents from the standings simulation. As-of: nightly; rules versioned by season.
raw_data: Standings and seeds before the Play-In
nba.play_in_path_model.why: Players on teams finishing 7-10 reach the playoffs only through the Play-In, whose games probably do not count for this contract.

nba.playoff_rotation.label: Playoff rotation tightening and minutes inflation
nba.playoff_rotation.mechanism: Playoff games feature shorter rotations and higher starter minutes, changing player props and team-level ratings relative to the regular season.
nba.playoff_rotation.rationale: Stars play several more minutes per game and bench depth matters less; regular-season minutes baselines understate playoff volume for starters and overstate bench contributions. Subtle: the effect varies by round and by series pace/blowout probability.
nba.playoff_rotation.measurement: For each player-season with >=20 regular-season games and a playoff series, compute the ratio r = playoff minutes per game / regular-season minutes per game (regular season through the last 20 games to avoid rest-game noise), pooled by role bucket (top-3 minutes, other starters, rotation, bench) and round, 2010-present, with shrinkage of player r to the bucket mean at k=8 playoff games. Team rotation depth = number of players averaging >=12 minutes in the series, versus regular season. Output for each player: expected playoff minutes = projected regular-season minutes x r_bucket,round with sd, conditioned on series pace and blowout probability from own-model margin. As-of: games before tip; regular-season baseline fixed at season end.
free_sources: cdn.nba.com liveData JSON (boxscore, playbyplay, odds; free, unofficial)
raw_data: player-game minutes regular season and playoffs, starter flag
nba.playoff_rotation.why: Star minutes inflation in the playoffs widens the scoring tail that a 50-point game needs.

nba.points_upper_tail_rate.label: Player-specific upper-tail frequency of points given full-minutes games (ceiling-game rate)
nba.points_upper_tail_rate.mechanism: Scoring has a heavier right tail than a negative binomial fit to the mean implies because hot shooting, FT surges and OT stack; the cubic escalator weights this tail heavily.
nba.points_upper_tail_rate.rationale: The scalar escalator pays (y/50)^3 so its expected value is dominated by 35+ outcomes; a model calibrated to the mean misprices it, and the 30+/40+ rungs depend on the same tail.
nba.points_upper_tail_rate.measurement: For each player estimate exceedance probabilities P(pts >= 1.4m), P(pts >= 1.7m) and P(pts>=2.0m) where m is the minutes-conditional mean, on games with >=30 minutes over a 3-season window; fit a generalised-Pareto above the 85th percentile of residuals with shape shrunk to a league-wide value (prior weight 60 exceedances). Output the tail index and exceedance rates.
nba.points_upper_tail_rate.why: Player-specific exceedance rates relative to his mean give a second estimate of the far tail that the ceiling model extrapolates.

nba.heavy_minutes_tail_prob.label: Probability of heavy-minutes games (38+ minutes, OT)
nba.heavy_minutes_tail_prob.mechanism: The extreme counts come from nights with heavy minutes, whose probability depends on game closeness, depth and the coach's usage of the star.
nba.heavy_minutes_tail_prob.rationale: A single projected minutes figure hides the 10-20% of nights with 38+ minutes that produce the top bands, and nights with 20-25 minutes that produce the bottom ones.
nba.heavy_minutes_tail_prob.measurement: Per player: share of games with minutes >= 38 over the last 80 games (half-life 30), shrunk to role prior with k=15 games; condition on own-model closeness (P(|margin| < 8) from the margin model) and OT probability 0.06; produce P(minutes >= 38) and mean count in that regime = rate per minute x 40; as-of lineup status.
nba.heavy_minutes_tail_prob.why: 50-point games almost always come with 38+ minutes; this gives the weight of that regime in playoff games.

nba.playoff_matchup_assignment_shift.label: Playoff matchup assignment shift (primary defender effect)
nba.playoff_matchup_assignment_shift.mechanism: In a series the primary defenders assigned to stars shift counts relative to regular-season rates, adjusted game by game.
nba.playoff_matchup_assignment_shift.rationale: Regular-season position-based opponent allowances miss the specific defender and the series adaptation. The 5-15% shift magnitude is SOURCE_UNVERIFIED (recalled, not estimated).
nba.playoff_matchup_assignment_shift.measurement: For each offensive player O and defender D in the same season compute points per 100 partial possessions guarded (matchup table, min 50 possessions), shrunk to D's overall defensive effect with k=100 possessions and to O's season rate. Series assignment share s_D = 0.5 x share of O's matchup possessions D took in regular-season meetings between the two teams (pooled across seasons if rosters unchanged) + 0.5 x share in playoff games to date (weight rises with games played). Shift = sum_D s_D x (shrunk matchup rate - O's baseline per-100 rate), reported in points and assists per 100, with a standard error from possession counts. Update after each series game with a 2-game half-life; as-of: games completed before tip. Treat the shift as noisy and cap its weight with an out-of-sample test.
raw_data: leagueseasonmatchups: offensive player, defensive player, partial possessions, player points, assists, FGM/FGA allowed
nba.playoff_matchup_assignment_shift.why: A series-long primary defender compresses the star's tail for four to seven correlated games.

nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.label: Own-model regulation tie probability P(OT)
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.mechanism: P(OT) = mass of regulation margin at zero from a heteroscedastic margin density with a late-game excess-mass correction.
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.rationale: The draft claims P(OT) is roughly flat across spreads, but a Gaussian with sd 12 gives 3.3% at pick-em and 2.3% at 10 points, so the dependence on spread is large; the right model is a decreasing function with an empirical excess factor.
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.measurement: P_gauss(0) = phi(mu/sigma)/sigma with mu own-model margin and sigma from own ratings and pace (nba.lineup_adj_rating and nba.pace; about 12, scaling with sqrt(possessions)); multiply by excess factor kappa(|mu|) estimated by isotonic regression on 10 seasons of games as observed OT rate divided by P_gauss(0) in |mu| buckets of 2 points; kappa about 1.7-1.9 overall; output with beta interval; use own-model mu, not closing lines. Margin is integer-valued with parity tied to the total, and free-throw, three-point and intentional-foul structure moves mass onto and off zero, so estimate the observed integer pmf at 0 (and smoothed mass at +/-1 to +/-4) over 15 seasons and let kappa(|mu|) absorb the discreteness rather than reading the continuous density at zero.
raw_data: team-game regulation and final scores with period counts (15 seasons)
own-model expected margin and sd per game
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.why: Overtime adds about five minutes and a small extra chance of 50; market-free probability of a regulation tie.

nba.stat_dist.reason: The body of the per-game points distribution (overdispersed count) anchors the tail threshold; the 50-point exceedance itself comes from the ceiling model.

nba.minutes.reason: Minutes are the scale of every scoring chance, but must be re-based to playoff rotations and their heavy-minutes regime, not regular-season projections.

nba.usage.reason: Shot and free-throw share per possession is the second driver of a 50-point game; it rises when a co-star is out.

nba.pace.reason: Playoff pace runs a few possessions below the regular season, lowering per-game scoring chances for every player.

nba.opp_def_pos.reason: Regular-season positional allowances average over many opponents; a playoff series is one opponent with a planned primary defender, handled by nba.playoff_matchup_assignment_shift.

nba.three_volume.reason: Three-point attempt volume raises both the mean and the variance of points, and most modern 50-point games include many made threes.

nba.player_shooting_regression.reason: A hot regular-season shooting stretch inflates a naive tail; single-game and seasonal percentages must be shrunk to talent.

nba.injuries_pit.reason: Game-day status and restrictions decide whether a given playoff game is a full-workload chance at all.

nba.rotation.reason: Regular-season rotation patterns are superseded in the playoffs by tightened rotations captured in nba.playoff_rotation.

nba.single_game_ceiling_tail.reason: Per-game generalised-Pareto exceedance of 50+ points (with overtime adjustment) is the core per-game probability; it needs a playoff rescaling.

nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.reason: Lopsided playoff games cut star minutes in the fourth quarter, removing 50-point chances; market-free margin-to-minutes curve.

nba.preseason_roster_aging_prior.reason: Before the season ends it feeds the team strength that sets qualification and advancement; once the bracket is set it adds nothing.

nba.milestone_rates.reason: Double- and triple-double base rates do not enter a points-only threshold; the playoff triple-double series is priced in player_milestones. Detached from this archetype by archetype patch.

nba.combo_covariance.reason: Covariance between points, rebounds and assists has no role in a points-only playoff threshold. Detached from this archetype by archetype patch.

nba.avg_rounding_and_games_state.reason: Season-average rounding belongs to KXNBASTATAVG in season_stat_markets; no average enters a single-game playoff threshold. Detached from this archetype by archetype patch.

nba.team_win_streak_hazard.reason: Team win-streak hazard belongs to KXNBAWINSTREAK in season_stat_markets; it has no role in a player points threshold. Detached from this archetype by archetype patch.

nba.undefeated_start_survival.reason: First-loss survival belongs to KXNBALASTTOLOSE in season_stat_markets; unrelated to playoff scoring. Detached from this archetype by archetype patch.

nba.division_race_tiebreak_state.reason: Same mechanism as nba.tiebreak_ledger inside nba.standings_sim; irrelevant to playoff single-game points; detached from this archetype by archetype patch.

nba.cup_finals_pair_probability.reason: Cup Finals pairing belongs to KXNBAMATCHUP in series_and_cup; Cup games are not playoff games. Detached from this archetype by archetype patch.

nba.garbage.reason: Defined from the point spread (a market price), so it is a benchmark; blowout truncation uses the market-free nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve. Detached from this archetype by archetype patch.

nba.standings_sim.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (stage s1) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

nba.fouls_ft.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (stage s4) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

interactions.mechanism: The contract compounds a small per-game tail over a random number of games; for p near 1% the value is roughly p times expected games, so a contender's star with 18 expected games is worth several times an equal scorer on a first-round team.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realised playoff 45+ and 50+ game incidence by player against per-game tail times games played, bucketed by team depth of run.

interactions.mechanism: Advancement is conditional on the star's health and his games are conditional on advancement, so the joint probability of 'healthy and still playing in round three' exceeds the product of marginals for teams that depend on him and falls below it for deep teams.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate runs with and without coupling team strength to the star's health state and compare games-played distributions with historical star playoff games.

interactions.mechanism: Playoff minutes inflation applies only in competitive games; in a lopsided series the star sits fourth quarters, so the heavy-minutes regime needed for 50 depends on the series strength gap.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress star playoff minutes on game margin and series seed gap over 15 seasons; compare 40+ minute frequency in close versus lopsided series.

interactions.mechanism: When a co-star is out, usage jumps by several points and the 50-point tail thickens sharply; with both creators healthy the tail is thin, so the effect is a regime switch rather than a linear shift.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare 40+ point game rates for stars in games with and without the second-highest-usage teammate over 5 seasons.

interactions.mechanism: An elite primary defender assigned for a whole series lowers the scale of the tail for every game of that series, so the per-game tails are positively correlated within a series and the union is smaller than independent games imply.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare stars' playoff points tails by primary-defender quality bucket and test within-series correlation of residuals.

nonlinearities.shape: power-law (generalised Pareto) decay of exceedance in N
nonlinearities.why: Moving the strike from 45 to 50 cuts per-game probability by a factor of roughly two to four depending on the tail index, so small errors in the shape parameter move the price more than errors in mean points.

nonlinearities.shape: convex effect of usage on P(50+)
nonlinearities.why: A few points of extra usage add little to the mean but shift the far tail strongly because 50 points needs both volume and hot shooting; the response accelerates at high usage.
